title: Americans don’t have to choose between our AI future and ripping off copyright owners
description: The DOJ's embrace of fair use for AI training breaks with the White House's own framework, as OpenAI, Microsoft and news groups battle over copyright.
fullContent:
One of the biggest court battles over artificial intelligence (AI) is putting an age-old legal principle to the test — and raising important questions about the Trump administration's AI policy.

Several news organizations, including The New York Times, are suing OpenAI and Microsoft for using millions of newspaper articles to train AI systems. The newspapers argue that the tech firms violated basic copyright protections. The tech firms contend that training their models on those articles qualifies as "fair use," a longstanding principle that allows copyrighted material to be used in certain ways without permission from or compensation to the copyright owner.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has sided squarely with OpenAI's position — breaking with the administration's previously more balanced stance on the issue. The DOJ filed a statement of interest embracing an extreme vision of fair use that would grant AI companies virtually unfettered access to copyrighted material for commercial training, without obtaining permission from or compensating the creators whose works fuel these systems.

MIKE DAVIS: THE TRUMP DOJ SHOULD WITHDRAW ITS STATEMENT OF INTEREST IN THE OPENAI LAWSUIT

This expansive interpretation threatens to turn a narrow copyright exception into a blanket exemption for the world's most powerful and profitable industries.

The DOJ's reasoning is that requiring a copyright license for material used in AI training would impose high costs on AI developers. It claims those costs could make it harder for small companies to compete and hamper U.S. AI leadership and national security.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

Those concerns deserve consideration. But the DOJ's aggressive arguments in the brief depart from more measured guidance elsewhere in the administration. The White House's official AI framework acknowledges valid arguments on both sides of the copyright debate.

Likewise, the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, adopted by G20 ministers at the Commerce Department's recent Innovation Ministerial, recognize that the intersection of AI and copyright poses "complex legal and policy questions." The principles note the "essential role" of copyright protections in supporting creators and call for respecting IP as a pillar of G20 AI policy.

MUSIC INDUSTRY FENDS OFF FLOOD OF AI MUSIC 'STEALING' THE CHARTS

The DOJ statement also overlooks how its stance could favor larger AI companies over smaller firms and startups. Several AI startups have argued that paying for the material they use provides more reliable access to training material, reduces legal uncertainty and improves models. Other companies have emerged to aggregate copyrights and make licensing easier.

It's particularly problematic for large AI companies to complain about paying for access to copyrighted materials. They are among the best positioned to pay for those materials, and doing so would help develop the kind of licensing markets they claim are lacking.

OBAMA CRITICIZES TRUMP ON APPROACH TO AI, ESCALATES WARNING FOR STRONGER REGULATION

And even if national security were a legitimate justification, the government could not simply disregard property rights. The Constitution and other laws require just compensation when private property is taken for public use, and intellectual property rights are still property rights. Letting AI firms appropriate creators' IP without permission or compensation would be akin to letting data center builders seize private land without paying fair value.

If courts adopt the DOJ's position that fair use protects AI developers in virtually all circumstances, it would reduce incentives to create new works. Copyrights encourage creative work by assuring writers, artists and other creators that their work can't be easily stolen or copied. Licensing those rights allows creators to earn a living and underpins over $1 trillion in U.S. economic activity.

Weaker copyrights could result in fewer human-created books, articles, research papers, films and songs. Ironically, that could eventually leave AI systems with fewer and lower-quality materials to train on – a scenario that serves no one's interests.

All of this is why the Trump administration would be wise to follow its own AI framework and let the court system evaluate AI copyright disputes case by case, rather than arguing for unfettered fair use exceptions.

Policymakers also have a role to play. One promising bill is the bipartisan CLEAR Act. Introduced in February by California Democrat Sen. Adam Schiff and Utah Republican Sen. John Curtis, the CLEAR Act would require AI developers to publicly disclose the copyrighted works used in each new generative-AI model's training dataset.

The proposal would not settle whether any particular training practice qualifies as fair use. But it would give creators more information about whether their work helped train an AI system, enabling them to pursue appropriate compensation or other remedies when they believe their rights have been violated.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That kind of targeted reform offers a useful model for copyright enforcement in the age of AI. Rather than treating licensing as an obstacle to innovation, policymakers should foster a market where AI developers can efficiently license copyrighted material while respecting creators' rights.

AI innovation is vital to America's future. But America's creative industries still depend on strong copyright protections. Policymakers need to promote both.

title: NFT Sales Climb To $33M As Buyers Return Despite The Crypto Crash
description: Bitcoin just hit a two-year low and Ether is trading near $1,650. Yet one corner of crypto is quietly heating up. NFT sales rose 3.88% to $33 million in the seven days through Nov. 21, according to CryptoSlam data. More importantly, the number of people buying jumped sharply. Buyer addresses climbed 60.89% to 109,319, while […]
fullContent:
Bitcoin just hit a two-year low and Ether is trading near $1,650. Yet one corner of crypto is quietly heating up.

NFT sales rose 3.88% to $33 million in the seven days through Nov. 21, according to CryptoSlam data. More importantly, the number of people buying jumped sharply.

Buyer addresses climbed 60.89% to 109,319, while seller addresses rose 68.95% to 85,937. That is a sharp turnaround from the previous week, when both counts had dropped by more than 70%.

And Ethereum is leading the way.

Buyers Are Coming Back To NFTs

The jump in activity stands out against the wider market. Bitcoin slid to around $55,100 on Saturday, while Ether fell to about $1,649 on Friday, according to Reuters.

Despite that, NFT traders stepped up. The total number of transactions slipped 3.63% to 578,892, but the value of each sale grew. The average NFT now sells for about $57, up from roughly $53 in the prior week.

Fewer, larger trades from more buyers point to a market where demand is broadening rather than drying up. It is worth noting that CryptoSlam counts wallet addresses, and one person can trade through several wallets.

NFT sales rose 3.88% to $33M in the past week, while Ethereum ($ETH) trading volume jumped 33%, maintaining its lead in NFT activity. A Bitcoin $BTC collectible recorded the week’s biggest individual sale, signaling renewed market activity.

#NFT #ETH https://t.co/5KulaYOtDP

— Mike Andrew (@Mike_ATrades) November 21, 2026

Ethereum Leads NFT Sales With A 33% Jump

Ethereum was the standout blockchain of the week. NFT sales on the network climbed 33.50% to $12.91 million, about 39% of the entire market.

Buyer activity on Ethereum more than doubled, with CryptoSlam recording 13,108 buyer addresses. Wash trading was minimal at just $51,379, suggesting most of that volume came from real demand.

Polygon held second place with $7.46 million in sales, even as its volume dipped 8.01%. Its buyer addresses rose 62.73% to 33,053. However, CryptoSlam flagged another $17.55 million in Polygon trades as wash volume, so its headline figure deserves a closer look.

Bitcoin came third with $3.87 million, down 20.72%, though its buyer addresses surged 87.16% to 6,489. Base also had a strong week, with sales up 31.12% to $1.93 million, overtaking BNB Chain. Solana finished seventh with $1.15 million, up 2.91%.

nft market this week:

• total sales: $33.63m • courtyard: $7.08m • bored apes: $1.75m • cryptopunks: $841k

courtyard did about 2.7x the volume of apes and punks combined

people aren’t buying monkeys anymore https://t.co/P6Bk8uDqhm

— MANI (@0xmani) November 15, 2026

Blue Chips Are Back In Demand

The collection rankings show that established names are drawing buyers again.

Courtyard, a platform for tokenized physical collectibles on Polygon, kept the top spot with $6.35 million in sales across 125,328 transactions. Bored Ape Yacht Club came second with $1.85 million, up 5.20%.

CryptoPunks cleared $1 million, reaching $1.04 million across 19 trades, up 24.04%. Mutant Ape Yacht Club more than doubled its volume, rising 113.53% to $834,964.

Bitcoin’s BRC-20 collections also stood out, even as overall Bitcoin NFT volume fell. $FTSS jumped 135.46% to $766,799, while $ATMC rose 27.58% to $681,169.

Six-Figure Sales Return

Big-ticket trades are back too. The week’s top sale was a Bitcoin $X@AI BRC-20 entry, which changed hands for 5.9916 BTC, worth about $381,783.

Mutant Ape Yacht Club #1134 came second at $342,251, paid in 189.65 ETH. Two Alchemix V3 Transmuter tokens followed at about $275,566 and $266,169.

Async Art #199 sold for around $210,870, and VeeFriends #9573 fetched $201,750. In total, eight NFTs sold for more than $160,000 during the week.

Ethereum Price Levels To Watch

With Ethereum leading NFT activity, ETH’s price is worth watching. The token is trading near $1,650, its lowest level in months.

The first target for bulls is reclaiming $1,750. Above that, the psychological $2,000 level is the key resistance that would signal a real recovery.

On the downside, $1,600 is the first support to hold, followed by $1,500.

Stronger NFT demand alone won’t turn the market around while tech stocks and the Fed weigh on risk assets. But rising buyer counts during a crash suggest some collectors see these prices as an opportunity. For more updates, follow the latest Ethereum news.

What do you think?

Is the jump in NFT buyers an early sign of recovery, or just bargain hunters stepping in during the crypto sell-off?

title: XRP Price Could Have Its Worst Month in Recent History
description:
XRP has fallen below $0.90 for the first time in nearly two years, trading near $0.89. The token dropped more than 6% in 24 hours. Now, with November losses topping 28%, XRP could close one of its worst months in recent history. XRP Loses a Key Support for the First Time Since 2024 A support
The post XRP Price Could Have Its Worst Month in Recent History appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
XRP has fallen below $0.90 for the first time in nearly two years, trading near $0.89. The token dropped more than 6% in 24 hours.

Now, with November losses topping 28%, XRP could close one of its worst months in recent history.

XRP Loses a Key Support for the First Time Since 2024

A support level is a price zone where buying demand has historically stopped a decline. For XRP, $0.90 had held on a sustained basis since November 2024.

That changed this week. The altcoin broke below the level amid a sharp deterioration across the crypto market. Bitcoin slipped below $56,000 and dragged most altcoins lower.

Just last week, XRP also posted its lowest weekly level for the first time in two years.

Meanwhile, US stocks suffered a heavy selloff, driven by weakness in tech and AI shares. Crypto liquidations also topped $1 billion in recent sessions, which amplified the selling pressure.

For XRP, the damage has been especially severe. The token now sits more than 75% below its record high near $3.65 from July 2025.

In November alone, XRP has lost over 28%. If the trend holds until month’s end, it could become the token’s worst month of the year.

It could also mark its weakest such month on record, surpassing the 23.6% drop seen in 2019.

How Much Lower Could XRP Go?

Bearish signals dominate for now. After losing $0.90, the next support sits near $0.80.

In a more pessimistic scenario, the token could slide toward the $0.64 to $0.70 zone.

Weak flows into spot XRP ETFs reinforce that outlook. According to SoSoValue, these funds have recorded about $30.8 million in net outflows in November.

That puts them on track for their worst month since launching in November 2025.

So far, March holds that record, with roughly $31.2 million in outflows. Meanwhile, total net assets have dropped below $1 billion to about $990 million, down from $1.42 billion in October.

As a result, buyers have struggled to defend key levels.

However, some indicators suggest XRP has entered extreme oversold territory. Bulls would first need to reclaim $0.90, which now acts as resistance.

After that, a recovery above $0.99 to $1.00 could open the path toward $1.10.

In a broader rebound, XRP could even revisit the $1.30 to $1.50 range. Historically, the token has staged strong recoveries after deep monthly losses, provided overall sentiment improves. Still, the altcoin has often struggled to rally while Bitcoin keeps falling.

For now, XRP sits at a critical point. The coming weeks should reveal whether $0.89 marks a temporary floor or the start of a deeper downtrend.

title: Solana Is Building A Quantum Shield Without Giving Up Its Speed, Even As SOL Trades Near $69
description: The SOL price is having a rough month. But behind the chart, Solana’s developers are working on a problem most blockchains haven’t started to tackle yet: how to survive the arrival of powerful quantum computers without losing the speed that made the network famous. SOL trades near $69, caught in the same sell-off that dragged […]
fullContent:
The SOL price is having a rough month. But behind the chart, Solana’s developers are working on a problem most blockchains haven’t started to tackle yet: how to survive the arrival of powerful quantum computers without losing the speed that made the network famous.

SOL trades near $69, caught in the same sell-off that dragged Bitcoin to its lowest level in two years this week. Yet the network’s long-term Solana quantum roadmap is quietly taking shape.

It has three moving parts: new signatures for users, a redesigned consensus system for validators, and a way to safely move existing wallets.

None of it is live yet. But the groundwork is further along than many investors realize.

Why Quantum Computers Are A Long-Term Risk

Today, Solana uses a signature scheme called Ed25519 to prove who owns an account and who can move funds. Like most blockchains, it relies on elliptic-curve math.

A powerful enough quantum computer running Shor’s algorithm could, in theory, break that math. An attacker could work out a private key from public information and forge signatures to move coins they don’t own.

That machine doesn’t exist yet, and no one can say when it will. But upgrading a live network takes years, so preparation needs to start early. The US National Institute of Standards and Technology made that point when it released its first post-quantum standards in 2024.

“We encourage system administrators to start integrating them into their systems immediately, because full integration will take time,” said Dustin Moody, who leads NIST’s post-quantum standardization project.

Falcon: The Compact Signature Solana Picked

Solana’s answer for user accounts is Falcon. Two of the network’s main client teams, Anza and Jump Crypto’s Firedancer, studied the problem separately and reached the same conclusion: Solana needs a post-quantum signature scheme with compact signatures built for high-throughput blockchains.

Both teams have already built initial Falcon implementations. The Solana Foundation said in April that “network performance is not expected to see a meaningful impact” once a migration is activated.

Size is the reason Falcon won. A current Ed25519 signature takes up just 64 bytes. Falcon-512 needs 666 bytes, while the alternative ML-DSA standard needs 2,420 bytes, according to Jump Crypto’s migration analysis. On a network processing thousands of transactions per second, every extra byte adds bandwidth costs.

Falcon is still roughly ten times larger than today’s signatures, but it is the smallest option among the post-quantum signature schemes NIST has selected. Jump also noted that verifying Falcon signatures is relatively simple, while the more complex signing work happens off-chain in wallets.

What would Solana’s consensus look like in a post-quantum world?

Meet Quantumglow: a proposed adaptation of Alpenglow that aims to protect consensus while preserving fast finality.

@jacobvcreech and @qkniep explain how it works. Full video below https://t.co/G005a4KcSI

— Solana Developers (@solana_devs) October 22, 2026

 

Quantumglow Aims To Keep Finality Under A Second

User signatures are only half the problem. Validators also use cryptography to vote on blocks and agree on the state of the ledger.

In October, Solana switched on Alpenglow, a new consensus system targeting finality of around 150 milliseconds, down from roughly 12.8 seconds before. Alpenglow relies on compact signatures that bundle many validator votes together, and no equally efficient post-quantum version exists.

That is where Quantumglow comes in. Anza researchers Quentin Kniep, Kobi Sliwinski and Roger Wattenhofer introduced the design in July, saying it “features a similar state-of-the-art performance as Alpenglow, despite a radical shift in cryptographic primitives.”

Instead of squeezing a large post-quantum signature into every message, Quantumglow removes signatures wherever possible. It uses a custom hash-based scheme called Ax and only sends a large signature alongside small amounts of data.

It is important to separate the two. Alpenglow is live. Quantumglow is still research with no deployment date.

A Safe Exit For Existing Wallets

The final piece is protecting coins that already sit in today’s wallets. A user needs a way to prove ownership that a quantum attacker couldn’t copy.

Anza has built a prototype that does exactly that. It lets a holder prove they know the seed material behind an existing account and link it to a new post-quantum key. Because breaking a signature doesn’t reveal the original seed, an attacker wouldn’t be able to fake the migration.

The prototype proof is still large, at roughly 400 kilobytes, so more engineering is needed. But migration is a one-time step, not something users would pay for on every transfer.

The Solana Foundation’s roadmap lays out the order clearly: keep researching Falcon and its alternatives, adopt a post-quantum scheme for new wallets if quantum becomes a credible threat, and then migrate existing wallets.

Why It Matters For SOL Holders

Quantum risk is often cited as one of crypto’s biggest long-term threats. A network that can show a tested path to post-quantum security, without sacrificing performance, has a strong argument for institutions planning to hold assets for decades.

Solana ain’t waiting around for Q-Day.

Right after shipping Alpenglow (~150ms finality), Solana devs dropped Quantumglow: a research design swapping in hash-based signatures for validators, keeping the chain quantum-resistant without killing that speed.

Future quantum computers could crack standard crypto and fake validator votes. The catch? Quantum-proof signatures are usually heavy and murder network throughput.

Quantumglow works around that bloat. It’s still in research and only covers validators for now (wallets come later), but hardening the consensus layer before the threat arrives is the move.

— Lark Davis (@LarkDavis) October 25, 2026

That kind of fundamental progress has kept building even as the price falls. Earlier this year, network activity kept growing even as SOL slid below $80, and institutional appetite was strong enough to push Solana ETF inflows above $1.16 billion.

Solana Price Levels To Watch

SOL’s 24-hour range has stretched from about $65 to $71.60. The first target for bulls is reclaiming that $71.60 high, followed by the $75 level the token lost last week.

Above that, the $80 zone is the key resistance that would signal a real trend change.

On the downside, $65 is the first support to watch. A break below it would put the psychological $60 mark in play.

For now, macro pressure from falling tech stocks and a likely Fed rate hike is driving the price. But Solana quantum readiness is the kind of long-term work that tends to matter once the market looks past the panic. For more updates, follow the latest altcoin news.

What do you think?

Will Solana’s quantum readiness become a major selling point for institutions, or is quantum risk still too far away to move the SOL price?

Why Quantum Computers Are A Long-Term Risk

Today, Solana uses a signature scheme called Ed25519 to prove who owns an account and who can move funds. Like most blockchains, it relies on elliptic-curve math.

A powerful enough quantum computer running Shor’s algorithm could, in theory, break that math. An attacker could work out a private key from public information and forge signatures to move coins they don’t own.

That machine doesn’t exist yet, and no one can say when it will. But upgrading a live network takes years, so preparation needs to start early. The US National Institute of Standards and Technology made that point when it released its first post-quantum standards in 2024.

“We encourage system administrators to start integrating them into their systems immediately, because full integration will take time,” said Dustin Moody, who leads NIST’s post-quantum standardization project.

Falcon: The Compact Signature Solana Picked

Solana’s answer for user accounts is Falcon. Two of the network’s main client teams, Anza and Jump Crypto’s Firedancer, studied the problem separately and reached the same conclusion: Solana needs a post-quantum signature scheme with compact signatures built for high-throughput blockchains.

Both teams have already built initial Falcon implementations. The Solana Foundation said in April that “network performance is not expected to see a meaningful impact” once a migration is activated.

Size is the reason Falcon won. A current Ed25519 signature takes up just 64 bytes. Falcon-512 needs 666 bytes, while the alternative ML-DSA standard needs 2,420 bytes, according to Jump Crypto’s migration analysis. On a network processing thousands of transactions per second, every extra byte adds bandwidth costs.

Falcon is still roughly ten times larger than today’s signatures, but it is the smallest option among the post-quantum signature schemes NIST has selected. Jump also noted that verifying Falcon signatures is relatively simple, while the more complex signing work happens off-chain in wallets.

What would Solana’s consensus look like in a post-quantum world?

Meet Quantumglow: a proposed adaptation of Alpenglow that aims to protect consensus while preserving fast finality.

@jacobvcreech and @qkniep explain how it works. Full video below https://t.co/G005a4KcSI

— Solana Developers (@solana_devs) October 22, 2026

 

Quantumglow Aims To Keep Finality Under A Second

User signatures are only half the problem. Validators also use cryptography to vote on blocks and agree on the state of the ledger.

In October, Solana switched on Alpenglow, a new consensus system targeting finality of around 150 milliseconds, down from roughly 12.8 seconds before. Alpenglow relies on compact signatures that bundle many validator votes together, and no equally efficient post-quantum version exists.

That is where Quantumglow comes in. Anza researchers Quentin Kniep, Kobi Sliwinski and Roger Wattenhofer introduced the design in July, saying it “features a similar state-of-the-art performance as Alpenglow, despite a radical shift in cryptographic primitives.”

Instead of squeezing a large post-quantum signature into every message, Quantumglow removes signatures wherever possible. It uses a custom hash-based scheme called Ax and only sends a large signature alongside small amounts of data.

It is important to separate the two. Alpenglow is live. Quantumglow is still research with no deployment date.

A Safe Exit For Existing Wallets

The final piece is protecting coins that already sit in today’s wallets. A user needs a way to prove ownership that a quantum attacker couldn’t copy.

Anza has built a prototype that does exactly that. It lets a holder prove they know the seed material behind an existing account and link it to a new post-quantum key. Because breaking a signature doesn’t reveal the original seed, an attacker wouldn’t be able to fake the migration.

The prototype proof is still large, at roughly 400 kilobytes, so more engineering is needed. But migration is a one-time step, not something users would pay for on every transfer.

The Solana Foundation’s roadmap lays out the order clearly: keep researching Falcon and its alternatives, adopt a post-quantum scheme for new wallets if quantum becomes a credible threat, and then migrate existing wallets.

Why It Matters For SOL Holders

Quantum risk is often cited as one of crypto’s biggest long-term threats. A network that can show a tested path to post-quantum security, without sacrificing performance, has a strong argument for institutions planning to hold assets for decades.

Solana ain’t waiting around for Q-Day.

Right after shipping Alpenglow (~150ms finality), Solana devs dropped Quantumglow: a research design swapping in hash-based signatures for validators, keeping the chain quantum-resistant without killing that speed.

Future quantum computers could crack standard crypto and fake validator votes. The catch? Quantum-proof signatures are usually heavy and murder network throughput.

Quantumglow works around that bloat. It’s still in research and only covers validators for now (wallets come later), but hardening the consensus layer before the threat arrives is the move.

— Lark Davis (@LarkDavis) October 25, 2026

That kind of fundamental progress has kept building even as the price falls. Earlier this year, network activity kept growing even as SOL slid below $80, and institutional appetite was strong enough to push Solana ETF inflows above $1.16 billion.

Solana Price Levels To Watch

SOL’s 24-hour range has stretched from about $65 to $71.60. The first target for bulls is reclaiming that $71.60 high, followed by the $75 level the token lost last week.

Above that, the $80 zone is the key resistance that would signal a real trend change.

On the downside, $65 is the first support to watch. A break below it would put the psychological $60 mark in play.

For now, macro pressure from falling tech stocks and a likely Fed rate hike is driving the price. But Solana quantum readiness is the kind of long-term work that tends to matter once the market looks past the panic. For more updates, follow the latest altcoin news.

What do you think?

Will Solana’s quantum readiness become a major selling point for institutions, or is quantum risk still too far away to move the SOL price?

title: Bitcoin Core Patches Stall Bug Found by an AI Scan
description:
Key Takeaways An automated LLM scan found the flaw first. A single message could stall nodes 12+ seconds. Fixed in […]
The post Bitcoin Core Patches Stall Bug Found by an AI Scan appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

  • An automated LLM scan found the flaw first.
  • A single message could stall nodes 12+ seconds.
  • Fixed in 30.5, 31.3 and 32.1.
  • Unsupported 29.x gets no patch at all.

Bitcoin Core developers published the security advisory for CVE-2026-117348 on November 20, rating the bug medium severity and classing it as “easily discoverable”, a label that decides how quickly the public hears about a flaw.

How an AI Scan and a Second Researcher Found It

The first report arrived on July 8 from Project Loupe, Elias Rohrer’s research effort at Spiral. The flaw surfaced in an automated LLM scan, and Bitcoin Core contributor Gregory Sanders validated the finding before taking it to the project’s security team. On August 4, a researcher known as Stutxo reported the same issue independently.

Two unrelated parties finding one bug within four weeks is the risk the “easily discoverable” category is meant to address. Under Bitcoin Core’s disclosure policy, such bugs get a public advisory alongside the fixed releases, without the usual severity-based waiting period. By comparison, a high-severity mining-template bug disclosed earlier this month stayed under embargo for 396 days after its fix. Coindoo has covered why the project moved to the faster track.

What the Bug Did Inside a Node

An orphan transaction spends an output from an earlier transaction the node has not received yet. That alone doesn’t make it invalid. The node keeps it in a holding area, the orphanage, until the missing parents turn up.

Starting with version 29.0, when a peer announced an orphan by its wtxid, the node listed that orphan’s parents and checked each one against its mempool and its filters of recently seen transactions. Peers announce transactions in inv messages, which can carry up to 50,000 entries, and the software did not skip duplicates.

That gave an attacker an easy way to waste a node’s time. According to the advisory, the attacker could send an orphan with thousands of missing parents, then send inv messages repeating its wtxid 50,000 times. Every repeat would trigger the full parent check again. Each such message could stall the node for more than a dozen seconds, and in that window it would process nothing from other peers, blocks included. The advisory describes the stall as temporary and does not mention any exploitation.

Nothing in the advisory suggests the flaw let invalid transactions through validation or exposed wallet keys. It affected how fast a node could keep up, not what the node accepted.

Sanders opened the fix as pull request #35878 on August 4, and it was merged two days later. A patched node handles each announced transaction once per inv message, however many times the message repeats it. The 31.3 release notes list the change as “process unique tx INVs only.”

Who Got the Fix, and When

How the patch reached users depends on which branch they run:

32.x

Patched from launch

32.1, released October 27, shipped with the fix. 32.0 was tagged but never released.

31.x

Fixed November 20

31.0 to 31.2 are affected. Upgrade to 31.3.

30.x

Fixed November 20

30.0 to 30.4 are affected. Upgrade to 30.5.

29.x

No fix planned

29.0 to 29.5 are affected. The branch reached end of life on October 27.

Anyone on 32.x has run patched code since the branch’s first public release, weeks before the advisory went out. The 30.x and 31.x fixes were backported on November 17 and released alongside the advisory, so users of those branches learned about the flaw and received the patch at the same moment.

Bitcoin Core’s maintenance policy covers the three latest major versions, and branches past end of life generally don’t receive security fixes. The project recommends running the latest maintenance release of the most recent major version an operator can upgrade to.

Which Setups Feel a Stall First

While a node is stalled, it isn’t reading new blocks or transactions from its peers. The rest of the network carries on. Only that node’s view falls behind, and it catches up once processing resumes.

The exposure depends on what relies on that node. A merchant payment server, a wallet backend or a Lightning node that takes chain data from a single Bitcoin Core instance sees whatever delay that instance sees, so a payment can confirm on-chain before the service registers it. Operators who run several nodes or keep a fallback data source are better placed to ride out a stall on one of them.

READ MORE:

Is Bitcoin Dead? Jack Mallers Points to Its History

Checking That a Node Is Patched and Keeping Up

A node that is running is not necessarily patched or in sync. After upgrading through the official release instructions, three checks confirm the fix is live and the node is current:

  1. Confirm the running version. bitcoin-cli getnetworkinfo returns a subversion field such as /Satoshi:31.3.0/. Query the live process, because a node that hasn’t restarted is still running the old binary.
  2. Confirm it has caught up. In bitcoin-cli getblockchaininfo, blocks should match headers once the node is in sync.
  3. Confirm dependent services see the same chain. Compare the node’s tip height against an independent source and against any payment, wallet or Lightning software that reads from it.

Operators still on 29.x won’t find a patched build to download. Closing this hole means moving to 30.5, 31.3 or 32.1.

title: Bitcoin Price Crashes To Two-Year Low Near $55,000, Analysts Say A Bottom Could Be Close
description: The Bitcoin price just hit a level traders haven’t seen in more than two years. But as fear hits extremes and leverage gets wiped out, some analysts believe the worst of the selling may be almost done. BTC fell below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July, then kept sliding overnight. It touched […]
fullContent:
The Bitcoin price just hit a level traders haven’t seen in more than two years. But as fear hits extremes and leverage gets wiped out, some analysts believe the worst of the selling may be almost done.

BTC fell below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July, then kept sliding overnight. It touched $55,106 on Coinbase in the 06:00 UTC hour on Saturday, visiting its lowest level since September 2024. By mid-morning, it had bounced back to around $57,800.

Bitcoin is now down roughly 28% for the quarter and more than 55% below its October 2025 peak above $126,000.

The drop wasn’t driven by anything inside crypto. It came from Wall Street.

AI Stocks Drag The Bitcoin Price Lower

The sell-off was part of a broad rout in risk assets. The Nasdaq Composite lost 5.3% on Friday while Nvidia sank nearly 14%. Even gold fell to its lowest since September 2025, a sign that investors were selling almost everything to raise cash.

Reuters pointed to weeks of concern about the profitability of massive AI infrastructure spending, rising borrowing costs, regulatory risks after the Democrats’ midterm win, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure.

The Fed is adding pressure too. Traders now see a 97.9% chance of a rate hike on Dec. 9. Institutional selling also accelerated. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $582.3 million in net outflows on Thursday, led by a record $541.1 million exit from BlackRock’s IBIT. That is a sharp reversal from September, when Bitcoin ETF annual flows turned positive.

Leverage did the rest, with around $2.4 billion in crypto bets wiped out as prices broke through key support.

The Anthropic IPO Is Done. Will Liquidity Come Back?

For weeks, traders blamed part of the selling on investors raising cash for the Anthropic IPO. That event is now behind the market.

Every gain since the election — wiped out

Bitcoin just crashed below $56,000, its lowest since September 2024. $2.4 BILLION liquidated in 24 hours, $160 BILLION gone from the market in 12 hours

ETH down 10%, BNB down 10%, Fear & Greed in pure extreme fear.

Are you buying this blood or waiting for lower?

— GOJO.eth (@gojoosama) November 21, 2026

Anthropic priced its shares at $83, above its marketed range, and raised $81.3 billion in the largest IPO in history. The stock opened at about $111.50 on Nov. 19, a 34% premium, before slipping below $100 as the broader market turned lower.

That could matter for crypto. According to well-known analyst Michaël van de Poppe, speculative capital rotated toward the IPO, and part of the selling became a self-fulfilling prophecy as traders dumped risk assets on the expectation that others would. But he argues it is only a matter of time until investors realize the IPO’s upside is limited compared to undervalued assets, and liquidity flows back into Bitcoin.

#Crypto is a ton of speculative capital.

Now, as everything is being tokenized, it’s very easy to swap between assets.

That’s why you see all exchanges being able to trade the Anthropic IPO and capital is allocated towards that, especially speculative capital.

If you’re not trading it, you’ll still be selling your current risk-on assets due to the thesis that people will trade it. It’s a self-fulfilling prophecy.

There will be a point that investors start to realize that the upside on the Anthropic IPO won’t be as much compared to the undervaluation of other assets, so it’s just a matter of time until liquidity will flow back into #Bitcoin.

— Michaël van de Poppe (@CryptoMichNL) November 14, 2026

In a separate post, van de Poppe said a local bottom for Bitcoin was “around the corner” as the IPO approached, adding that “buying the dip is vital.”

The SpaceX listing in June offers a precedent. Bitcoin bottomed near $59,000 a week before that IPO and went on to rally strongly once the selling pressure cleared.

Extreme Fear Has Marked Past Bottoms

Sentiment has collapsed. The crypto Fear and Greed Index has sunk deep into extreme fear territory, the same zone it hit during previous capitulation phases.

That kind of panic often appears near turning points. When most traders are already out or positioned for further losses, there are fewer sellers left to push prices lower.

The leverage flush supports that view. Glassnode had flagged the $59,500 to $62,600 range as a zone packed with potential long liquidations. That zone has now been cleared, removing a big source of forced selling.

The Bitcoin price is also trading far below what it costs to produce new coins. JPMorgan estimated Bitcoin’s production cost at around $85,000 in September, a level its analysts have said historically acts as a “soft floor” for price. That puts pressure on high-cost miners in the short term, but such deep discounts have previously coincided with late-stage sell-offs.

Bitcoin Price Levels To Watch

The first target for bulls is reclaiming $60,000. Getting back above that psychological level would signal that Saturday’s flush marked a local low.

Above that, the $62,500 to $63,000 zone is the next resistance, followed by the 200-week moving average near $67,800 to $68,000. Reclaiming that line would put the bear market narrative in serious doubt.

On the downside, Saturday’s low near $55,100 is the key level to hold. A break below it could open the door to the psychological $50,000 mark.

The macro picture remains the biggest risk. As long as AI stocks keep falling and the Fed looks set to hike, Bitcoin may struggle to break away from Wall Street. For more updates, follow the latest Bitcoin news.

What do you think?

Is Bitcoin’s drop to $55,000 the capitulation bottom, or is a test of $50,000 still coming?

title: Ethereum Price Prediction: 2 Key Levels Matter More Than a $12.9M NFT Week
description: Ethereum led weekly NFT sales at $12.9M as buyers doubled, but ETH trades far below its key averages. Here is why support near $1,540 decides the next move.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Ethereum led all blockchains in weekly NFT sales as its buyer count more than doubled.
  • ETH sits deep below both key moving averages, and momentum still favors sellers.
  • The closest floor now decides whether a relief bounce or a deeper slide comes next.

New buyers flocked to Ethereum's NFT market last week, and very little of the volume looked like wash trading.

The coin itself tells a darker story. ETH has bled value for a month and trades in deeply oversold territory. Traders now want to know whether buyers can hold the nearest floor long enough for a bounce.

Ethereum Buyers Double as NFT Sales Climb to $12.9M

Ethereum led every blockchain in NFT sales over the seven days through Nov. 21, 2026, according to CryptoSlam data. Sales on the network rose about 33% to $12.91 million. That gave Ethereum roughly 39% of the whole market.

Buyer activity drove the gain. Ethereum counted 13,108 buyer addresses, more than double the prior week. Only $51,379 of its volume was flagged as wash trading, which suggests the demand was mostly genuine.

Polygon looked different. It ranked second with $7.46 million in sales, down about 8%. CryptoSlam also flagged $17.55 million of its activity as wash trades.

Across all chains, NFT sales grew about 4% to $33 million. Transactions slipped slightly to 578,892. Fresh buyers, rather than more frequent trading, lifted the total.

High-end collectors also showed up. Mutant Ape #1134 sold for $342,251, or 189.65 ETH.

ETH Trades Far Below Both Averages After a 33% Monthly Slide

Ethereum (ETH) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

ETH traded near $1,660 at last check. That leaves the coin far beneath both of the moving averages traders watch most closely. A moving average smooths out daily swings by tracking the average closing price over a set number of days.

The 50-day average sits around $2,160. The 200-day average is higher still, near $2,260. Price below both lines means the short-term and long-term trends point the same way, which is down. Each average now acts as a ceiling that buyers would have to break through.

ETH gained about 2% over the past day. Over the past week, it lost roughly 14%, and over the past month it gave up about a third of its value.

That daily uptick looks small next to the damage. One green session after weeks of selling often reflects short sellers locking in profits. It rarely signals that fresh demand has arrived.

Sellers have controlled almost every bounce since late October.

The NFT rebound has not changed that picture. More wallets bought digital collectibles on Ethereum, but that buying happens in small amounts and often uses ETH already held. It has not pulled new money into the coin itself.

Oversold Readings Hint at Relief but Sellers Still Steer

Momentum gauges tell a split story. The daily RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 23. Readings below 30 count as oversold, so sellers have pushed the price further and faster than usual.

Stretched readings like this often come before a relief bounce. Traders who sold late tend to buy back, and bargain hunters step in. That can lift the price for a few sessions even inside a downtrend.

Other signals argue against reading too much into it. The MACD, which compares short and longer-term price momentum, remains below its signal line. In plain terms, momentum is still pointing down.

Trend-strength readings show a firm downtrend led by sellers. A strong, seller-driven trend can keep a coin oversold for weeks. Any rebound from here may fade quickly unless buying volume picks up and holds.

Why $1,540 Is the Floor That Matters Most

Support sits near $1,540, a short distance below the current price. That level marks the first real test for buyers if the selling resumes.

The next support is much lower, around $1,200. Losing the first floor could open a deep slide, with little in between to slow it. That gap is why this one level carries so much weight right now.

Overhead, the first resistance stands near $2,170. It lines up almost exactly with the 50-day average, so the two form a single, stronger ceiling. Reclaiming that zone would be the first sign that the downtrend is losing its grip.

Above it, the next barrier waits near $2,300. That level sits just past the 200-day average. Buyers would need to clear both before the longer-term trend could turn up.

Bounce Toward the 50-Day or Slide to $1,200

Two paths stand out from here.

  • Bullish: If buyers defend support, the oversold RSI could fuel a relief rally toward the 50-day line. A daily close below that floor would cancel this view.
  • Bearish: A break of support would point the price toward the much lower second floor. A quick recovery back above the broken level would invalidate the move and trap late sellers.

NFT Cheer Cannot Override a Broken Trend

Ethereum's busier NFT week shows real users returning to the network. It does little for the coin's price. The two levels on the daily chart will set ETH's direction from here.

A short relief bounce remains possible, but the broader trend still points down. Oversold coins can stay oversold for weeks. If the nearest floor gives way, selling could speed up quickly.

title: More trouble for Nvidia as SEC reportedly probes accounting amid historic stock slide
description:
Nvidia's worst week on record just got worse. Now the government is asking questions about its books.
Nvidia (NVDA) stock fell 14% Friday, its worst day since the DeepSeek rout in January 2025 and its seventh straight loss, before bouncing nearly 4% in after-hours trading. The drop came as Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission's probe of the chipmaker is examining potential accounting issues.
The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that the probe includes an examination of whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors. Nvidia didn't respond to Bloomberg's request for comment on that report, and the SEC declined to comment.
The selling set records. Nvidia shed about $490 billion in market value Friday and nearly $900 billion this week, as its stock had its worst week since October 2008. That tops the $573 billion it lost last week, previously the biggest one-week drop for any company on record, according to Dow Jones Market Data.
Since its Oct. 6 record, Nvidia has lost about $2.7 trillion in market value, more than the $2.5 trillion that The Kobeissi Letter called the biggest 45-day loss for any stock in history. The world's most valuable company six weeks ago now ranks fourth in the US, behind Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet (GOOGL).

Nvidia's latest quarterly report raised a few questions. The company said its 10-Q, the detailed quarterly filing, would come "in the coming weeks" instead of the same evening as usual, and the release mentioned an ongoing investigation by an independent board committee.
Nvidia booked about $104 billion of revenue through its Singapore unit in 2025, roughly half its sales, the Financial Times reported. The Journal said the disclosure questions include Singapore-based Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer US officials suspect of rerouting its chips to China. 
Nvidia's customers are also taking longer to pay, with bills outstanding at 64 days of sales, the most since 2022. It's not clear which of these, if any, the SEC is focused on.
Washington wants answers fast. "I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday, after Jensen Huang's exit as CEO. President Trump said Friday he "would love to see Jensen be given a second chance," while criticizing the chipmaker's new leadership.
California is digging in too. Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenaed Nvidia Thursday, investigating whether its advanced chips reached China and whether the company misled investors. "Companies cannot mislead their investors," Bonta said.
The sell-off spread across chip stocks, which had their worst week since 2001, and the broader market.
Baird's Ted Mortonson, a technology desk sector strategist, saw more scrutiny coming even before Friday's report.
"Every single deal that Nvidia has done on circular finance is going to be put under the microscope," he said on Yahoo Finance's live show Thursday.

title: Republicans face 'brutal' 2028 Senate map after Dems 2026 blue wave
description: Incoming NRSC chair Sen. Bernie Moreno calls the GOP's 2028 Senate map "absolutely brutal" as Republicans must flip six seats to reclaim majority control.
fullContent:
Incoming Senate Republican campaign chairman says the party faces a "very tough" road ahead as the GOP aims to take back their majority in 2028 after taking significant losses in the midterms earlier this month.

Democrats convincingly grabbed control of the Senate and will hold a large 56-44 majority when the new Congress is sworn in at the start of the new year, they also won control of the House and multiple governors' seats flip from red to blue, as well.

In the Senate, the new split means Republicans will need to flip at least six seats in the 2028 elections to win back the majority. That number rises to seven seats if they lose the White House in the next election cycle.

One senator told Fox News Digital that Republicans can "forget 2028."

"It is an absolutely brutal map," Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno, the incoming National Republican Senatorial Committee chair, recently told Fox News Digital, as he pointed to the states up for grabs in 2028.

SENATE REPUBLICANS FEAR 'BRUTAL' 2028 MAP COULD KEEP DEMOCRATS IN POWER FOR YEARS

But the first term senator from Ohio added that in "politics, things change pretty quickly."

He's not kidding.

At the start of the 2026 cycle, the Democrats faced a steep and narrow path to winning back the majority, but by Election Day the party was able to ride a massive blue wave formed by an extremely favorable political climate to flip nine Senate seats .

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, looking ahead to the next election, said in an interview on Fox News' "America Reports, "We can come back — we will."

"I've been there before, and we just have to get out and win the hearts and minds of the American people," he added. "And that means coming up with a compelling economic message, talking about secure streets, secure border, safe streets, and in more money in your pocket. I mean, I think those are the things that the American people care the most about."

Looking ahead to the next two years, when he will be leading the GOP minority in the Senate, Thune said "we now have an opportunity in the minority to draw those bold lines, those contrasts, and make sure that we are delivering a message that connects with the middle of the electorate."

In 2028, Republicans will need to hold onto seats in battlegrounds Wisconsin and North Carolina, where GOP Sens. Ron Johnson and Ted Budd are up for re-election.

Meanwhile, Republicans will work to flip seats held by Democratic Sens. Mark Kelly of Arizona, John Fetterman of Pennsylvania, Raphael Warnock of Georgia, Catherine Cortez Masto of Nevada, and Maggie Hassan of New Hampshire.

Dem flips key Senate seat in battleground North Carolina as Cooper defeats Trump ally

TRUMP GRIP ON GOP FACES MAJOR POST-ELECTION TEST

Fetterman, who has repeatedly visibly broken with his party and seen his poll numbers among Democrats crater, faces all-but-certain primary challenges if he seeks re-election. Meanwhile, Kelly and Warnock are mulling White House runs in 2028.

Senate showdowns will also be held in 2028 in six states that President Donald Trump carried by double-digits two years ago that become key battlegrounds in this year's midterms.

Among them are Ohio, where former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown won a ticket back to the Senate with a five point victory over appointed GOP Sen. Jon Husted. Brown will fill out the final two years of Vice President JD Vance's old Senate term, so he'll face re-election in 2028.

Republicans will be defending seats in four states where Democrats scored Senate flips in this year's midterms. The four seats are held by GOP Sens. Chuck Grassley of Iowa, Jerry Moran of Kansas, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, and Tim Scott of South Carolina,

Massive upset: Andrews downs Trump-backed Graham in ruby-red South Carolina

In Florida, appointed Republican Sen. Ashley Moody narrowly defeated progressive Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon in a special election. Moody, who is filling out Secretary of State Marco Rubio's old Senate term, will face re-election in two years.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Kyle Kondik, managing editor of Sabato’s Crystal Ball at the University of Virginia Center for Politics, which is a leading nonpartisan political handicapper, told Fox News Digital Republicans could win the Senate back by flipping six states in 2028 : Arizona, Georgia, Ohio, Nevada, New Hampshire, and Pennsylvania.

Dems seize the Senate as blue tidal wave crashes deep into Trump country, topples GOP strongholds

"Those are five states Trump won state in 2024," as well as New Hampshire, which then-Vice President Kamala Harris carried by single digits.

"The Democrats just showed that they could win all these double-digit Trump states" in the midterms," Kondik noted. "The Republicans don't have to flip any double-digit Harris states to win the Senate back" in 2028.

Kondik also highlighted that there there will be a Senate special election next November, a year ahead of the 2028 showdowns.

That ballot box contest will be held in Minnesota, where Democratic Sen. Amy Klobuchar is about to step down after winning the state's gubernatorial election. Klobuchar will pick a replacement senator when she steps down, and the state will hold a special contest on Election Day 2027 to choose a successor to fill out the final three years of Klobuchar's current term.

title: Not Just Bitcoin: Even Gold and Silver Can’t Escape the Market Rout
description: Central banks keep buying gold, but that hasn't halped its price at all lately.
fullContent:
Remember the end of 2025 and the start of 2026? Silver was everywhere. Gold too, but its smaller sibling managed to steal the spotlight with an amazing run after years and years of remaining on the sidelines.

Just a quick recap: silver traded at under $30 against the dollar in April 2025. By late January 2026, its price had skyrocketed by over 4x to an all-time high of $122. Gold’s performance was quite impressive as well, going from under $3,000/oz in April 2025 to a peak of its own at $5,600 in late January. Although the following several months have been nothing short of an economic and macro calamity, both so-called safe-haven assets have failed to maintain their rally. Or even retain their gains.

$15T and Counting

The Kobeissi Letter highlighted at the end of the business week the scale of the damage, noting that gold fell below $3,550 per ounce, while silver plummeted beneath $42. The market commentators claimed that the two metals have now erased roughly $15 trillion (yes, with a T) in combined market value since their respective record highs earlier in 2026.

Gold’s reversal has been particularly dramatic and surprising to an extent. After its $5,600 ATH on January 29, the precious metal slumped by roughly 37% in months to $3,500 on Friday. Reuters reported that the bullion also closed with an 8% weekly decline, which made it its worst performance in eight months.

Silver’s pain has been quite apparent as well, with a 65% drop within the same timeframe. Expectedly, BTC has been caught in the same liquidation wave, dumping from $81,000 earlier this month to $55,000 on Saturday, showing that both the newer and traditional “hard money” trades have struggled as investors scramble for liquidity.

But Central Banks Keep Buying

What makes gold’s collapse especially striking is that central banks have hardly stopped buying. In fact, recent data suggests that many have ramped up their efforts. We recently reported that central banks accumulated 321 tonnes in Q3, 42% more than a year earlier, the strongest quarterly total since Q4 2024. Year-to-date purchases reached 675 tonnes, 6% above the same period in 2025. China and Poland were among the largest gold players.

The World Gold Council continues to expect these institutions to remain significant buyers, citing diversification and risk management as the key motivations. Yet, that demand has not been enough to stop prices from falling.

The reason could stem from the fact that central-bank accumulation is only one component of the market. Gold is currently being overwhelmed by a stronger US dollar, rising Treasury yields, and expectations for additional Fed rate hikes. Markets now assign roughly a 90% probability to a December increase, making non-yielding assets such as gold less attractive relative to cash and government bonds.

There’s also evidence of forced selling, with Reuters citing market participants who said investors liquidated gold positions to cover losses elsewhere as the AI-driven equity rout intensified.

title: Oil Prices Dropped 21%, Yet Global Markets Aren't Celebrating. Why?
description:
Brent crude slid 22% to a 2.5-month low as Iran peace hopes erased the war premium. Key support sits at $89.
The post Oil Prices Dropped 21%, Yet Global Markets Aren't Celebrating. Why? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Oil prices have fallen at a pace rarely seen outside a global financial crisis. Yet stock markets are struggling, inflation remains stubborn, and the economic relief investors expected has barely materialized.

Brent crude has plunged roughly 21% since late October, falling from $117.45 to $92.57 on Friday. It briefly approached $89 earlier this month, erasing much of its recent rally.

According to Steno Research, the US “all-in barrel,” which includes estimated insurance costs, lost $36.9 in just 14 days. That exceeds the $35.2 decline recorded during the 2008 financial crisis.

“The oil price has NEVER dropped this fast unless the economy was in a complete crash,” founder Andreas Steno Larsen wrote.

Why Are Oil Prices Crashing?

The decline largely reflects improving supply conditions.

Traders previously feared the US-Israeli war with Iran would severely disrupt Gulf oil exports. However, diplomatic hopes have grown, while shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered to roughly pre-war levels.

Washington has also released emergency crude to ease shortages.

The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve has consequently fallen to 276.4 million barrels, its lowest level since 1982.

Why Isn’t the Oil Crash Helping Global Markets?

Cheaper crude should ease inflation, as market commentator Ted Pillows highlighted. But the benefits have been uneven.

US gasoline prices have fallen below $4 per gallon. Diesel, essential for transporting goods, remains comparatively expensive because of refinery disruptions and tight fuel supplies.

That means businesses are still facing high shipping costs, while consumers have yet to see substantial relief.

Meanwhile, US inflation has spread beyond energy. The Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates in December, keeping borrowing costs elevated.

Stocks, particularly AI-related companies, are also struggling with concerns over valuations and economic growth.

For now, cheaper oil is providing some relief. But persistent inflation and the prospect of higher interest rates continue to weigh on global markets. The oil crash alone has not been enough to reverse those pressures.

title: Swift assurances from officials after wave of nationwide outages raises questions, expert says
description: SMET CEO Danny Cooper says ruling out a cyberattack too fast risks missing hackers after the JPMorgan Chase, Microsoft outages and air travel ground stop.
fullContent:
Amid a slew of high-profile disruptions that struck major pillars of American life over the past week, including a nationwide ground stop that halted air travel, banking outages at JPMorgan Chase and other lenders, and a service disruption at Microsoft, officials were quick to reassure the public that nothing nefarious was behind the failures.

During the ground stop, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the homeland and the banking system remained secure, insisting that the disruptions showed no signs of a cyberattack or malicious activity.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton similarly stated that officials saw no evidence of a coordinated or state-sponsored attack, pointing instead to routine patching and system upgrades.

DHS CHIEF TELLS AMERICANS TO 'BREATHE' AMID TECH OUTAGES, INSISTS HOMELAND IS 'SECURE'

"Based on what we know today … these are separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes," Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee on Wednesday. "They are not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack."

Major companies, including Microsoft and JPMorgan Chase, also attributed the disruptions to internal technical issues or software bugs rather than malicious intrusions.

US INFRASTRUCTURE CRUMBLES AS ADVERSARIES POWER UP – LEAVING AMERICANS DANGEROUSLY EXPOSED: CYBER EXPERT

To Danny Cooper, CEO of critical infrastructure security firm SMET, the speed with which those assurances were issued poses a problem.

"A blanket statement like 'there's no malicious activity associated with any of the outages' is almost impossible from a probability perspective," Cooper told Fox News Digital.

THE OUTAGES AMERICA HAS SUFFERED WEREN'T AN ATTACK, BUT THE NEXT FAILURE COULD BE

Public anxiety tends to spike around a single question in the aftermath of a major disruption: Was it a coincidence or an attack? Public skepticism is understandable given how many critical systems stumbled within a five-to-six-day window, Cooper said.

"How plausible is it that all these pillars or whatever all suffered major independent technical failures within a five- or six-day window?" Cooper asked. "I think highly improbable. And I understand why the American public is calling this into question and deeply empathize with that. The pattern recognition is there."

DUFFY: INVESTIGATORS EXAMINING 2 ROUTERS AFTER NATIONWIDE FAA GROUND STOP, NO SIGNS OF FOREIGN CYBERATTACK

Even when officials point to routine maintenance or aging hardware, Cooper argued that ruling out foul play too quickly skips investigative steps that take time to execute properly, which could potentially undermine efforts to fix vulnerabilities and prevent future incidents.

"If a company or the government is making a statement that is as bold as 'we are certain there is no malicious activity here' without having the time to actually do an appropriate investigation, in the case of this sort of cyber domain, some cyber forensics and a full audit of what transpired, that's not quite how it works," she said.

PERPETUAL PARALYSIS: WHY EVERYTHING IS GRINDING TO A HALT

"On the physical side, being able to fully interrogate what has happened in the environment, who was there, and so on about what is happening in the periphery and what led up to that moment in time, those things take time."

An instant "nothing to see here" message can also deepen public suspicion, Cooper said, particularly when multiple institutions and agencies echo that conclusion before audits can be completed.

JOIN THE CHAT: RECENT TECH OUTAGES LOOM OVER MULLIN TESTIMONY ON WORLDWIDE THREATS

The Democratic National Committee (DNC) also sounded the alarm over conflicting statements coming from the Trump administration.

"The administration has repeatedly offered conflicting statements about the causes of the outages," DNC Deputy Communications Director Kendall Witmer said in a statement. "Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin suggested that SI – Trump’s preferred name for Artificial Intelligence (AI) – is responsible for the multiple outages that have occurred in recent days, according to a "very smart" tech guy he talked to. Then, yesterday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio contradicted Mullin and would not attribute the outages to AI."

MICROSOFT’S MASSIVE OUTAGE OFFERS A LESSON IN HOW TO BRING THE WORLD BACK ONLINE

Much of the official explanation surrounding the November disruptions centered on software updates and system upgrades. Organizations frequently schedule maintenance and can experience downtime when rolling out changes at scale, especially if teams move too quickly, Cooper noted.

However, those windows are what sophisticated adversaries watch closely, she warned.

"If companies are disproportionately moving to execute these sorts of upgrades en masse, then yes, it's possible that you would have a higher number of downtime or outages," she said.

"But it's also quite possible that, particularly given the sophistication of cyber adversaries, whether it's hackers, whether it's non-state entities, whether it's nation-state entities, it's also possible that they are using those software updates or upgrades or patches and in those moments actually injecting malware and exploits and so on."

title: DEPROGRAMMED: He lived as a woman for six years, hit ‘rock bottom’ and found Jesus. Then he detransitioned.
description: After six years living as a woman, Diego Arellan says pain, rejection and suicidal thoughts led him to become a Christian through his sister's testimony.
fullContent:
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 800-273-TALK (8255).

Diego Arellan said he had never encountered transgender ideology until he moved to the United States from Peru as a teenager. He said people later encouraged him to transition because of the way he behaved. Ultimately, he lived as a transgender woman for six years before becoming a Christian and detransitioning.

"I started hanging out with a lot of people that were living that lifestyle and that also recommended me to live that lifestyle because [of] the way I acted," Arellan told Fox News Digital.

"I found that out of like this clinic who offer that pretty much transitioning to become your opposite gender. And so, through that process … in my mind it was like, 'I definitely have to do this because this is the right path. Everything that I'm seeing out there, like in social media, or anywhere I go I see, like this is a way you have to go in order for you to feel fulfilled, at least because I always struggle with my identity,'" he continued.

PRISHA MOSLEY: AS A DETRANSITIONER AND MOM, I KNOW WHAT GENDER IDEOLOGY STOLE FROM ME

"I transitioned when I was 18 and a lot of things happened during that season just because I was very immature in that season … I went through a lot [of] gender dysphoria," Arellan said.

He went on to describe what he said were side effects of the hormone pills he took, saying his body was reacting to something that was "not natural."

"[I had] a lot of like, pain on my body and just changes, but I still went through it because I really thought that this was gonna be the path that was gonna make me happy … There was a lot of rejection as well from the people I start[ed] dating … I was lying not only to me, but I was lying to the people out there who thought they were dating any other woman, but in reality, [I] was not," he continued.

WOMAN WHO LIVED AS MAN SAYS SHE GRIEVED ‘UNWANTED BODY PARTS’ AFTER TRANSITION

"There was a lot of confusion, a lot of stress, a lot like just also wanting to kill myself at one point because of all these things I was building and thinking that this was the right path again," Arellan added.

Arellan said he had breast augmentation surgery, a Brazilian butt lift and Botox injections in different areas of his face.

"It was turning into an addiction because it was never enough. Everything I see on my face … I started to hate it because I just kept looking at myself and I look[ed] at the mirror and I look[ed like] I'm a man just having long hair," he said.

"I achieved everything I wanted [and] I still felt so empty and that's where a lot of things changed," Arellan said.

WOMAN WHO UNDERWENT DOUBLE MASTECTOMY AT 14 TELLS SURGEON, 'YOU STOLE MY GIRLHOOD'

According to a research paper by Eric Kaufmann, published on the Social Science Research Network (SSRN), the share of surveyed university students identifying as transgender fell from nearly 7% in 2023 to under 4% in later survey data. The paper also reported a decline of approximately 10 percentage points in the share identifying as non-heterosexual.

Arellan discussed his move to Miami, where he dated "a sugar daddy" and experienced "crazy" things that opened his heart to his sister’s testimony of her experience with Jesus Christ.

"I was [at] rock bottom, I hated myself. I had a lot of money. I did a lot [of] things that were really bad. But my sister — she shared with me her testimony of how she encountered Jesus — and that was it," he said.

Arellan, who now runs an online shop called "D-King merch" selling Christian clothing, offered advice to people reconsidering their gender transitions.

"Following Jesus is not easy. It can be narrow, it can be hard, but it's so worth it," he said.

title: Utah mommy blogger Ruby Franke's daughter begs parole board not to let her out of prison: 'she is a monster'
description: Shari Franke revealed weekly nightmares of her mother's house as she urged the Utah Board of Pardons and Parole to keep Ruby Franke behind bars.
fullContent:
Shari Franke, the eldest daughter of disgraced Utah parenting blogger and convicted child abuser Ruby Franke, urged the Utah Board of Pardons and Parole to keep her and former associate Jodi Hildebrandt behind bars ahead of their upcoming parole hearings.
