title: Ethereum Dips to $1.5K, Stops $33 Above Its 2026 Low
description:
Key Takeaways About 90% of the summer rally erased. The June floor faces its third test. RSI near 20, matching […]
The post Ethereum Dips to $1.5K, Stops $33 Above Its 2026 Low appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

  • About 90% of the summer rally erased.
  • The June floor faces its third test.
  • RSI near 20, matching the June washout.

Ether futures liquidations reached $545 million over 24 hours as the wider market sold off, according to CoinGlass data cited by CoinDesk.

How Much of the Summer Rally Is Left?

Very little. ETH climbed from a June low near $1,505 to $2,803 in late September, and in under two months it has given nearly all of it back. At $1,628, about 90% of that advance is gone, and Saturday’s low at $1,538 had erased 97% of it before buyers stepped in. From the September high, ETH is down about 42%.

The way Saturday’s session has traded so far matters more than the low itself. ETH opened near $1,623, dropped to $1,538, and then recovered to $1,628, up 0.31% on the day as of 08:45 UTC, with about 15 hours left. That leaves a long lower wick, the first sign this week that buyers are willing to defend a level. It won’t count as a signal unless the candle closes that way.

Why Does the June Low Carry So Much Weight?

Because the market has tested it before and it held each time. The first test came in early June, when ETH crashed to about $1,505 on the heaviest volume of that period, with daily RSI deep in oversold territory. The second came in late June, when price dipped back to just above $1,500 and held again. The rally to $2,803 started from that double test.

1
Early June
Near $1,505 · held
2
Late June
Just above $1,500 · held
3
November 21
Low $1,538 · in progress

The current approach rhymes with June in two ways. Daily RSI is at 19.83, back in the same washed-out range it reached at the June low, and still under its own average at 25.86. Friday’s selling came on one of the heaviest volume bars since the June crash. A floor that holds a third time can become the base of a larger bottom. A floor that keeps getting retested can also wear down, because every bounce from it absorbs some of the buying behind it.

Below the June low, the next reference is the April 2025 low near $1,395, the deepest point of the previous correction.

Why Did Bitcoin Break Its Floor While ETH Kept Its Own?

On Saturday, bitcoin fell through its 2026 low near $57,700 and traded at $55,130, its lowest since September 2024. ETH didn’t break its 2026 low, even though it has fallen harder: about 42% from its September high, against roughly a third for bitcoin.

The difference is where each floor sits. ETH’s June crash went much deeper than bitcoin’s summer dip, so ETH’s 2026 low sits further below the recent range. That gave ETH more room to fall before reaching it. ETH’s floor is intact for now, but bitcoin losing its own one leaves ETH testing support in a market where the largest asset has already broken down.

What Is Pressing From Above?

The overhead levels form four clusters, and each one is a place where the next bounce could stall. Tap or click a level for the detail.

Near $1,783: the level that broke in mid-November
The 0.786 retracement held up the July lows. ETH broke it in mid-November, and the bounce that followed stalled when it reached the level again from below. It’s now the first line any recovery has to retake.
Near $2,000: the round number
The 0.618 retracement sits almost exactly at $2,000, where ETH spent much of the summer before its August breakout.
$2,127–$2,154: the 200-day and the midpoint
The 200-day average at $2,127 has started to tip lower, and it sits beside the 0.5 retracement. ETH trades about 23% below it.
$2,267–$2,368: the shorter averages
The 50-day at $2,267 has crossed under the 100-day at $2,368 and is falling toward the 200-day. The 0.382 retracement sits between them.

The averages show the trend. The 50-day is falling fastest and has already crossed under the 100-day, while the 200-day has only just started to roll over. Until price gets back above at least the first cluster, every rally runs into levels where recent buyers are underwater.

What Is the Largest Holder Doing?

Bitmine, the Tom Lee-chaired company that holds more ETH than any other public firm, has kept buying through the decline. Its latest weekly update showed 6,077,745 ETH, about 4.97% of supply, valued at roughly $11.1 billion at $1,823 on November 15. At Saturday’s price, the same stake is worth about $9.9 billion. Lee called the drop a “waterfall decline in price” that doesn’t reflect Ethereum’s fundamentals, The Block reported. The company has bought every week since mid-2025, and its next update will show whether it added on this week’s slide toward the June low.

Where Is the Line Drawn?

●
Green: a daily close back above the 0.786 near $1,783. ETH would have retaken the level it lost in mid-November, turning the breakdown into a failed one and putting $2,000 back in view.
●
Amber: holding between $1,505 and $1,783. The June floor survives its third test. The signs to watch are Saturday’s lower wick holding into the close and RSI crossing back above its average.
●
Red: a daily close below $1,505. The June floor gives way on its third test, and the April 2025 low near $1,395 becomes the next reference.

ETH sits about 8% above its June low and about 9% below the level it lost in mid-November.

title: Crypto Market Cap Dumps Below $2T as Bitcoin Rollercoaster Intensifies: Weekend Watch
description: ZEC and HYPE are today's biggest losers among the larger-cap alts. Two out of the top four cryptocurrencies are now stablecoins.
fullContent:
Bitcoin’s price experienced another major leg down on Friday and Saturday, plummeting to its lowest level since September 2024 at $55,000 before rebounding by $3,000.

The altcoins followed suit, going through massive volatility. Overall, though, the total crypto market cap has tanked by roughly $900 billion in weeks, dipping below $2 trillion on CMC.

BTC Tanks Hard

What a time to be alive and invested in all financial markets, especially crypto. It was just last weekend when BTC struggled at $66,000 after it had already declined by $15,000 in 10 days. The following several days were painful but in a relatively modest manner, with the cryptocurrency ranging between $65,000 and $62,000.

The upper boundary was too strong for the bulls to pass through, but the lower was tested too many times, and it felt inevitable that it would eventually crack. The Anthropic IPO, widely considered the biggest catalyst behind bitcoin’s collapse, provided the necessary push, and BTC indeed dumped below $62,000 as the week was coming to a close.

Friday was a particularly painful trading day, with BTC eventually slipping below $60,000 for the first time since early July. The bears kept the pressure on, and the cryptocurrency ultimately dumped below that July low and tanked to $55,000 on Saturday morning. This became its lowest price tag in well over two years.

Whether it was a dead-cat bounce or a more profound recovery, it’s unclear at the moment, but BTC managed to regain $3,000 almost immediately and now sits close to $58,000. Nevertheless, its market cap is down to just $1.160 trillion, while its dominance over the alts has dropped to 58.1% on CMC.

Alts Bleed Again

Ethereum slumped to $1,550 earlier today before rebounding to $1,625 as of now. XRP dipped toward $0.85, and it’s below $0.90 now. BNB, SOL, DOGE, XMR, LINK, and ADA have all tanked by 7%-8% on a 24-hour scale. ZEC and HYPE lead the adverse trend with double-digit losses and now trade at $730 and $58, respectively.

The landscape around the mid- and lower-cap alts is similar, with massive losses from NEAR, QNT, ONDO, RAIN, SUI, UNI, and many others.

The total crypto market cap dipped below $2 trillion today for the first time in more than two years. The metric has shed approximately $900 billion in the past few weeks.

title: Matt Hougan Sees HYPE Becoming the Next Amazon, but Hyperliquid Just Fell 11%
description: Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan calls Hyperliquid the next Amazon, yet HYPE slid 11% and trades below both averages. See why $74.50 resistance and $41 support matter now.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan said Hyperliquid could become the next Amazon as it expands into real-world assets and prediction markets.
  • HYPE sits below both key moving averages, and momentum gauges still favor sellers despite an oversold reading.
  • The chart shows a wide gap below current prices, with the nearest clear floor sitting far beneath the market.

Hougan has pitched Hyperliquid as a future Amazon for finance. The token hit a broad market sell-off just as the bullish call made the rounds.

The timing tests the thesis. Hyperliquid's revenue and buybacks look steady, yet HYPE has slid hard for weeks and sellers still set the pace. Traders now want to know if buyback demand and an oversold chart can halt the slide before the token reaches its next floor.

Bitwise's CIO Pitches Hyperliquid as an Amazon for Finance

Hougan said on a podcast earlier in November that Hyperliquid could become "the next Amazon." His case rests on reach. The exchange is pushing beyond crypto perpetual futures into real-world assets and prediction markets.

Jeff Yan, Hyperliquid Labs co-founder and CEO, wants the platform to "house all of finance." The model works like a marketplace. Builders who launch a market must stake 500,000 HYPE, worth about $34.4 million on Nov 19. That stake stays locked for at least 183 days. Vaults let anyone open a fund with as little as $100.

The business already earns real money. Hyperliquid took in $72.6 million in revenue over the 30 days to Nov 19, and nearly all of it goes to buying back HYPE. More than 261 perp DEXs have launched since 2022, yet Hyperliquid held 57% of DEX perp open interest in October. Competition remains the main risk, since rivals could squeeze its margins.

HYPE fell about 11% on Nov 20 during a broad sell-off that hit Nvidia even harder and dragged Amazon down 2.5%. No project news drove the drop, and the token remains up about 75% over 12 months.

HYPE Trades Under Both Averages After a Month of Losses

Hyperliquid (HYPE) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

HYPE traded near $57.60 on Friday, down about 6% over the past 24 hours. The token now sits below both of its key moving averages, which track the average closing price over a set number of days. When price trades under them, those averages tend to act as ceilings, and sellers hold the upper hand.

The 50-day average stands near $76. The 200-day average sits around $69. HYPE would need to climb roughly a fifth just to retake the longer line. Until it does, rallies are likely to meet selling from traders who bought higher.

Their order tells its own story. The 50-day line still rides above the 200-day line. That setup points to a sharp, recent drop inside a longer uptrend. Only a few weeks ago, HYPE traded comfortably above both.

Losses have also picked up speed. The token is down about 20% over seven days and roughly 29% over 30 days. A large share of the monthly decline came in the last week alone. That pattern shows sellers pressing harder as the slide went on.

On the daily chart, price now hovers near the bottom of its 30-day range. Buyers have not yet stepped in with enough size to mark a clear low.

Oversold, Yet Sellers Still Hold Momentum

HYPE's daily RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, has dropped to about 26. Readings under 30 count as oversold. That means the selling has run fast and far, and a short relief bounce often follows such stretches.

Oversold does not mark a bottom on its own. Tokens can stay oversold for days when a trend has real force behind it. The other gauges suggest this one does.

MACD, which compares short and longer price averages, still sits below its signal line. In plain terms, momentum keeps pointing down. Trend strength readings also show a firm trend, and sellers are the ones driving it.

Taken together, the picture favors caution. Any bounce would first need to show that buyers can hold gains.

A Wide Gap Separates Price From the Next Floor

The nearest ceiling sits near $74.50, just above the 200-day line and just under the 50-day line. A daily close back above that zone would be the first real sign of repair. It would tell traders that buyers can absorb supply from those who bought higher.

Higher up, resistance waits near $82.60. Clearing it would put HYPE back above both averages and turn the trend neutral at the very least.

Below, the map looks thinner. The only clear support on the daily chart lies near $41, more than a quarter below the current price.

If selling continues, little stands in the way until that lower level. The buyback flow may cushion the fall, but the chart offers no nearby shelf to catch it.

What Flips the Script Within Three Days

Two paths look most likely over the next three sessions.

  • Bullish: The oversold reading sparks a relief bounce, and HYPE closes a day above $74.45. That would open a run toward $82.61, backed by steady buyback demand. The case fails if price slips back below $57.57.
  • Bearish: Broad selling keeps pressure on the token, and HYPE drifts toward $40.99 with no shelf in between. This view fails if buyers reclaim $74.45 on a daily close.

Strong Story, Weak Tape

Hougan's thesis has real support in the numbers. The revenue is steady, the buybacks keep running, and Hyperliquid still leads its market by a wide margin. The chart still lags that story.

A wider sell-off could drag HYPE lower before buyback demand makes a dent. Rising competition from rival perp DEXs could also squeeze margins and test the marketplace pitch.

title: Zelensky calls Putin a 'killer' after Trump describes him as a friend
description:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has said Vladimir Putin is a "killer" in response to Donald Trump referring to the Russian leader as his "friend" in China this week.
Speaking to CNN, Zelensky said it was up to the US president "how to call Putin" but "for us, he is an enemy... for us, he's a killer".
Before Thursday's historic trilateral meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Putin, Trump called Putin his "friend" and said the two leaders have had a "great relationship for many years".
Russian attacks continued overnight, with two people killed, including a boy, and 52 injured in missile and drone strikes on Zelensky's hometown of Kryvyi Rih in the central Dnipropetrovsk region, officials said. 
Ukraine's state emergency service DSNS said 11 people were also injured in the north-eastern Kharkiv region, and one person in Rivne, in the north-west.
On Friday, at least nine people were killed in Russian strikes targeting bridges in the capital Kyiv and railway stations in western Ukraine - with Zelensky calling the attack the "biggest this year" after an onslaught of 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic, and more than 400 drones.
The strikes came days after Ukraine had badly damaged the Crimean Bridge.


[EPA]

Hours after Friday's strikes on Ukraine, Trump told reporters at the White House that Putin would "love to end the war".
"They [Zelensky and Putin] both want to end it and it's a very good thing I have a relationship," he said on Friday.
Trump also doubled down on his description of the Russian leader as a friend but said he "can't speak" to whether Putin is a friend to the US.
However Zelensky said despite Trump's stance, he saw Putin as "a killer".
"I think mostly for the people in the world, he is a killer because he's killing - by the way- he's killing each day and night," he told CNN.
Zelensky also said speaking about Putin like he was a "friend" meant "he doesn't feel enough pressure". 
The war of words came as neighbouring Poland said a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace in the south-east of the country early on Friday.
Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said the missile hit a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border.
This was about 100km from where European troops - from 11 of the 36 member nations of the coalition of the willing - were completing a training exercise, Polish authorities said.  Another cruise missile and a jet-powered drone were suspected to have hit two other locations, they added.
On Saturday, Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski told the BBC the cruise missiles had guidance systems, so "it is very unlikely that they veered off course as a result of Ukrainian electronic warfare".
"This is a war in Europe that affects our security," he told Radio 4's Today programme, also referencing similar incidents in recent months across Europe.
Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow.
Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned "grave violations of Polish airspace" and said the military alliance had scrambled its jets in response.
Russia has made no comment about the violations, which took place during Friday's massive attack on Ukraine.
Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Russia targets Kyiv crossings days after Ukraine hits Crimean Bridge
Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say
Trump greets 'my friend' Putin as pair shake hands 
This article originally appeared on BBC at https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cxnv4zvmdy0jo?xtor=AL-72-%5Bpartner%5D-%5Byahoo.north.america%5D-%5Bheadline%5D-%5Bnews%5D-%5Bbizdev%5D-%5Bisapi%5D

"I think mostly for the people in the world, he is a killer because he's killing - by the way- he's killing each day and night," he told CNN.

Zelensky also said speaking about Putin like he was a "friend" meant "he doesn't feel enough pressure".

The war of words came as neighbouring Poland said a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace in the south-east of the country early on Friday.

Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said the missile hit a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

This was about 100km from where European troops - from 11 of the 36 member nations of the coalition of the willing - were completing a training exercise, Polish authorities said. Another cruise missile and a jet-powered drone were suspected to have hit two other locations, they added.

On Saturday, Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski told the BBC the cruise missiles had guidance systems, so "it is very unlikely that they veered off course as a result of Ukrainian electronic warfare".

"This is a war in Europe that affects our security," he told Radio 4's Today programme, also referencing similar incidents in recent months across Europe.

Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow.

Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned "grave violations of Polish airspace" and said the military alliance had scrambled its jets in response.

Russia has made no comment about the violations, which took place during Friday's massive attack on Ukraine.

Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

title: Crypto Fear Reaches Extreme Levels as Bitcoin Plummets to $55K
description: The popular metric is deep in "extreme fear" territory.
fullContent:
Bitcoin’s rapid collapse below $60,000 and all the way down to $55,000 on Saturday morning has pushed the overall crypto sentiment to some of its darkest levels in months.

Santiment Intelligence said bearish commentary now heavily outweighs bullish discussions, while the Fear and Greed Index has plunged to just 12 – a dramatic reversal from the greed seen only a month ago.

Retail Sentiment Deep in Fear

Analysts at Santiment reported that BTC’s bullish-to-bearish commentary ratio on social media channels fell to 0.59 after BTC broke below $60,000 on Friday evening. Since then, though, the asset’s crash only intensified, dumping to $55,000 on Saturday morning for the first time in over two years.

In other words, bearish comments now substantially outnumber bullish ones across social platforms monitored by the analytics company. Santiment classified the reading as an “extreme fear” zone, suggesting that retail patience is beginning to break after weeks of relentless declines. Recall that the cryptocurrency pumped to $81,000 on November 5, but dumped by $26,000 in less than three weeks to this morning’s low.

The mood shift has been quite dramatic within this timeframe. Santiment warned earlier in November that overall sentiment around BTC, ETH, and XRP had fallen deep into bearish territory. At the time, bitcoin still saw 0.82 bullish comments for every bearish one, but that ratio has now deteriorated to 0.59 as the asset has continued marking fresh lows.

The popular Bitcoin Fear and Greed Index confirms this thesis, with the metric sitting at just 12 out of 100. This means it’s firmly in “extreme fear” territory, while it sat around 70 a month ago, which was close to extreme greed.

Can Things Turn Around?

Extreme fear is not automatically bearish. As the immortal advice from Warren Buffett goes, investors should be fearful when others are greedy, and, most importantly in this case, vice versa. Alternative.me’s website says something very similar, as low sentiment readings can typically indicate that investors have become excessively pessimistic, potentially creating buying opportunities.

Santiment has made a similar contrarian argument in the past, noting that major rallies frequently begin when retail traders remain deeply skeptical.

However, this doesn’t necessarily mean that BTC has indeed bottomed. Sentiment can remain depressed for long periods during sustained bear markets, particularly if ETF withdrawals, whale selling, and weak liquidity continue.

title: XMR Falls Toward $440 as a $13.5M Wrapped Monero Hack Rattles Privacy Coin Traders
description: Monero slid toward $440 after a $13.5M hack hit Wagyu's wrapped XMR token on Hyperliquid. XMR now trades below its 200-day average, the level bulls must reclaim.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • A hacker drained about $13.5M through Wagyu's wrapped Monero token on Hyperliquid, while native XMR stayed untouched.
  • Monero sits below both key moving averages, and oversold momentum has yet to slow the sellers.
  • The 200-day average now acts as the ceiling bulls must reclaim before any repair begins.

A compromised deployer key wiped out Wagyu's wrapped Monero token on Hyperliquid within half an hour. The founder blamed a breach at an Icelandic web host and pledged to cover user losses himself.

The Monero network itself was never at risk, yet XMR sold off alongside the broader market. Traders now weigh a relief bounce against a deeper slide toward far lower support.

A Wrapped Token Collapses While Native Monero Stays Intact

XMR1, a wrapped Monero token on Hyperliquid issued by cross-chain swap service Wagyu, lost more than 99% of its value in about 30 minutes. The token dropped from about $500 to around $1 after its deployer key was compromised.

On-chain analysis from Bitquery shows the deployer account sent 5.2 million XMR1 to a fresh account. That account sold roughly 364,000 tokens to 388 buyers for $13.5 million, then swapped the proceeds into ETH. About 7,350 ETH now sits across three wallets. The attacker's account was first funded through Tornado Cash minutes before the setup.

Wagyu founder PerpetualCow blamed a breach at Icelandic host 1984.hosting. He said the key sat on an old deleted server whose logs and files the host had kept. In a joint statement with CERT-IS, 1984 ehf. confirmed an extensive, sophisticated cyberattack and temporarily shut all services. PerpetualCow promised to personally refund all losses. Wagyu plans a relaunch but gave no timeline.

Native Monero was never touched by the exploit. Its price still fell about 8% on Nov 20. Bitcoin and HYPE also slid that day. Questions linger over Wagyu itself. The same deployer still controls nearly all ZEC1, its Zcash token, and the service suffered a separate data leak in October. Wagyu also appeared in ZachXBT's tracing of a suspected $106 million theft.

Monero Slides Under Both Moving Averages After a Brutal Month

Monero (XMR) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Monero trades near $442, down about 3% in the past day. The slide since the exploit has been steady, with no sharp crash. On the day of the hack, XMR still changed hands close to the price its wrapped copy had tracked before the collapse. Sellers have since pushed it well below that mark.

The longer windows tell a harsher story. XMR has lost about 16% in a week and roughly 29% in a month. Those numbers show the hack landed on a coin that was already falling.

A moving average smooths out daily swings by tracking the average closing price over a set number of days. Traders use the 50-day line to judge the recent trend and the 200-day line for the bigger picture. Monero now sits below both.

The 50-day average stands near $546, more than $100 above the current price. Short-term buyers who entered over the past two months are mostly holding losses.

Right now, the 200-day line near $474 matters more. XMR has slipped under it, which means the long-term trend line has flipped from a floor into a ceiling. A coin trading under both averages is in a clear downtrend by the most common chart definitions.

Sellers Stay in Charge Even as Oversold Readings Pile Up

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, reads about 29. Anything under 30 counts as oversold. In plain terms, sellers have pushed the price down faster than usual, and the move looks stretched.

Stretched moves often snap back for a while. Short sellers take profits, and bargain hunters step in. That can produce a quick relief bounce even inside a larger downtrend.

The other gauges argue against reading too much into that. The MACD, which compares short and long price averages, still sits below its signal line. That means momentum is pointing down and has not started to turn.

Trend strength tells a similar story. A real trend is in place, and sellers are driving it. An oversold coin can stay oversold for days when that pressure holds. Buyers need to see momentum flip before any bounce looks like more than a pause.

Why the Old 200-Day Line Now Caps Every Rally

The nearest resistance sits right at the 200-day average. That overlap matters. Two separate signals point to the same ceiling, so sellers who missed the earlier exit are likely to wait there.

A daily close back above that line would ease the pressure. It would show buyers can hold the long-term trend again, and the coin would no longer sit under both averages. The next hurdle above is the round number where Monero traded on the day of the hack. Clearing both would mark the first real repair since the slide began.

The downside picture is far less comfortable. The nearest support sits near $169, a long way below the current price. That leaves a wide air pocket with few obvious levels to slow a decline.

If selling continues, the next support is lower still, around $145. Neither level is likely to come into play quickly, but the gap shows how little the chart offers buyers on the way down.

Relief Bounce or Another Leg Down

Two paths stand out from here, and the 200-day line decides between them.

  • Bullish: A daily close back above the 200-day average would open a run toward the round number Monero held on the day of the hack. A drop back under today's price would void that setup.
  • Bearish: A rejection under the 200-day line would extend the slide toward the distant first support. A close above the hack-day price would cancel that view and hand control back to buyers.

Wagyu Owns the Hack and Monero Owns the Trend

Native Monero came through the exploit intact, yet its chart joined the selling. The coin looks oversold, and sellers still set the direction. That holds until XMR reclaims its 200-day line.

The risks lean lower. Support sits far below, and the same deployer still controls ZEC1. Any fresh trouble at Wagyu could keep privacy coins swinging hard.

title: Bitcoin Price Sinks to $55K as Its 2026 Floor Gives Way
description:
Key Takeaways Price broke the 2026 low near $57,700. Daily RSI at 16, lowest since late 2023. Network’s average cost […]
The post Bitcoin Price Sinks to $55K as Its 2026 Floor Gives Way appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

  • Price broke the 2026 low near $57,700.
  • Daily RSI at 16, lowest since late 2023.
  • Network’s average cost sits near $53,400.
  • $2.4 billion in crypto bets liquidated.

Bitcoin is down 28% for the quarter, extending a bear market that began after its October 2025 peak above $126,000.

Below the 2026 Floor

The break built over two sessions. On Friday, bitcoin fell through $60,000 for the first time since July, as worries over stretched valuations in artificial intelligence stocks hit risk assets, Reuters reported. The daily candle still closed near $58,952. Saturday’s session reached $59,248 and then slid to $55,130.

That low sits about 4.5% under the July low near $57,700, the level many traders had treated as this bear market’s bottom. It was also the base of the August–September recovery that lifted Bitcoin back above $70,000 before it stalled below $90,000. As of 06:49 UTC on November 21, BTC traded near $57,576, down 2.33%: off the low, but still just under the old floor.

Two Zones Below, One Ceiling Above

The chart marks two zones from earlier in the cycle. The upper one, roughly $50,500 to $55,400, is built from bitcoin’s mid-2024 lows, and Saturday’s low stopped almost exactly at its top edge. The lower one, $39,000 to $45,000, covers the early-2024 range. Between the two, the chart has very little trading history.

The upper zone also holds Bitcoin’s realized price, the average price at which every coin on the network last moved. Glassnode put it near $53,400 and said on Friday that the market-value-to-realized-value ratio had slipped to just above 1.

Below about $53,400, the average Bitcoin holder would be underwater for the first time since early 2023.
Based on Glassnode’s realized price

Overhead, the resistance levels have bunched together. The 200-day average at $72,473, Glassnode’s short-term holder cost basis near $74,100, Strategy’s average purchase cost of $75,452 and the 50- and 100-day averages near $77,000 all sit between $72,000 and $78,000. The 50-day has just slipped under the 100-day. For Strategy, the drop means its 850,849 BTC are worth about $50.2 billion against about $64.2 billion paid, and MSTR shares hit a new 52-week low, Yahoo Finance reported.

Oversold, Liquidated and Redeemed

The daily RSI reads 16.18, under its own average at 25.96. That’s the lowest reading on this chart, which goes back to late 2023.

Much of the selling was forced. Crypto futures liquidations reached $2.53 billion over 24 hours ($2.27 in longs), including more than $1 billion in bitcoin futures and a single $51.71 million long position, according to CoinGlass data.

ETF buyers have turned into sellers. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust recorded $541.1 million in net outflows on Thursday, its largest single-day withdrawal since launch. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost more than $580 million that day, bringing November’s outflows to about $3.47 billion, according to CoinDesk’s market briefing. Analysts also pointed to rising inflation-adjusted Treasury yields and a more hawkish Federal Reserve outlook. The Nasdaq fell more than 4% on Friday to its lowest since April, and gold dropped to its lowest since September 2025.

What the Big Names Are Saying

LEANING LOWER
“

Next stop … goblin town. Hold on to your butts.

Arthur Hayes, BitMEX co-founder, on X, Nov. 20, with no level or timeframe
“

Bitcoin would go down to $10,000.

Arthur Hayes, on a podcast this week, describing a 1929-style policy response he doubts authorities would choose
“

…a melt-down that most likely will lead to deflation.

Peter Brandt, veteran trader, on X, Nov. 20, describing financial and raw-material markets
LEANING HIGHER
“

Seller exhaustion will come long before Saylor exhaustion.

Michael Saylor, Strategy executive chairman, on X, Nov. 19
“

Bitcoin has weathered so much bad news.

Cathie Wood, ARK Invest CEO, to CNBC, Nov. 20

The two camps are arguing over different timeframes. Hayes and Brandt are describing the next few weeks, against a backdrop of an AI-driven credit squeeze and falling commodity prices. Wood said ARK’s $1.5 million bull case for 2030 still stands and that a return to the all-time high before the end of 2027 wouldn’t surprise her. Saylor said only bitcoin going to zero would break Strategy, which he said holds about 3.4 years of cash. He has also said that below a certain mNAV, Strategy could sell Bitcoin to buy back its STRC preferred stock. Neither bull named a near-term floor.

Two Cases From Here

The bear case builds if…
☐ Daily closes stay below the July low near $57,700
☐ Price closes under the top of the 2024 zone
☐ The realized price near $53,400 gives way
☐ A close under the zone’s base leaves the early-2024 zone as the next area with history
The bull case builds if…
☐ Saturday’s candle closes back above $57,700, making the break a failed breakdown
☐ RSI turns up from below 30 and crosses back over its average
☐ Price reclaims $60,000, the level lost on Friday
☐ The larger test remains the $72,000–$78,000 ceiling

For now, Bitcoin trades a fraction of a percent below its broken 2026 low and about 8% above the network’s average cost.

The post The Largest Hyperliquid Treasury Is One Bad Day From the Red appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Crypto treasury companies have had a brutal year, and most now sit on deep paper losses. Hyperliquid Strategies, the largest Hyperliquid treasury, was one of the few still showing a substantial profit on its pile of tokens.

That profit has now shrunk to a few cents per token. Hyperliquid (HYPE), the token the company holds, fell about 28% over the past month. 

A Profit Measured in Cents

The HYPE price stood at $56.94 at press time, according to BeInCrypto Markets data. Hyperliquid Strategies holds about 38.9 million HYPE, according to its latest results. As of October 28, its blended cost stood at $56.35 per token.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

That blended figure includes staking rewards. For the tokens it actually bought, the company paid $61.13 on average. That means those purchases are already underwater. 

The Cost of Buying Near the Top

The thin margin comes from when the company bought. During the September quarter, it spent $785 million on 9.1 million HYPE, its earnings release shows. That works out to roughly $86 per token.

BeInCrypto tracked that buying spree while HYPE traded near its record high. Every expensive purchase lifted the company’s average cost, raising the price HYPE must hold. 

The next earnings report could also take a hit. The latest quarterly profit came mostly from paper gains on HYPE, valued at a far higher price. If prices stay here, the next report would likely show a large loss.

The Smaller Rival With Room to Spare

Hyperion DeFi, a smaller Hyperliquid treasury, tells a calmer story. Its filing puts its average cost at $40 per token as of September 30.

Hyperliquid Strategies has almost no such cushion. A further drop of about 1% would push its blended holdings below cost.

title: Peter Schiff Warns ETH Could Hit $1,000 by Monday After Ether Breaks Key Support
description: Peter Schiff says ether could crash to $1,000 by Monday after breaking $1,600 support. We look at the $1,200 floor and oversold signals traders are watching now.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Peter Schiff warned that a weekend crypto crash could drag ether down to $1,000 by Monday.
  • Ether's momentum gauge sits deep in oversold territory, yet sellers still control the trend.
  • Traders are watching one support floor that stands between ether and Schiff's target.

Gold advocate Peter Schiff renewed his bearish call on ether Friday, saying the token broke a trend line he had flagged six days earlier.

The warning lands as forced selling hits leveraged bulls across the market and ether trails bitcoin. Thin weekend liquidity could magnify any move. Traders now want to see whether buyers defend the next floor.

Schiff Doubles Down as Ether Slips Under $1,600

Schiff issued the warning on Nov. 20, pointing to a weekend sell-off as the trigger. "Ethereum broke below key support at $1,600. It just traded below $1,580, down 16.5% in the six days since I issued this warning," Schiff said. He added there is a "real risk of a crypto crash over the weekend that sends ether to $1,000 by Monday."

His first warning came on Nov. 14, when he said of ether, "That chart looks even more ominous." His case rests on a monthly Bitstamp chart. A trend line drawn from the June 2022 low sat near $1,600, and ether has now broken it. Schiff sees the next buyers near the 2022 low, just under $1,000.

The selling hit the whole market. Bitcoin fell to $58,701 on Bitstamp. Coinglass data showed $427.51 million in ether liquidations over 24 hours, more than double the weekly average. Longs made up $375.07 million of that, or roughly 88%. Some 25,371 traders were liquidated. Leveraged bulls took the brunt of the drop.

Ether Trades Far Beneath Both Long-Term Averages

Ethereum (ETH) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Ether traded near $1,560 at last check, down about 4% over the past day. The losses run deeper on longer timeframes. The token has dropped about 19% in a week and about 37% in a month.

That slide has pushed the price to the bottom of its monthly range, leaving this month's buyers underwater. On the daily chart, each bounce has stalled at a lower level than the one before.

The moving averages tell the same story. A moving average smooths out daily swings by tracking the average closing price over a set period. Ether sits well below its 50-day average near $2,160. It also trades under its 200-day average near $2,260.

Traders read a price under both lines as a clear downtrend. Those averages now act as ceilings overhead.

The gap between the two averages matters too. The 50-day line has slipped beneath the 200-day line. That means recent prices are weaker than the longer-term trend, a sign the selling has gathered pace this autumn.

Schiff's target still sits a long way down. Measured from the Nov. 20 level, ether would need to fall about 38.2% more to reach it. A drop of that size over a single weekend would be extreme even by crypto standards. The trend points lower, but the distance remains large.

Sellers Stay in Charge Even at Extreme Oversold Readings

The daily RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, has dropped to about 17. Any reading under 30 counts as oversold. This one sits deep in that zone, a level ether rarely reaches.

Readings this low often come before short relief bounces. Sellers run out of fresh supply, and some traders cover short bets. Such bounces can be sharp and still fade within days.

Other gauges show no turn yet. The MACD, which tracks shifts in momentum, remains below its signal line. That means downward pressure is still building. Trend strength gauges also show sellers in control. Bulls need these signals to flatten before any lasting recovery can take hold.

$1,200 Is the Floor Before Schiff's Target Comes Into View

The nearest support on the daily chart sits near $1,200. That level is the first real floor between ether and Schiff's target. Buyers stepped in there before.

A close below that level would leave no mapped support underneath. The next stop would be the 2022 low that Schiff flagged. At that point, his call would move from a stretch to a live risk.

Bulls have their own markers overhead. The first resistance stands near $1,710, just above the broken trend line. A daily close back above it would undercut the crash case and suggest the breakdown was a false move.

The bigger test sits near $2,170, close to the 50-day average. Reclaiming that zone would signal that buyers had taken back control of the trend.

Two Weekend Paths for Ether

The levels above define two paths into the weekend.

  • Bullish: An oversold bounce that reclaims first resistance would open the way toward the zone near the 50-day average. The setup fails if ether slips back under its latest trading level, which would show buyers lack follow-through.
  • Bearish: A daily close below the support floor would put Schiff's target in play, with no mapped level in between. A close back above first resistance would cancel that case.

Trend Favors Bears but the Target Is a Stretch

Ether's downtrend remains in place. Schiff's call still needs one more break. The floor below has to give way before his target comes into reach by Monday.

Weekend trading adds its own risk. Thin liquidity and heavy leverage can turn small moves into large swings, in either direction.

title: Strategy Breaks Silence After BTC Crash as Bitcoin Position Dumps to $17B in Paper Losses
description: Bitcoin's latest capitulation has put unprecedented pressure on the largest corporate holder.
fullContent:
Bitcoin’s price collapsed to $55,500 on Saturday morning and continues to struggle below $56,000 as of press time, which pushed Strategy’s enormous BTC treasury roughly $17 billion underwater on paper, at least.

Yet Michael Saylor and the company he co-founded are showing little sign of abandoning the long-term BTC strategy, even as its immediate capital-allocation priorities appear to be shifting toward supporting its digital credit business.

Strategy Speaks Out

The latest SEC filing shows that the world’s largest corporate holder of BTC has 850,849 BTC on its balance sheet, acquired for approximately $64.2 billion at an average price of $75,452 per unit. The firm added another 485 BTC between November 9 and November 15 for $33.4 million, paying an average of $68,887 for the latest batch.

Recall that it was just a couple of weeks ago when bitcoin’s price tapped $81,000, and Strategy’s position was well in the green. Since then, though, the market has deteriorated, and the cryptocurrency tanked to $55,500 on Saturday morning for the first time in over two years. Given this valuation, BTC’s position is worth $47.2 billion, leaving the firm approximately $17 billion below its $64.2 billion aggregate acquisition cost.

It’s worth noting that these are all paper losses. Strategy has not realized a $17 billion loss by liquidating its bitcoin position now, nor has it outlined plans to do so. This figure moves rapidly with BTC’s price.

Against that backdrop, Saylor and the company he co-founded offered more insight into how they are thinking about capital allocation. In a post shared by Wu Blockchain, they said:

“During the 2022 bear market, our Net Reserve was negative. 1/3rd of our BTC was pledged as collateral. But we survived and emerged stronger.

Today, our Net Reserve is $35 billion. All our BTC is unencumbered. And our conviction and optionality have never been stronger.”

What Does It Mean?

Strategy can effectively choose among several capital-allocation routes, including exchanging MSTR issuance for bitcoin, STRC, or US dollars. However, Saylor indicated that the firm’s current top priority is supporting its digital credit business, particularly STRC, rather than blindly maximizing BTC purchases under every market condition.

That is already visible in its latest numbers. Strategy raised approximately $244.7 million from MSTR share sales during November 9-15, but allocated only $33.4 million to BTC purchases. The lion’s share was instead directed toward STRC repurchases. The same trend has persisted since the company restarted its bitcoin purchases in the autumn, with most of the money spent going toward the digital credit part of its business rather than BTC.

The post AMD Stock Crashes Another 13% – What’s Driving This Crisis? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) shares tumbled nearly 13% on Friday, November 20. The chipmaker has now lost more than 24% over five trading days.

Three main factors explain the latest selloff, from AI valuation fears to new legal pressure.

The 3 Factors Behind AMD’s Crash

A stock selloff is a rapid decline in share prices as investors rush to sell. In AMD’s case, several forces hit the stock at once.

1. Anthropic’s Rocky Debut

Anthropic’s rocky market debut weighed heavily on AI stocks. The company, which trades under the ticker ANT, slumped about 12% on its second day of trading.

That weak performance spread pessimism across the AI supply chain. NVIDIA fell about 7%, while Micron dropped roughly 12%. As a result, investors reassessed valuations tied to AI demand.

2. Mounting Legal Pressure

Meanwhile, several law firms announced investigations into potential securities class-action claims against AMD. The probes focus on whether the company misled investors about its ties with Chinese manufacturer IEIT Systems.

The investigations followed a report released the previous day. Consequently, risk-averse investors chose to reduce their exposure.

3. A Global Chip Selloff

A global semiconductor rout added further pressure. Overnight, chip stocks in Taiwan and South Korea led steep declines across Asian markets.

That weakness spilled into US trading, and the Nasdaq Composite fell nearly 3%. Moreover, AMD broke below its 200-day moving average near $429, which accelerated institutional selling.

What Comes Next for AMD Stock?

The short-term outlook remains uncertain. AMD is still a key player in high-performance computing and AI accelerators, and its long-term story has not changed.

However, AI valuation concerns, legal uncertainty, and a technical breakdown now weigh on the stock together.

Reclaiming the $429 level would mark a first step toward stabilization.

Anthropic’s trading in the coming sessions will also matter, since it now serves as a gauge for AI sentiment. If its shares stabilize, pressure on chipmakers like AMD could ease.

On the legal front, the firms have only announced investigations into potential claims so far. Still, a five-day loss of more than 24% shows how quickly sentiment can turn in the AI trade.

For now, investors will watch upcoming guidance and any updates on the legal investigations.

title: XRP Falls Below $0.95 as $1.4 Billion in Long Liquidations Sweep the Crypto Market
description: XRP lost its 95 cent floor as $1.4 billion in long liquidations hit crypto. Momentum is oversold, but bulls need a close above $1.01 to cancel the breakdown.
fullContent:
Quick Take

  • XRP lost its 95 cent floor as a wave of long liquidations swept across the crypto market.
  • Daily momentum sits deep in oversold territory, yet sellers still control the trend.
  • Bulls need a daily close back above $1.01 to cancel the breakdown.

XRP broke below a short-term floor as forced selling of leveraged bets hit the whole crypto market. Sentiment gauges slid to extreme fear, and heavy volume backed the move.

The break leaves XRP with thin chart support below current prices and bounces capped by falling averages. Traders now want to know whether an oversold market can spark a recovery before liquidation clusters pull price lower.

Leveraged Longs Pay the Price as XRP Loses Its 95 Cent Floor

XRP slipped below $0.95 over the past day, giving up a level that had served as a short-term floor. That support formed after a rebound off $0.90 earlier in the slide. Trading volume rose about 28% as the level gave way, a sign that sellers drove the break with conviction.

The damage reached well beyond one token. Long liquidations across crypto reached nearly $1.4 billion in 24 hours, CoinGlass data show. Traders who borrowed to bet on higher prices were forced out of their positions. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index dropped to 8, its lowest reading since February.

Liquidation heatmaps show the next large clusters of leveraged positions sitting near $0.9019 and $0.8934. Price often gets pulled toward those pockets as stops trigger.

One analyst who tracks XRP sees rebounds as short-lived bounces. His base case is a drop toward $0.80 unless XRP reclaims $1.01. Over three to six months, he said a Democratic midterm win could unwind post-election gains and send XRP to $0.50 to $0.60.

A Third of XRP's Value Gone in a Month

XRP (XRP) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

XRP traded near $0.88 at last check, down about 36% over the past 30 days. Most of the damage came before the latest break.

The past week alone accounts for a drop of about 13%. Losses on that scale late in a monthly slide show the selling picking up speed.

Today's dip of about 4% looks mild by comparison. It is the latest step in a decline that was already well underway.

Moving averages tell the same story. These lines track the average closing price over a set number of days, and they help show the direction of the broader trend. XRP sits well below its 50-day average near $1.17. That gap means the short-term trend has turned firmly against holders.

The 200-day average, a gauge of the long-term trend, stands even higher at around $1.31. Price below both lines means each average now acts as a ceiling. Every bounce in recent weeks stalled well below that ceiling as sellers stepped in.

Oversold Readings Have Not Stopped the Selling

XRP's daily RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 24. Readings below 30 count as oversold, meaning the selling has run hot and fast. Levels like this often come before relief bounces. They do not mark a bottom on their own.

Other gauges show no sign of a turn yet. The MACD, which compares short and long price averages, remains below its signal line. In plain terms, momentum is still pointing down. Trend strength readings confirm that sellers lead a real trend.

The shorter time frame points the same way. On the 4-hour chart, a bearish candle confirmed the breakdown below the recent trading range. The 4-hour RSI has held below 40 since then. Buyers have yet to show up with enough force to slow the decline.

Why $1.01 Matters More Than Any Floor Below

That level is the nearest resistance on the daily chart. A close back above it would cancel the breakdown and put the former trading range back in play. Until then, every bounce stays inside a falling market.

Beyond it, sellers wait near $1.20, close to the 50-day line. Clearing both would be the first sign that buyers have regained control of the short-term trend.

Below current prices, the chart looks far emptier. The nearest chart support sits around $0.63, well below current prices. No marked floor appears in between, so a further slide would have little to slow it beyond the liquidation clusters.

A move toward that support would bring the analyst's bearish mid-term targets into reach months ahead of his timeline.

Relief Rally or Another Leg Lower

Two paths stand out from here, and each hinges on a clear level.

  • Bullish: An oversold bounce that reclaims $1.01 on a daily close would open a run toward $1.20. A drop back under the recent low would hand control back to sellers.
  • Bearish: If XRP keeps failing under $0.95, a sweep of the liquidation clusters near $0.90 could drag price toward $0.80. Reclaiming the breakdown level would invalidate this path.

Sellers Stay in Charge Until $1.01 Falls

Sellers still set the pace, and the deeply oversold momentum gauge argues for a bounce at most. A reversal would need buyers to retake that resistance, and they have not.

Traders should expect violent swings. Sentiment sits at extreme fear, and leverage remains crowded on both sides. Either condition can spark a fast squeeze in whichever direction catches the most positions offside.

title: Bitcoin Price Plunges to $55.5K for the First Time Since September 2024
description: The liquidations on a daily scale reached $2.4 billion as the market continues to experience new lows.
fullContent:
The cryptocurrency market just can’t catch a break in the past few weeks, and it almost felt inevitable that bitcoin would eventually dump to a new low, beneath the July 1 floor of $57,700.

That took place on Saturday morning when the asset slumped to $55,500 for the first time in well over two years.

Markets Unravel

The chart above paints a clear and painful picture. Bitcoin plummeted to $57,700 on July 1, which many analysts described as this bear market’s low, especially since the asset skyrocketed in mid-August past $70,000 and even neared $90,000 in September. However, it was rejected there, and the subsequent retracement has been extremely violent.

The landscape worsened over the past month, especially after Binance suffered the biggest hack in terms of USD value. The conclusions of the US midterms, the massive ETF outflows, the war uncertainty, and the Anthropic IPO all contributed to another nosedive. The result is more than evident, with BTC barely hanging above $56,000 as of press time.

Recall that it had risen to $81,000 a day after the US elections on November 5, meaning that it has lost $25,000 in less than three weeks. The altcoins have crashed hard as well, with ETH dumping to $1,550, BNB tanking to $500, and XRP plunging to well below $0.90. HYPE and ZEC have dived by double digits in the past day alone.

Liquidations on the Rise

CoinGlass data shows the actual damage of the market slump. The total value of liquidations in the past day alone is up to almost $2.4 billion. The lion’s share, or $2.2 billion, came from long positions.

Moreover, 343,141 traders have been wiped out within the same timeframe, while the single-largest liquidation took place on Binance. It was a whopping one, worth nearly $52 million, and it involved the BTC/USDT pair.

title: XRP Bulls Lose $0.99: The Next Downside Targets Are Ugly
description: XRP was rejected at $1.00 once again this week.
fullContent:
The popular cross-border token has fallen further below the key $0.99 support level that analysts had been watching for weeks, which could now open the door to new lower lows.

Ali Martinez sees $0.80 and $0.64 as the next major downside zones, while EGRAG CRYPTO believes the token is deeply oversold. However, this doesn’t guarantee that the bottom is confirmed.

How Low Can XRP Go Now?

Martinez previously outlined $0.99 as the lower boundary of XRP’s broader channel and described it as a critical area the bulls needed to defend. However, they failed over the past several days, and the analyst sounded the alarm about further declines. The breakdown, he said, suggests a deeper correction may already be underway, with the next major levels sitting around $0.80 and $0.64.

For this bearish setup to weaken and perhaps be invalidated, XRP would have to blast through the $0.99 resistance and establish it as a support level again. Martinez’s warning comes as the broader outlook around the cross-border token has significantly deteriorated lately. Other analysts, such as ChartNerd, recently pointed out that a failure to reclaim the resistance between $1.03 and $1.14 could eventually send the asset back to $0.89 and even $0.70.

Martinez’s $0.64 low would represent the more bearish extension of a downside scenario that has been developing for weeks.

XRP BREAKS KEY SUPPORT LEVEL

$XRP has broken below the $0.99 lower boundary of the channel, suggesting that a deeper correction may now be underway.

The next major support levels I’m watching are $0.80 and $0.64.

For the bearish outlook to weaken, XRP would need to reclaim $0.99 as support.

— Ali Charts (@alicharts) November 20, 2026

Oversold XRP, but That’s Not All Good

EGRAG CRYPTO, one of the most vocal XRP bulls, didn’t appear too convinced in his latest post that the asset will simply collapse in a straight line. He noted that the token’s RSI is already in oversold territory, and XRP is already testing the lower boundary of a falling wedge. Although this combination can sometimes precede a short-term reversal, EGRAG remains cautious and outlined a few lower targets to test first.

The first is the major line at $0.915, which he described as critical support. If it falls, the analyst agreed that $0.80 remains firmly in play.

Nevertheless, he gave some hope to the bulls, indicating that there’s a possibility of a relief rally before another final retest of the lows. If that scenario plays out, XRP could rebound to $1.20-$1.25 and even up to $1.40, which he called his “zone of confidence.” A move back into those levels would provide much stronger evidence that buyers are regaining control. For now, though, there’s little evidence supporting this case.

title: Can Dogecoin Repeat a 760% Run From $0.054? A Technical Analyst's Call Meets the Chart
description: Dogecoin trades below the $0.054 floor analyst Ali Martinez tied to a past 760% rally. Here is what the chart says about his bullish call and DOGE support.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Crypto analyst Ali Martinez says Dogecoin could rebound from a floor that once launched a 760% rally.
  • DOGE already trades below that floor, with momentum indicators still favoring sellers.
  • Whether buyers can reclaim $0.054 will decide if his bullish setup survives.

Martinez's timing makes the call a hard test. DOGE has fallen sharply this month and now sits beneath the floor he flagged. Oversold readings hint at exhaustion, yet sellers still control the trend. Traders now watch whether buyers can win that level back.

Ali Martinez Bets on the Floor Behind a 760% Rally

Crypto analyst Ali Martinez sees a possible Dogecoin rebound from $0.054, a level he flagged as a key floor for the meme coin.

His reasoning rests on history. Martinez noted that the same zone preceded the 760% rally. He framed the setup as a chance for DOGE to bounce from "the level behind" that earlier run.

The call came without a price target or a time frame. It does carry one clear condition. Buyers need to defend that floor as support.

Live prices complicate that picture. DOGE trades near $0.051, about 6% below the level Martinez highlighted, so his condition is not met right now.

Dogecoin also slipped about 5% in the last day. A quick reclaim of the floor would put the setup back in play.

Dogecoin Sinks Far Beneath Both Key Averages

Dogecoin (DOGE) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Dogecoin's broader trend leaves little room for doubt. The coin trades below its 50-day moving average near $0.072, which tracks the average close of the last 50 sessions. It also sits under the 200-day average around $0.086, a common gauge of the long-term trend.

When price holds beneath both lines, each one tends to act as a ceiling. That is the textbook shape of a downtrend.

Recent losses point the same way. DOGE has shed about 21% this week and roughly 38% this month.

A reversal would have a long way to go. The 50-day average sits roughly 41% above the current price.

Oversold Readings Have Not Stopped the Selling

The Relative Strength Index (RSI), a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits at 22. Readings below 30 mark a coin as oversold. Selling at that pace often runs out of steam, and relief bounces tend to follow.

An oversold reading is not a reversal signal by itself. The MACD, a trend-following momentum tool, still sits below its signal line. That means momentum keeps pointing down.

Trend strength readings also show sellers in control. Until that changes, any bounce remains unconfirmed.

A Gap Down to $0.030 Raises the Stakes

The nearest support sits at $0.030. That floor lies far below the current price. No further support level shows up beneath it, so a break there would leave DOGE with little to slow a slide.

That gap raises the stakes for buyers. Martinez's level is the first test above price, and reclaiming it would be an early sign of stabilization.

Overhead, the first resistance matches the 50-day line. The next one waits near $0.078, about 53% above the current price. Clearing both would mark a real change in trend.

Two Paths From Here

Both outcomes turn on how DOGE closes relative to Martinez's level.

  • Bullish: A daily close back above Martinez's floor would validate his call. That would open a run toward the 50-day line, the first resistance overhead. The setup fails if price slips back under the floor after reclaiming it.
  • Bearish: Continued daily closes below Martinez's level keep sellers in charge. That path exposes the lone support far below. A firm reclaim of the floor would cancel this scenario.

The Call Hinges on One Reclaim

Martinez's call depends on DOGE winning back his floor first. So far the chart has not delivered that, and sellers still set the pace.

Oversold conditions can last for weeks. With support thin beneath the price, any further breakdown could turn sharp quickly.

title: DOJ turns attention to Democratic operatives in Alaska Senate election probe
description:
Alaska Democratic Senator-elect Mary Peltola looks on during a midterm election night watch party in Anchorage, Alaska, on November 3. - Justin Sullivan/Getty Images/File
With Alaska’s Senate race now called, the Justice Department is shifting focus toward Sen.-elect Mary Peltola’s campaign as part of its ongoing criminal investigation into an alleged scheme to run a spoiler candidate against her opponent, according to two people familiar with the matter.
The focus marks a shift in the investigation, which thrust the Justice Department into the center of a contentious political race. For months, investigators had focused on whether former candidate Daniel J. Sullivan intended to siphon votes from Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, whose name is similar.
Just before the election, however, a New York Times report described an alleged coordinated effort involving the Peltola campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) to improve her chances of victory.
Peltola has publicly said she was not aware of the alleged effort.
With public pressure from President Donald Trump and from Justice Department headquarters, some officials weighed whether a possible charge could be brought against the alleged spoiler candidate nicknamed “Decoy Dan,” according to one of the people familiar with the discussions.
The investigation has since shifted away from Daniel J. Sullivan and is now focused on Peltola’s campaign, the DSCC and outside political consultants allegedly involved in the scheme, another person familiar with the matter said.
The Justice Department also has sent dozens of FBI agents to Alaska and issued hundreds of subpoenas and preservation letters as part of the probe, that person said.
Gerald Heikes, a longshot candidate, was issued a subpoena as part of a DOJ probe, CNN previously reported.
More than a dozen people have received letters saying they may be targets of the investigation, CNN has reported.
Democrats have denounced the investigation as politically motivated, arguing that recruiting spoiler candidates is a common and legal strategy.
Meanwhile, the Justice Department has moved to drop its lawsuit seeking to block certification of Peltola’s victory. The suit argued that certification should be delayed while an investigation determined whether voters had been confused. A judge rejected the Justice Department’s longshot certification delay effort before Election Day, a move that hinged on whether the margin of Peltola’s victory was larger than the number of votes Daniel J. Sullivan received. The official count shows that even if Daniel J. Sullivan’s votes were counted for Sen. Sullivan, Peltola would still win.
Two days after the race was decided, the administration asked a court to declare the case moot.
CNN has reached out to the Peltola campaign and the DSCC for comment.

title: How Low Will Bitcoin Price Drop? Analysts Predict
description:
Bitcoin broke $60,000. See how low analysts at Wintermute, Cowen, and Rekt Capital think BTC could fall next.
The post How Low Will Bitcoin Price Drop? Analysts Predict appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
How low can Bitcoin go? BTC price fell below $57,000 on Friday, losing 30% in a month. Analysts suggest the pain might not be over. Most point to a bottom around $50,000 to $54,000. 

Bitcoin’s realized price sits just under $54,000. It is the average buying price of all Bitcoin holders. 

US spot Bitcoin funds have already shed about $3.47 billion this month.

Wintermute Expects Bitcoin Around $50,000

Crypto market maker Wintermute called the bear market unfinished in its November 16 update.

The firm pointed to the 200-week moving average near $68,000. That is Bitcoin’s average weekly closing price over roughly four years. Traders treat it as a long-term floor, and Bitcoin closed below it.

Money flows are the bigger worry. US spot Bitcoin ETFs are about $1.9 billion net negative in 2026. In 2025, they drew $21 billion in inflows.

“With flows negative and the 200-week lost, we expect pressure into the $50s, with Saturday’s $62k low the first level and the $60k put cluster on Deribit the next magnet,” Wintermute indicated.

A put cluster is a pile of options bets that pay out if the price falls to a set level. Both of Wintermute’s levels have now broken.

The Federal Reserve (Fed) adds pressure. Traders see a 97.9% chance of a rate hike on December 9. Higher rates hurt assets that pay no interest.

What Happens if Bitcoin Falls Below $54,000?

Crypto analyst Benjamin Cowen listed what Bitcoin usually does in bear markets. It typically falls in the fourth quarter of a US midterm election year. It also tends to fall after the first hike in a rate cycle.

Cowen said Bitcoin normally drops below its realized price, now under $54,000. He added that it then reaches the “balanced price,” which he described as “much lower” without giving a figure.

His on-chain risk gauge reads 0.167. In Cowen’s data, bottoms form when it falls below 0.1.

Meanwhile, BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes, now chief investment officer at Maelstrom, expected further downside, a remark he made when Bitcoin traded for $61,405 on Friday.

“Next stop … goblin town,” wrote Hayes.

Hayes gave no price target. “Goblin town” is trader slang for a deep bear-market low.

What Does Bitcoin’s Weekly Chart Show?

On the weekly chart, Bitcoin opened the week at $65,351 and fell as low as $57,100. That is a drop of over 10%, with more than two days before the weekly close.

  • The Relative Strength Index (RSI) reads 33.82. It means Bitcoin is nearing oversold levels, and selling may be stretched.

The RSI sits well below its own average of 53.89 and is still falling. Bitcoin’s weekly RSI last slipped under 30 in early 2026 and in mid-2022, near major lows. That leaves room for more selling before the gauge flashes oversold.

  • Volume profiles add another layer.

These horizontal bars show where traders have bought and sold most heavily in the past. Green bars mark bullish volume, while red bars mark bearish volume.

Between $60,000 and about $72,000, red bars outweigh green. That suggests sellers are clustered overhead, ready to meet any rebound.

Below the current Bitcoin price, the picture flips. Green bars outweigh red from roughly $58,000 down to $50,000, signaling buyers waiting lower.

That buyer zone overlaps the $50,000 to $54,000 range analysts flagged. It also matches the August 2024 lows, when Bitcoin briefly dipped near $50,000 before rebounding.

A weekly close below $50,000 would take price into thinner volume, where support is weaker.

Is a Bitcoin Bottom Closer Than It Looks?

Not every analyst sees months of pain. Rekt Capital says Bitcoin is less than 2% from forming a new bottom in the fourth quarter.

That would put Bitcoin back in step with its four-year cycle. The pattern describes Bitcoin’s habit of peaking and bottoming in roughly four-year swings.

Wintermute itself refuses to call a low. Still, it noted that weekly closes below the 200-week average have appealed to patient investors on a multi-quarter view. Earlier this month, Grayscale called the slide an attractive entry point.

Wintermute said it would turn less defensive only after:

  • A daily close above $68,000 with same-day ETF inflows.
  • A softer Fed outlook would also change its view.

The next tests come fast. The Fed’s preferred inflation gauge lands on November 25, followed by the rate decision on December 9.

Wintermute noted markets already price in three hikes by March. For now, Bitcoin is trading less like a hedge and more like a bet on US interest rates.

The post How Low Will Bitcoin Price Drop? Analysts Predict appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Nvidia and SanDisk Bets Joined Bitcoin in a $1.76 Billion Liquidation Wave
description:
Some crypto traders lost money on chip stocks over the past day, without ever touching Wall Street. Their losses landed in the same pile as Bitcoin (BTC) liquidations. That pile hit $1.76 billion in 24 hours. Wall Street’s Chip Trade Now Lives on Crypto Exchanges A liquidation happens when an exchange shuts a borrowed bet
The post Nvidia and SanDisk Bets Joined Bitcoin in a $1.76 Billion Liquidation Wave appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Some crypto traders lost money on chip stocks over the past day, without ever touching Wall Street.

Their losses landed in the same pile as Bitcoin (BTC) liquidations. That pile hit $1.76 billion in 24 hours.

Wall Street’s Chip Trade Now Lives on Crypto Exchanges

A liquidation happens when an exchange shuts a borrowed bet because the trader can no longer cover losses.

Crypto platforms now offer these bets on stocks through perpetual futures. The contracts track a share price, never expire, and trade around the clock.

SOXL, a fund that tracks semiconductor stocks with triple leverage, led the stock-linked losses. About $36 million in SOXL positions were liquidated, roughly double the XRP (XRP) total on Coinglass.

Bets on SanDisk stock and Nvidia stock followed, with close to $28 million liquidated in each.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

The Day Nvidia Lost Its Bronze Medal

The damage started on Wall Street. On Friday, Nvidia fell behind Alphabet to become the fourth most valuable US company. Alphabet was worth about $3.25 trillion. Nvidia sat at roughly $3.03 trillion according to Companies Market Cap.

The chipmaker had already slid into a bear market earlier this month. On Friday, its shares hit their lowest level since June 2025.

STS Digital CEO Maxime Seiler linked the crypto slide to the tech rout in comments to Forbes.

“This is a one-sided risk-off, with AI and tech leading it and Bitcoin down at $59,500.”

Bitcoin Loses $60,000 for the First Time Since July

The selling did not stop at $59,500. The Bitcoin price now stands at $58,558, down about 5% in a day. It is the coin’s first time since July below $60,000.

Some analysts had been watching that level. Katie Stockton of Fairlead Strategies told CNBC the bottom of Bitcoin’s trading range sat just below $60,000. 

That leaves leveraged traders with little room. If buyers fail to defend this zone, longs could face another round of forced selling. 

Stock perps now tie crypto leverage to Nasdaq trading hours. Until chip shares steady, their losses are likely to keep showing up in crypto liquidation totals.

title: Peter Brandt Sets a $31,400 Bitcoin Target as He Flags the Risk of a 75% Drawdown
description: Peter Brandt sees Bitcoin at risk of a 75% drawdown toward $31,400. RSI is deeply oversold, and $62K is the first level bulls must reclaim to turn the trend.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Veteran trader Peter Brandt warned that Bitcoin could suffer another deep crash like those in its past.
  • Daily momentum sits at an extreme oversold reading, yet sellers still control the trend.
  • Bulls need a daily close above $62K to show the first real sign of a turn.

The warning lands after a sharp monthly slide that left Bitcoin stretched and nervous. Traders now want to know whether an oversold bounce can hold.

Brandt Warns Bitcoin Could Lose Three Quarters of Its Peak

Peter Brandt, a veteran commodities trader known for classical chart analysis, has warned that Bitcoin faces the risk of a 75% drawdown. He put his downside target near $31,400. Brandt did not attach a time frame or specific conditions to the call.

His reasoning rests on history. Bitcoin has suffered crashes this deep before, and Brandt sees no reason the pattern cannot repeat. He framed it as a risk worth respecting, and he stopped short of calling it a certainty.

The live chart puts that target in context. Bitcoin trades near $58K, so the target sits about 46% below the current price.

On the daily chart, little stands in the way of a drop. No support level is mapped beneath the current price.

The call would weaken if Bitcoin recovered and held above the averages overhead.

Bitcoin Trades Far Beneath Averages Clustered Near $75K

Bitcoin (BTC) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Bitcoin now trades well under both of its key moving averages. A moving average smooths out daily swings to show the broader trend. The 50-day average sits near $74K. The 200-day average sits close by, near $75K, and both hang far above price.

That setup is bearish. When price holds below these averages, they tend to act as a ceiling on rallies. The two lines sit so close together that they form one heavy barrier.

The slide behind this structure has been steep. Bitcoin fell about 31% over the past 30 days. The selling also sped up recently, with a loss of about 15% in the last seven days alone. Roughly half of the monthly damage came in a single week.

Bitcoin finished the past 24 hours flat. A quiet day after a sharp drop often means sellers are catching their breath. One calm session does not reverse a trend that has run lower for weeks.

Sellers Stay in Charge Even at Extreme Oversold Readings

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits at 16 on the daily chart. Readings below 30 count as oversold, and this one is extreme. Selling this stretched often runs out of fuel, and a sharp bounce can follow.

Oversold does not mean finished, though. In strong downtrends, RSI can stay pinned low for days or weeks while price keeps sliding.

Other gauges side with the sellers for now. The MACD, which tracks shifts in momentum, remains below its signal line, so momentum still points down. Trend strength readings confirm a real trend, and sellers lead it.

$62K Is the First Wall Bulls Must Climb

The first resistance above price is the line bulls need to clear. A daily close above it would mark the first real sign of a relief rally. That would open a path toward the next resistance, which sits right where the two moving averages cluster overhead.

Clearing that upper zone would be a much harder task. It would also put pressure on Brandt's bearish case.

Below price, the chart shows no clear floor. That empty stretch is the gap Brandt's call targets.

Relief Bounce or Another Leg Down

Two paths stand out from here.

  • Bullish: A relief bounce produces a daily close above the first resistance. That would open a run toward the cluster of moving averages overhead. The case fails if Bitcoin slips back below its current level.
  • Bearish: Sellers reject price beneath the first resistance and resume the slide into unmapped territory below. A daily close above that resistance would invalidate this view.

The Trend Backs Brandt but Oversold Odds Cut Both Ways

For now, the trend favors the sellers, and Brandt's case keeps its footing until Bitcoin reclaims the first resistance.

The missing support cuts both ways. With no mapped floor, a fresh drop could gather speed quickly. A short squeeze from such stretched readings could move just as fast in the other direction.

title: Migrant caravan heads toward U.S. despite Trump's warnings
description:
Migrants from several Central American countries are walking towards the US (Jose TORRES)
A caravan of about 250 migrants, mostly from Central America, entered Mexico Friday after setting off on foot to reach the United States, despite President Donald Trump's warnings.
The group of young men and families with children, carrying their belongings on their backs, crossed the border bridge from Guatemala into Tapachula, AFP confirmed.
Carrying a banner that read "God with us," the migrants were not impeded by Mexican authorities. 
Since Trump's Republican party were dealt a harsh blow in the US midterm elections, migrant movement has increased, with half a dozen caravans crossing into Mexico in hopes of reaching the US.
Several migrants told AFP they had been in the United States previously, but were expelled during Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raids.
"I'm a victim of ICE, too. Right now I'm going for my little girl who is in Houston," 31-year-old Honduran Saba Najera said. "She's a newborn, they didn't even let me enjoy her, but that motivates me even more, it gives me more strength to cross the border."
The larger caravans have been blocked by security forces, and others have dispersed after Mexican immigration agents told them there was no chance of crossing into the US and offered them an opportunity to apply for asylum in Mexico.
Another caravan of about 100 migrants was moving toward the state of Oaxaca on Friday.
Trump has threatened to double tariffs on Mexico if the country doesn't stop the advance of the tariffs. 
His rebukes of the caravans figured prominently into his first term and his campaign against his predecessor Democrat Joe Biden.
