title: Trump and Dana White give Marine Band $500,000 after White House UFC event
description:
President Donald Trump and Ultimate Fighting Championship chief Dana White gave the U.S. Marine Band a $500,000 Friday. (ALEX WONG/Getty Images)

President Donald Trump and Ultimate Fighting Championship chief Dana White gave the U.S. Marine Band a $500,000 "big bonus" Friday, thanking the musicians who played the White House's summer UFC Freedom 250 fight card.
The check was presented at a reception on the South Lawn's new helipad, the first event held there.
Trump told the crowd the band had also performed for the visiting Chinese president and for King Charles, calling its members talented enough to play in the world's top orchestras.
The gift grew on the spot. The two men had first announced a $200,000 contribution from their personal funds before Trump raised the total.
"We're now making it $500,000. Now, everyone's going to get a lot of money," Trump said.
He put the band's size at about 170, and all 135 of its musicians attended.
Known as "The President's Own," the band dates to 1798. It landed a 2027 Grammy nomination this week for best orchestral performance for the album "John Williams and 'The President's Own' Vol. 3," a feat Trump called unprecedented.
The musicians supplied live music for the June 14 fight card on the South Lawn. White said the job took eight weeks of planning and 39 songs from 32 artists, many in custom arrangements.
"This band prepared for Freedom 250 like it was a military operation," he said.
War Secretary Pete Hegseth and House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., attended the helipad event, along with acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao and Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Eric Smith, KATU reported.
Trump said the band will perform for dozens of world leaders at the Group of 20 summit in Miami in December.

title: Federal court rules House unconstitutionally passed $1.7 trillion spending bill in 2022
description:
By Nate Raymond 
   Nov 20 (Reuters) - The US House of Representatives unconstitutionally passed a $1.7 trillion government funding bill in 2022 through a pandemic-era rule allowing lawmakers to vote by ‌proxy rather than in person, a federal appeals court ruled on Friday. 
   The New Orleans-based ‌5th US Circuit Court of Appeals voted 9-8 to uphold an injunction that outgoing Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton ​secured blocking enforcement of a provision of that measure that gave pregnant workers stronger legal protections. 
   Democrat Nancy Pelosi, the speaker of the House at the time, helped implement the proxy voting rule in May 2020 following the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic as an emergency measure. The rule was ditched when ‌Republicans took control of the House ⁠after the November 2022 elections. 
   Before Republicans took control, the House used the proxy voting rule to pass a spending package that included the provision Paxton challenged, ⁠called the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act. It was signed into law by Democratic President Joe Biden. 
   The bill passed the House on a 225-201 vote, with 226 members voting by proxy. 
   Friday's ruling, powered by the 5th ​Circuit's ​conservative majority, held that the proxy rule violated the ​US Constitution's quorum clause, which the court ‌said requires a majority of House members to be physically present to pass legislation. 
   "While the chambers of the legislature have much discretion regarding their rules of procedure, the Quorum Clause’s constraints on congressional power cannot be circumvented by congressional fiat," wrote US Circuit Judge Cory Wilson, an appointee of Republican President Donald Trump. 
   While the decision concerns how the entire bill was passed, the relief that ‌the 5th Circuit granted Paxton's office was narrow, as it ​barred the US Department of Justice and the Equal ​Employment Opportunity Commission from enforcing the pregnant ​workers provision against Texas. 
   The DOJ, which defended the law, and Paxton's office did ‌not respond to requests for comment. 
   US Circuit ​Judge James Graves, an appointee ​of Democratic President Barack Obama, in a dissenting opinion called the ruling "illogical, inexplicable, and invalid." 
   He said the majority read a physical-presence requirement into the quorum clause that does not ​exist. Graves said the majority provided ‌no explanation for why, if the entirety of the law was unconstitutionally passed, its ​ruling "should be limited only to one small sliver of the multitrillion dollar bill." 
   (Reporting by ​Nate Raymond in Boston; Editing by William Mallard)

fullContent:
By Nate Raymond

Nov 20 (Reuters) - The US House of Representatives unconstitutionally passed a $1.7 trillion government funding bill in 2022 through a pandemic-era rule allowing lawmakers to vote by ‌proxy rather than in person, a federal appeals court ruled on Friday.

The New Orleans-based ‌5th US Circuit Court of Appeals voted 9-8 to uphold an injunction that outgoing Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton ​secured blocking enforcement of a provision of that measure that gave pregnant workers stronger legal protections.

Democrat Nancy Pelosi, the speaker of the House at the time, helped implement the proxy voting rule in May 2020 following the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic as an emergency measure. The rule was ditched when ‌Republicans took control of the House ⁠after the November 2022 elections.

Before Republicans took control, the House used the proxy voting rule to pass a spending package that included the provision Paxton challenged, ⁠called the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act. It was signed into law by Democratic President Joe Biden.

The bill passed the House on a 225-201 vote, with 226 members voting by proxy.

Friday's ruling, powered by the 5th ​Circuit's ​conservative majority, held that the proxy rule violated the ​US Constitution's quorum clause, which the court ‌said requires a majority of House members to be physically present to pass legislation.

"While the chambers of the legislature have much discretion regarding their rules of procedure, the Quorum Clause’s constraints on congressional power cannot be circumvented by congressional fiat," wrote US Circuit Judge Cory Wilson, an appointee of Republican President Donald Trump.

While the decision concerns how the entire bill was passed, the relief that ‌the 5th Circuit granted Paxton's office was narrow, as it ​barred the US Department of Justice and the Equal ​Employment Opportunity Commission from enforcing the pregnant ​workers provision against Texas.

The DOJ, which defended the law, and Paxton's office did ‌not respond to requests for comment.

US Circuit ​Judge James Graves, an appointee ​of Democratic President Barack Obama, in a dissenting opinion called the ruling "illogical, inexplicable, and invalid."

He said the majority read a physical-presence requirement into the quorum clause that does not ​exist. Graves said the majority provided ‌no explanation for why, if the entirety of the law was unconstitutionally passed, its ​ruling "should be limited only to one small sliver of the multitrillion dollar bill."

(Reporting by ​Nate Raymond in Boston; Editing by William Mallard)

The post Bitcoin Breaks Below 59000 Within 2% of Summer Low appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
Bitcoin below 59000 printed on both spot and futures in the same session. Price traded within about 2% of the 2026 summer low near $57,700. Binance BTCUSDT last traded near $58,950 on November 20 after tagging a session low of $57,700.10. CoinGecko spot sat near $58,870 on the same tape with a 24-hour decline of about 5.3%. The break erased the August-September rebound. Nasdaq and AI-linked shares sold off. Futures venues forced roughly $1.5 billion in crypto liquidations.

Why Bitcoin Below 59000 Matters Now

The summer floor sits near $57,700 from the early July slide. CoinGecko OHLC prints show a July 2 low of about $57,779 on that chart. This means today's Binance wick to $57,700.10 tagged that band almost exactly. Spot near $58,870 still sits only about 2% above the $57,700 handle. In other words, bitcoin is testing the same summer base that defined the first half of 2026. It is not holding the midyear rebound.

That rebound had carried Bitcoin from the July trough toward a late-September peak near $87,330 on CoinGecko OHLC. The climb through late August and September is gone from the tape. Price is back at the door of the summer low rather than midrange between $70,000 and $80,000. This means holders who bought the August-September bounce now sit underwater against that peak. The market is pricing the July floor again.

The Liquidation and Equity Forced Move

CoinGlass-tracked futures liquidations across major venues reached about $1.49 billion over 24 hours. Long liquidations were about $1.35 billion of that total. Short liquidations were only about $142 million. Bitcoin alone accounted for about $736 million in forced closes, with roughly $669 million on the long side. This means the flush was a long wipeout rather than a short squeeze on leveraged books. Binance BTCUSDT open interest value also slipped by about $331 million. Price fell from the low-$60,000s into the high-$50,000s.

The equity tape set the risk tone on the same day. The Nasdaq Composite closed at 22,617.73 on November 20. That was down about 5.3% from the prior close of 23,879.20. Nvidia finished at $125.53 after a session loss of about 12.6%. The stock traded as low as $124.50. The Invesco QQQ Trust closed at $608.45, down about 5.7% from the prior close. This means AI and megacap tech selling hit the same risk channel that often pulls crypto when cash demand rises. Global crypto market capitalization fell about 7.4% over 24 hours on CoinGecko.

What Traders Watch After the $57,700 Tag

The base number is the $57,700 summer low from the first half of the year. The session print that tested it is Binance's $57,700.10 low on the futures pair. The leftover gap from spot near $58,870 is only about 2% above that floor. Holders now treat a hold above $59,000 as the first reclaim into a midrange trade. A clean break under $57,700 would put a new 2026 low on the board. That would confirm the August-September rebound failed. Binance's 24-hour high near $62,615 remains the rejected ceiling from the same slide. The wider stake is whether cash preference in AI equities keeps forcing leveraged bitcoin longs out at that floor.

The post ETH Slides Below $1,600 in a 10% Friday Rout appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
Ether broke under $1,600 on Friday as major venues printed the ethereum price below 1600 around 19:13 UTC. Binance ETHUSDT first tagged $1,597.77 at 19:12 UTC. The 19:13 minute then closed at $1,599.67. Coinbase ETH-USD crossed the same handle in that minute window. That bar closed at $1,597.45. The Friday session cut Ether about 10% from the daily open near $1,757. The Binance low was $1,581.47.

Why Ethereum Price Below 1600 Matters

The Binance daily candle opened at $1,757.31. It printed a high of $1,770.55 and closed at $1,623.09. This means the open-to-low drawdown was about 10.0%. The open-to-close loss was about 7.6%. In other words, the sub-$1,600 print was the flush, not the Friday settle. The deepest Binance print sat at $1,581.47 inside the 19:18 UTC minute. Coinbase showed a matching flush. That venue's low sat near $1,578.78 in the same six-minute stretch.

The path into that low started earlier in the session. The 15:00 UTC Binance hour opened near $1,743. It closed at $1,655.57 after a low of $1,650.00. This means about five percentage points of the Friday loss landed before the $1,600 break. Later hours kept grinding lower until the 19:12 UTC cross.

The break arrived inside a broader crypto risk-off tape. Bitcoin on Binance fell from the mid-$61,000s into a $57,778 low in the same window. Binance ETHUSDT perpetual open interest dropped by about 55,000 ETH between 19:00 and 19:30 UTC. That drop came as price carved the sub-$1,600 lows. From 14:00 UTC to 22:00 UTC, open interest fell by about 123,000 ETH. That was roughly $535 million in notional terms. Funding on the Binance ETHUSDT perpetual later sat negative near -0.019% per period. This means leveraged longs paid as the flush forced positions off the book.

What Traders Watch After the Flush

Holders watching the Ethereum pair now treat $1,600 as the broken round handle. They treat $1,581.47 as the Friday session low on Binance. Spot volume on that venue ran near 666,000 ETH for the Friday daily candle. That was more than double Thursday's roughly 302,000 ETH. The pair later reclaimed toward $1,623 into the daily close. It held near that zone into Saturday's early prints. A slip back under $1,600 would renew Friday's flush. Prior ETH climbs after a $1,741 dip showed how fast a reclaim can form after a flush. A hold above the reclaim keeps the bounce intact after the $1,581.47 low. The next test is whether ETH can defend that zone on quieter volume. The first bounce was funded by the open-interest flush.

description:

It still sat about 4.6% lower over 24 hours against the prior day's prints near $0.95. Aggregated force-close tallies from Binance, Bybit, and OKX put about […]
The post XRP Price Rebound Lifts Pair About 2.5% to Near $0.91 appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
An XRP price rebound lifted Binance XRPUSDT about 2.5% in one hour to near $0.91. The pair climbed from about $0.888 in the 21:00 UTC hour on November 20. It still sat about 4.6% lower over 24 hours against the prior day's prints near $0.95. Aggregated force-close tallies from Binance, Bybit, and OKX put about $460,000 in liquidations across those venues in the same hour. Spot buyers and the daily downtrend have found themselves at opposing ends of the same tape. The bounce is a symptom of an hourly reclaim that has not yet erased the session's broader slide.

Buyers Stepped Into the Hourly Bid

On Binance, the 21:00 UTC hour opened at $0.8884 and closed at $0.9090. The high of that hour was $0.9121. The low in that window touched $0.8842, the softest print of the session. Spot volume on the bounce hour ran near 9.7 million XRP, or about $8.7 million in quote terms. The prior hour had already pushed the pair from about $0.895 toward the $0.888 handle. That followed a deeper slide from levels near $0.97 earlier on November 20.

That sequence puts the move on a timed candle rather than a full-day turn. Buyers lifted the pair about two cents off the hour open before the print settled near $0.91. The high at $0.9121 shows how far the reclaim reached inside sixty minutes. The close at $0.9090 kept most of that lift intact into the next hour.

Why the XRP Price Rebound Meets a Soft Daily Book

The hourly win sat beside a soft daily book. Against the November 19 21:00 UTC close near $0.954, the rebound finish still left XRP down about 4.6% on a 24-hour window. Broader trackers later showed a 24-hour change near minus 5%. That matches a tape that bounced hard without reclaiming the day's earlier range. Futures open interest on Binance XRPUSDT rose from about 273 million to about 278 million XRP across the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC hours. Leveraged size did not empty as spot jumped.

About $460,000 in force-closes on Binance, Bybit, and OKX hit during that rebound hour. The figure is modest beside the multi-million flush totals that often mark a full leverage reset. It does show leveraged books paid when price jumped from the $0.888 open toward $0.91. In other words, the tape printed a short-side squeeze of limited size. It was not a clean break of the daily downtrend.

Holders watching the pair now treat $0.888 as the bounce open and $0.91 as the first reclaim mark. A slip back under $0.90 would erase the hourly gain that defined this move. A hold above $0.91 keeps the bounce intact after the $0.884 session low. The next test is whether XRP can defend that zone on quieter volume. The first push was funded by the liquidation burst.

The post XRP Price Rebound Lifts Pair About 2.5% to Near $0.91 appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.

title: Solana Beats Robinhood With 10x ANT Trades as Anthropic Stock Went Wild
description: Anthropic shares opened at $11.50, 34% above the $83 offering price, but closed at $97.17 after dipping as low as $92.27 during trading.
fullContent:
Solana recorded more than 10 times as many Anthropic (ANT) trades as Robinhood Chain on November 19, as the AI company’s first day on Nasdaq saw its stock go 17% higher by the closing bell.

The activity points to growing demand for round-the-clock access to listed stocks through blockchain-based trading platforms, although traditional exchanges are still the main venue for price discovery.

Solana Records 815K ANT Trades on Anthropic’s Nasdaq Debut

Data shared earlier today by Sunrise, Solana’s day-one asset gateway, showed that ANT recorded more than 815,000 trades on Solana compared with about 79,000 on Robinhood Chain.

That difference was also noticeable in the number of holders, with Solana getting more than 13,000 while Robinhood had just 1,474. Meanwhile, the ANT trading volume on Solana went past $75 million as Robinhood settled approximately $28 million.

Anthropic’s tokenized stock became available on Solana through Sunrise just seven minutes after it started trading on Nasdaq, and in its first hour, it reportedly generated more than $26 million worth of volume on the platform. That figure then rose to around $60 million after four hours of trading, accompanied by 660,000 trades and at least 10,000 holders.

Nasdaq’s closing bell did not end ANT trading on Solana, with Sunrise pointing out that the token would remain available throughout the night. The stock closed at $97.17 on Wall Street, up 17%, giving the creator of the Claude AI chatbot a market valuation of roughly $1.77 trillion, even as the wider tech sector registered a 2.4% drop. At one point, ANT traded as high as $111, which briefly took Anthropic’s worth past the $2 trillion mark.

As CryptoPotato reported, Anthropic had priced its IPO at $83 per share, giving it a fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion. Initially, the AI firm had set the price range between $70 and $78, but strong demand from investors justified the higher valuation.

Binance to Refund Anthropic xStocks Subscribers

Meanwhile, things did not go too smoothly on Binance, with the exchange’s “IPO-style” subscription campaign failing to deliver the tokenized ANT stock in meaningful quantities to subscribers.

“Due to circumstances outside of our control, the allocation for the Anthropic xStocks IPO Campaign on Binance Wallet was not ideal,” the trading platform posted on X. “All participating users’ USDC will be fully returned from the relevant smart contract to their Binance Wallet.”

It added that it will be airdropping 2,957 Anthropic tokenized stocks to users based on how much each of them had committed, alongside $1 million worth of bStocks ANT tokens to those who had applied for a subscription.

title: Robert Kiyosaki Cheers the Bitcoin, Gold, and Silver Crash. Here is Why
description:
Robert Kiyosaki is once again welcoming a market crash. The “Rich Dad Poor Dad” author says he is most excited about Bitcoin’s slide and cannot wait to buy more. However, not everyone shares his optimism, as some analysts warn of a deeper correction ahead. Why Kiyosaki Welcomes the Market Crash The sell-off hit hard. Bitcoin
The post Robert Kiyosaki Cheers the Bitcoin, Gold, and Silver Crash. Here is Why appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Robert Kiyosaki is once again welcoming a market crash. The “Rich Dad Poor Dad” author says he is most excited about Bitcoin’s slide and cannot wait to buy more.

However, not everyone shares his optimism, as some analysts warn of a deeper correction ahead.

Why Kiyosaki Welcomes the Market Crash

The sell-off hit hard. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 and now trades near $58,200. It lost 31% over the past month.

Meanwhile, gold and silver shed roughly $1 trillion in six hours after Fed minutes signaled further rate hikes.

Kiyosaki blamed problems at the Federal Reserve, banks, and bond markets, along with US federal debt near $40.6 trillion.

In contrast, Bitcoin’s hard cap of 21 million coins makes it unique money, he argued.

His stance is consistent. Kiyosaki has long targeted $250,000 Bitcoin and openly uses debt to buy assets. Not everyone shares that confidence, however.

Is the Crash Really a Buying Opportunity?

Some analysts agree. Ash Crypto listed six reasons why November could prove a strong entry point.

These include past cycle bottoms after US midterms and possibly completed pre-IPO selling. The analyst also cited rising bank holdings of Bitcoin ETFs, which already control about 1.24 million BTC.

Lower oil prices, improving US manufacturing, and typical post-midterm stock gains round out the list.

Still, caution remains. Veteran trader Peter Brandt noted that every major Bitcoin bull market has ended with a correction of at least 75%. Measured from the recent high, that move would imply roughly $31,500.

With Bitcoin down about 54%, that scenario would require a much deeper slide.

Other traders watch intermediate support near $55,000, now just 6% below current prices. Meanwhile, long-term holders like Michael Saylor keep emphasizing accumulation.

“I began buying Bitcoin at $20,000 a coin… after the last crash. Will wait for Bitcoin bottom again. Lesson: ‘Your profit is made when you buy…not when you sell’,” Kiyosaki said in another post.

Ultimately, the debate remains open. Kiyosaki sees a chance to buy scarce assets, while history leaves room for a deeper correction first.

title: NEAR Sinks 12% Onto Its 200-Day SMA: Three Paths Ahead
description:
Key Takeaways Friday’s high stopped under the 0.618 level. Price sits about 3% above the 200-day. RSI near 31.7, not […]
The post NEAR Sinks 12% Onto Its 200-Day SMA: Three Paths Ahead appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

  • Friday’s high stopped under the 0.618 level.
  • Price sits about 3% above the 200-day.
  • RSI near 31.7, not yet oversold.
  • Heavy selling volume, two hours before the close.

Two days ago, Coindoo’s analysis of NEAR’s three-level squeeze marked the 0.618 retracement near $3.23 as the floor of a 29-cent band. Friday’s candle ended that setup.

Out of the Bottom of the Band

NEAR traded at $3.34 when that analysis ran, with the 0.618 below, the 100-day average above and the upper edge of its descending channel pressing down on price.

On Thursday, a push higher poked above the channel line and then closed back inside, at $3.21, just under the 0.618. Friday opened at that level and reached $3.226, less than a cent below the 0.618 at $3.229, before the selling started. The low came at $2.76. As of 21:42 UTC, with about two hours left in the session, NEAR traded at $2.83, down 11.94% on the day and about 15% below where it stood on November 18. The drop came as the broader crypto market sold off.

The three levels from November 18, two days later
0.618 retracement, near $3.23
Floor → Cap
+14% from price
Upper channel line
Under test → Held as resistance
Just under the 0.618
100-day average, now $3.55
Ceiling → Further away
+26% from price

Resting on the 200-Day

The November 18 piece laid out what losing the 0.618 would expose: the rising 200-day average, then the 0.786 retracement beneath it. NEAR is now at the first of those. The 200-day has crept up from $2.72 to $2.74 since then, and Friday’s low stopped just above it.

2.5¢
How far above the 200-day Friday’s low stopped
3.1%
Gap between the current price and the 200-day
71%
Share of the August–October rally given back

The averages above price point in different directions. The 50-day, at $4.34, is falling and sits near the 0.382 retracement at $4.28, making that the highest resistance band on the chart. The 100-day at $3.55 is still rising, as is the 200-day. There has been no bearish crossover between any of them yet, but the 50-day has dropped about eight cents in two days and is closing in on the 100-day from above. NEAR now trades 53% below its mid-October high near $5.99.

Inside the Channel

The descending channel that began in late October is still intact. Every rally since then has stopped at its upper line, Thursday’s included, and Friday’s high came where that line runs just under the 0.618. Price now sits in the lower half of the channel. The channel’s lower line runs below the 200-day and is sloping down toward the 0.786 level, so the two will be close together within days if the channel holds its shape.

What Sits Below the 200-Day

The levels under the 200-day map to two phases of the rally. The 0.786 near $2.48 sits in the September shelf where NEAR traded between $2.40 and $2.50 before its mid-September breakout. $2.20 sits at the lower part of that consolidation. The full retracement near $1.52 marks the August low the whole Fibonacci grid starts from.

$2.74 · 200-day
›

Three Ways From Here

The 200-day breaks
daily close < $2.70
The rising average stops acting as support, and the 0.786 near $2.48 becomes the next reference, with $2.20 below it if the channel floor gives way. Rebounds into the $3.00–$3.15 zone would be the first test from underneath.
The break fails
dip < $2.74, fast reclaim > $2.80
A quick move back above $2.80 after a dip under the 200-day would leave sellers trapped below the average. The deeper version is a washout into $2.45–$2.50, where the 0.786 meets the September shelf, with RSI falling into the low-to-mid 20s.
The channel breaks upward
daily close > $3.30–$3.35
NEAR would be back above the 0.618 and outside the channel, with the 100-day at $3.55 and the 0.5 near $3.76 next. The November 17 close near $3.40, which unwound within two days, shows that a single close up there isn’t enough on its own.

For now, the nearest support is the 200-day, about 3% below price, and the nearest resistance is the 0.618, about 14% above.

title: Bayer agrees to pay up to $7.25 billion over Roundup cancer claims spanning decades
description:
JEFFERSON CITY, Mo. (AP) — Agrochemical maker Bayer will pay up to $7.25 billion over two decades to resolve thousands of claims from U.S. cancer patients asserting the company should have warned people that its popular weed killer Roundup could cause lymphoma, according to a settlement approved Friday by a Missouri judge.
The nationwide settlement applies both to Roundup users who already are ill and those who become diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma in future years. Participants could get an average of between $10,000 and $165,000, depending on how they used the product, how old they were when diagnosed and the severity of their illness.
For Germany-based Bayer, which denies that Roundup causes cancer, the settlement provides some financial certainty against mounting litigation costs that have led it to contemplate pulling the product from U.S. agricultural markets. Bayer already has changed the formula for its Roundup version sold to residential users.
Litigants also faced uncertainty. While the settlement was pending, the U.S. Supreme Court undercut one of the central arguments in the Roundup lawsuits. The high court ruled in June that Bayer cannot be sued in state courts on claims it failed to warn about cancer, because federal regulations don't require a cancer warning label and states are forbidden from imposing additional labeling requirements.
Though some attorneys for cancer patients contend the settlement payouts are too small, others argue the deal is better than getting nothing — which became a heightened likelihood after the Supreme Court ruling.
In a written judgment granting approval, St. Louis Circuit Judge Timothy Boyer said the average individual payouts are “fair and adequate” and the total dollar amount is “among the largest in the history of mass tort personal-injury class action settlements.” The approved settlement includes $600 million for attorneys' fees.
The judge said there was a risk Bayer would have filed for bankruptcy protection if the settlement had been rejected.
Bayer CEO Bill Anderson said in a statement that the court-approved settlement is “a decisive milestone in the company’s strategy to mitigate the risks of both pending and future Roundup litigation."
The decision could be appealed.
Roundup has been used on weeds for over 50 years
Missouri-based Monsanto debuted Roundup weed killer in 1974 with the chemical glyphosate as its active ingredient. The product quickly became one of the most widely used herbicides in agriculture. Roundup is designed to be used with genetically modified seeds that can resist the weed killer’s deadly effect, thus allowing farmers to produce more while conserving the soil by tilling it less. 
The product also is commonly applied on lawns and gardens. 
Bayer added Roundup to its portfolio when it acquired Monsanto in 2018. With it came a growing number of lawsuits alleging glyphosate causes non-Hodgkin lymphoma. But that remains in dispute. The World Health Organization’s International Agency for Research on Cancer classified the chemical as “probably carcinogenic” in 2015. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has determined that it’s not likely to cause cancer in humans when used as directed.
About 200,000 Roundup-related claims have been made against Bayer, many coming from people who used it on residential lawns and gardens. As a result, Bayer has removed glyphosate from its new versions of Roundup sold for residential markets. 
The lawsuits have produced mixed results. Only a couple dozen cases have gone to jurors, some siding with Bayer and others with plaintiffs. In one case, a Georgia jury awarded plaintiffs $2.1 billion.
In the first Roundup verdict since the Supreme Court’s precedent-setting ruling, a Missouri jury in October sided with Bayer in a case alleging design defects, negligence and fraud. The verdict “should send a strong signal” that plaintiffs “will face significant challenges” pursuing Roundup-related cancer claims in the future, said Bill Dodero, Bayer’s U.S. general counsel and global litigation leader.
Attorneys disagree on whether the settlement is fair
Bayer previously set aside $16 billion to cover legal costs related to Roundup cases. The new settlement, which is in addition to that, is designed to address most of the remaining lawsuits, as well as any additional cases brought in the coming years by people who were exposed to Roundup before the settlement was proposed in February. 
“Today’s final approval order delivers guaranteed compensation to Roundup cancer victims who have waited more than a decade for justice," said Christopher A. Seeger, a court-appointed counsel for cancer patients in the case. 
The settlement calls for Bayer to make annual payments into a special fund for up to 21 years, totaling as much as $7.25 billion. The amount of money paid out to individuals would vary. Agricultural, industrial or turf workers exposed at length to Roundup could receive an average of $165,000 if they were diagnosed with an aggressive form of the illness while younger than age 60. But anyone diagnosed at age 78 or older would get significantly less, with an average of $10,000.
Some attorneys have said the individual settlement amounts are too small and the terms too restrictive. 
“This settlement is the scariest, worst future settlement that’s ever been contemplated,” attorney Gerson Smoger said during a September court hearing on whether the settlement was fair. He said it locked in future claimants for decades with no chance at punitive damages yet “kept the product that they were exposed to on the market, allowing the victims to continue to be exposed.”
The settlement was filed in St. Louis Circuit Court in Missouri, home to Bayer’s North America crop science division and the state where many of the lawsuits have been brought. 
This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/bayer-pay-7-25-billion-214217018.html

title: Anthropic Stock—The Bull, Base And Bear Case Into Nasdaq-100 Entry
description:
Anthropic PBC (NASDAQ:ANT) fell from a $115.10 high on Nov 19 to an $83.15 low on Nov 20, a 27% drop in 2 sessions.
Underwriters fully exercised their option on 147 million extra shares, so the overallotment short that normally funds a price-support bid is already closed.
The Dec 15 lockup step makes up to 303 million shares, about $25.1 billion at $83, eligible for sale. That is about 5 times Bloomberg Intelligence’s $4.6 billion Nasdaq-100 buying estimate.
SpaceX, the last mega-IPO, first closed below its IPO price 5 weeks after listing and bottomed 22% lower before recovering.
Anthropic PBC (NASDAQ:ANT) is trading within cents of its $83 IPO price after one of the fastest reversals ever seen in a mega-listing.
The stock opened at $111.50 on Nov 19 and hit $115.10 intraday. It then closed at $97.17, up 17% on the day. On Friday, however, the selling resumed. Shares opened at $89.86 and fell to a low of $83.15. That is a 27% drop from the high in under 2 trading days.
The timing made it worse. The S&P 500 and the Dow both entered correction territory on Friday, and the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for 2026. As a result, the largest IPO on record is now trading as a high-beta proxy for the whole AI trade.
Most coverage now treats $83 as “support” simply because it is the IPO price. That assumption deserves a closer look. The deal mechanics suggest the usual safety net is already gone.
Chart 1: Anthropic gave back its entire IPO pop in 2 sessions. Day 2 is intraday as of about 12:50 p.m. ET, Nov 20.



How The Greenshoe Removed The Bodyguard
In a typical IPO, underwriters sell more shares than the base deal. Anthropic’s base offering was 980 million shares, and the pricing release granted the banks a 30-day option on 147 million more. That extra 15% creates a short position for the syndicate.
The short then becomes a tool. If the stock trades below the offer price, underwriters buy shares in the open market to cover it. 
That buying is the familiar “stabilization bid,” and it is permitted under SEC Regulation M, Rule 104. If the stock trades above the offer, the banks simply exercise the option and buy the extra shares from the company at $83.
Anthropic’s closing announcement confirmed the second path. The deal closed at 1.127 billion shares, including full exercise of the 147 million-share option. Gross IPO proceeds reached about $93.5 billion, or about $119.5 billion including a concurrent $26 billion private placement.
That detail matters for anyone treating $83 as a floor. Full exercise means the syndicate covered its short through the option. 
Consequently, there is no remaining short position that obliges the banks to buy shares on a dip. Stabilization is still legally possible during the window, but the economic reason to do it is gone.
In plain terms, $83 is now a psychological level, not a defended one.
The Float Math Works Against A Quick Bounce
Anthropic sold 1.127 billion shares against roughly 13.1 billion shares outstanding. That puts the IPO float near 8.6%. Under the registration filings on SEC EDGAR, non-founder employees could also sell up to 10% of their holdings from day one, about 315 million shares.

title: Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5%
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5%
The bitcoin price slipped to near $58,300 on Friday afternoon, briefly dipping under its summer low, as a chip-led selloff sent the Nasdaq down about 5% and dragged crypto stocks and miners sharply lower.
This post Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5% first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5%

The bitcoin price slid to near $58,300 on Friday afternoon, down about 6.2% over the past 24 hours, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a deepening selloff in chip and artificial intelligence stocks sent the Nasdaq down about 5% and pushed bitcoin just under its summer low.

Bitcoin broke below $60,000 late Friday morning, a few hours after this morning’s report had it near $61,500. Over the past 24 hours, the bitcoin price has traded between $57,655 and $62,562, a drop of about $3,880. Bitcoin is down about 25% in November, on pace for its worst month since June 2022.

Chip stocks drag Wall Street lower

Selling on Wall Street sped up through the afternoon. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% in late trading and the S&P 500 dropped about 3.5%. Yahoo Finance said the Nasdaq was on pace to close negative for the year, while the S&P 500 was poised to close in correction territory.

Chipmakers led the drop. Nvidia (NVDA) fell about 12.5% to near $128, and AMD, Broadcom and Micron also posted double-digit losses. Gold futures dropped nearly 5%. Treasury yields fell as traders rotated into bonds and defensive sectors such as consumer staples and healthcare, Reuters reported.

Anthropic (ANT) fell nearly 12% to around $86 on its first full day of trading, leaving it just above its $83 IPO price. The stock had closed its Thursday debut at $97.17 after raising $81.3 billion in the largest IPO of all time, CNBC reported.

Liquidations and outflows weigh on the bitcoin price

Leveraged traders were forced out as the bitcoin price broke support. About $1.53 billion in crypto bets were wiped out over 24 hours, with long positions making up $1.4 billion of that total. Bitcoin alone accounted for around $540 million, while ether fell more than 8% to around $1,600.

Bitcoin funds have been sellers, too. Investors have pulled roughly $3.5 billion from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs so far this month, including $582 million on Thursday. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest one-day outflow on record.

Rate worries are adding pressure. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Friday on calls for a half-point Federal Reserve hike in December. Traders still saw a more than 98% chance of a quarter-point increase, and some strategists warned that further hikes could deepen the selloff.

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop looks driven more by the AI stock selloff than by problems inside crypto. Bitcoin has increasingly traded alongside other growth assets that depend on easy money, he said.

The dip to $57,655 briefly took bitcoin just under its summer low near $57,700. It is also on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, its longest losing streak since 2022.

Crypto stocks extend losses

Strategy (MSTR) fell about 8.4% to near $78.90, adding to the losses after the stock fell for a sixth straight day on Thursday. Coinbase (COIN) dropped about 5.5% to near $103. Robinhood (HOOD) lost about 9.6% and Circle (CRCL) fell about 7.9%.

Bitcoin miners fared worst. MARA Holdings (MARA) sank about 17% to near $5.17, IREN (IREN) fell about 17% and CleanSpark (CLSK) dropped about 16%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) lost about 8.4%, and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) fell about 9.4%. Many miners have expanded into AI data centers, tying their shares to the chip selloff.

The bitcoin price is now down more than 50% from its record above $126,000, set in October 2025.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $58,300.

This post Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5% first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

fullContent:
Could 2027 finally be the year Cardano (ADA) overtakes Ripple (XRP) in the cryptocurrency rankings? Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta AI predicts that, despite XRP’s established position among the industry’s largest digital assets, network upgrades, renewed institutional interest, and a shift in investor sentiment could make it more likely than it first appears.

Both cryptocurrencies have spent years competing for attention, albeit with very different propositions. XRP has built its reputation around cross-border payments and financial infrastructure, while Cardano has focused on research-driven development, decentralized applications, and a carefully structured ecosystem.

However, market leadership can change quickly during a cryptocurrency bull market. If Cardano delivers on its ambitious development roadmap while XRP struggles to maintain its momentum, the gap between the two could narrow considerably.

And while flipping XRP would require an extraordinary rally, ADA could climb to a valuation few investors currently anticipate.

Meta AI Predicts Cardano’s 2027 Roadmap Could Be a Major Catalyst for the Flippening

One of Cardano’s biggest opportunities heading into 2027 is its ongoing push to improve network scalability.

The planned Ouroboros Leios upgrade is particularly important. Designed to increase transaction throughput without compromising Cardano’s decentralized architecture, Leios could address a longstanding criticism: its ability to compete with higher-throughput blockchain ecosystems.

Cardano’s Dijkstra development cycle also introduces further improvements, with Peras activation targeted for the second quarter of 2027. Peras is designed to improve transaction settlement speed by reducing the time needed to achieve stronger confirmation confidence.

Meanwhile, developments around programmable tokens, decentralized finance, and real-world asset tokenization could help Cardano attract applications that generate genuine demand for ADA.

These upgrades won’t automatically translate into higher token prices, but successful implementation could give investors a compelling reason to reconsider Cardano’s long-term valuation.

How Could XRP Be Vulnerable to an ADA Flip?

XRP has several advantages that Cardano cannot easily replicate. Ripple has spent years building relationships across the financial sector, while the XRP Ledger continues to expand into institutional decentralized finance, stablecoins, and tokenized real-world assets.

The network processed an average of approximately 2.48 million daily transactions during the first quarter of 2026, while its real-world asset market capitalization reached $2.25Bn. These are meaningful indicators of ecosystem activity.

However, XRP’s enormous market capitalization also creates a challenge for investors seeking outsized returns. With a much larger valuation than ADA, XRP needs substantially more capital inflows to achieve the same percentage gains.

Recent market comparisons have placed XRP’s valuation at roughly ten times Cardano’s, highlighting the scale of the challenge. If capital rotates toward smaller, established layer-1 networks during the next bull market, ADA could benefit disproportionately.

ADA vs. XRP: What Does the Long-Term Chart Suggest?

ADA previously reached an all-time high around $3.10 during the 2021 bull market, demonstrating that the cryptocurrency can attract substantial speculative demand when market conditions are favorable.

A sustained recovery towards its previous peak would be an important psychological milestone. However, a genuine breakout beyond that region would potentially open the door to a much larger valuation.

For XRP, the challenge is maintaining its market leadership while competing with an expanding range of payment-focused blockchain networks. Its established institutional presence provides a strong foundation, but continued adoption growth will be necessary to justify a substantially higher valuation.

The key technical signal to watch for ADA is a sustained sequence of higher highs and higher lows on the weekly and monthly charts, accompanied by improving relative strength against XRP.

A decisive break above previous cycle resistance, followed by a successful retest, could signal that a longer-term trend reversal is underway.

title: Storms on East Coast and atmospheric river in California may disrupt Thanksgiving travel
description:
Forecasters are monitoring a possible late-season Atlantic tropical storm that could disrupt travel along the East Coast ahead of Thanksgiving.
A cluster of low-pressure systems just offshore the southeastern U.S. has a 40% chance of developing into a tropical depression or storm over the next seven days, according to the National Hurricane Center's 1 p.m. ET Friday update.
NHC forecasters say the system's development and path remain uncertain. "Regardless of development, strong winds, dangerous surf, rip currents and coastal flooding is expected along the southeast and mid-Atlantic coasts this weekend," the NHC wrote in a Friday post on X.
"The timing of this storm could be especially disruptive for people getting an early start on Thanksgiving travel," according to AccuWeather meteorologist Haley Taylor. "Heavy rain could move into some of the busiest travel corridors in the Northeast Sunday night and linger into Monday morning, creating difficult driving conditions. Even if the storm stays offshore, coastal communities could still experience impacts, so small changes in its track will make a big difference in what travelers encounter."
This year, AAA projects that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home for Thanksgiving between Tuesday, Nov. 24, and Monday, Nov. 30, including 72.9 million traveling by car and 5.96 million taking domestic flights.
Flooding concerns grow in Florida
More than 16 inches of rain fell near Cocoa Beach, Fla., over a 72-hour period ending Thursday, according to AccuWeather. Additional heavy rain could trigger flash flooding, as the St. Johns River near Cocoa reached 18.6 feet on Friday, surpassing the 17.55-foot record set in 1953.
"One area of low pressure was forming along the northeast coast of Florida on Friday," AccuWeather meteorologist Brett Anderson said. "The storm will continue to produce heavy rain on northeast Florida, spreading into coastal Georgia through Friday night, and then into South Carolina Saturday to Saturday night."
Heavy rain and strong winds threaten the Carolinas
The Carolinas face a tropical storm threat from Saturday into Sunday, according to AccuWeather. 
Heavy rain and wind gusts of 40 mph or greater could affect the Carolina coastline beginning Saturday morning. 
Coastal North Carolina could see wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph, potentially causing power outages and coastal damage. 
A storm surge of about 1 to 2 feet could affect coastal areas of eastern Florida and the Carolinas.
Tropical wind and rainstorm eye path.
AccuWeather

Travel disruptions along the I-95 corridor
Heavy rain could spread from the southeast into the mid-Atlantic on Sunday, reaching the Northeast by Monday morning and potentially disrupting early Thanksgiving travel.
Travelers along the I-95 corridor from Washington, D.C., to Boston could encounter flooded roads and delays. Wind gusts could also reach 40 to 60 mph in southeastern New England.
New York City officials said Thursday that they had activated the city's Flash Flood Emergency Plan ahead of the rain and wind storm that could bring 1 to 3 inches of rain and 30 to 40 mph wind gusts.
Atmospheric river threatens California travel
Map of atmospheric river forecast to affect California leading up to Thanksgiving Day.
AccuWeather

Meanwhile, on the West Coast, heavy rain from an atmospheric river could slow Thanksgiving travel along I-5 in Northern and central California, with the greatest impacts expected Tuesday and Wednesday. The storm could also trigger flooding and mudslides.
Heavy snow in the Sierra Nevada could also complicate travel across mountain passes, with possible restrictions and closures.
"Drivers along I-5 should prepare for heavy rain that can reduce visibility and leave water collecting on the roadway," according to Taylor. "Travelers heading into the Sierra will face a different challenge, with heavy snow potentially making mountain routes difficult or impassable."
Forecasters advise travelers to check updated forecasts before departing.

title: Semiconductor Stocks Heading for Worst 2-Month Slump Since 2001 as Nvidia, Anthropic and the AI Trade Crack: This Week on Wall Street
description:
Semiconductor stocks are closing out a two-month collapse with only one precedent, and it was written in the autumn of 2001.
The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) fell 10% on Friday alone and is down 34.5% since Sept. 30. In 25 years of trading, the only worse two-month stretch ended in September 2001, at 35.1%, when the dot-com bust met the Sept. 11 attacks. The worst two months of 2008 took 33.2%.
Chart: iShares Semiconductor ETF two-month rate of change since 2001. Source: TradingView




For the fifth week in six, the AI trade lost ground, and this time the blow came from Washington.
A Friday That Belongs in the Record Books
Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) fell 13% on Friday to $127, its lowest since May 2025 and 48% below its Oct. 6 record. The week’s 22% loss is its seventh straight weekly decline, the longest run since July 2008, and November’s 38% drop is its worst month since that same July. Roughly $1 trillion of market value vanished this week alone, and about $3.2 trillion since the peak.
SanDisk Corp. (NASDAQ:SNDK) dropped 16%, Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) 14%, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) 12.7%, Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) 12.4% and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. (NYSE:TSM) 9%. For the week, SanDisk is down 28% and Micron 23%. The VIX jumped 20% to 34.
The S&P 500 Enters a Correction
The S&P 500 fell 3.2% on Friday to 6,949, its seventh straight loss. The streak has cost 8.7%, the deepest seven-session slide since February 2020. At 11% below its Oct. 6 record close, the index is in a correction for the first time since April 2025, down about 8% for the week and 8% for November, its worst month since September 2022.
The Nasdaq 100 fell 4.7% on Friday and 9.5% for the week, and turned negative for 2026, erasing a gain that stood at 24% six weeks ago. Its 17% drop since Sept. 30 is the steepest two-month decline since November 2008, and it sits within a point of a bear market. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1.5% on Friday and 7.6% for the week.
Nothing offered shelter. Gold slid 3% to a 14-month low and Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) fell 5.6% to $58,400.
Washington Draws the Line at 16 Nanometers
Anthropic PBC (NASDAQ:ANT) raised $81.3 billion in the largest IPO on record and opened at $111.50 on Thursday, 34% above its $83 offer price. By Friday it was back near $88. Nvidia beat estimates on Tuesday and guided to $130 billion in revenue. Investors sold anyway, because the story had moved from demand to permission.
A Commerce Department rule that took effect on Wednesday bars Chinese chip designers from buying 16-nanometer and more advanced chips without a license. Taiwan Semiconductor suspended orders from some Chinese customers, and Nvidia halted H200 shipments to China and removed the country from its forecast.
On Thursday, California Attorney General Rob Bonta served Nvidia with an investigative subpoena over former CEO Jensen Huang‘s China ties, and House Democrats opened a probe into whether the company tried to influence a federal investigation into chip smuggling.
President Donald Trump, back from meetings with Xi Jinping, took questions at the White House on Friday and drew the line himself. “We want only older chips,” he said of exports to China, adding that “in two years, Blackwell will be obsolete.”
He then turned to Huang. “He made some bad decisions, but he is a brilliant person,” Trump said, and compared him to Elon Musk: “I came to Elon’s defense in my first term very strong.” He “would love to see Jensen be given a second chance” after “a big apology.”
A Fed That Wants to ‘Shock People’
The Federal Reserve offered no cushion. Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC on Wednesday that inflation is “kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out,” and that to bring it down, “you might need to, like, shock people” with a half-point hike at the Federal Open Market Committee’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.
Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, long a dove, told reporters on Thursday, “I do not see that at this moment we are on path back to 2%.”
Treasuries drew safe-haven buying. The 10-year yield fell to 4.92% from 5.14% a week earlier, the 2-year to 4.62% from 4.85%, and the 30-year to 5.31% from 5.47%.
Michigan consumer sentiment rose to 51.5 in November from 48.0, with year-ahead inflation expectations down to 3.7% from 4.7%. Detroit did not share the relief: General Motors Co. (NYSE:GM) fell about 7% and Stellantis N.V. (NYSE:STLA) about 12% to a new low.
Dell, Then Thanksgiving
Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL), down 12% on Friday, reports its latest quarterly earnings Tuesday after the close, with consensus at $6.55 a share on $49.48 billion in revenue and options pricing a 15.7% move, according to Benzinga Pro data.
After September 2001, the semiconductor index needed more than 12 years to recover the ground it lost that summer. After this week, the question for Dell’s call is not how many AI servers customers ordered. It is how many of them Washington will let them ship.

title: Wells Fargo Led Wall Street’s Bitcoin Buying Spree in September as Institutional Holdings Hit a Record
description: The figures reflected holdings until the end of September. The market structure has shifted significantly since then.
fullContent:
The third quarter of 2026 marked a major shift in institutional demand for US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products, as investment managers returned to buying after three quarters of net selling.

According to Galaxy Research, 2,166 institutional managers reported holdings of 356,491 BTC-equivalent worth $29.78 billion as of September 30, a record level.

Big Institutions Loaded Up

Their net additions reached 49,229 BTC-equivalent, or roughly $4.11 billion, the largest quarterly increase since Q2 2025. The buying was led by major financial institutions. Wells Fargo added 14,636 BTC, followed by Brevan Howard, Bank of America, Millennium Management and Jane Street. The most notable development, however, was the continued rise of advisors and wealth management platforms, which added 24,838 BTC-equivalent during the quarter, accounting for roughly half of institutional net buying.

Their total holdings climbed to a record 144,307 BTC, representing 40.5% of all Bitcoin held by 13F-reporting managers, reflecting growing access to the crypto asset exposure through traditional investment channels.

The number of institutions reporting positions also increased by 191 to 2,166, and ended up reversing declines in the first half of the year. But much of the new participation came from relatively small positions.

Bitcoin exposure remained concentrated among a handful of large institutions. Galaxy found that the 25 biggest holders accounted for 60.8% of reported holdings and the 50 largest controlled 71.2%. Wells Fargo emerged as the largest holder, as it overtook Jane Street with 30,553 BTC-equivalent, while hedge funds continued to lose ground as a share of institutional ownership. Their combined share fell to 19%, down sharply from 50.6% at the end of 2024, while advisors and wealth platforms continued to expand their presence.

September Holdings, November Uncertainty

There are also differences in how institutions use Bitcoin ETPs, as positions held by wealth managers may represent client allocations, while hedge funds and market makers may use them as part of hedged trading strategies, Galaxy stated.

Despite the strong accumulation during the quarter, the figures reflect holdings as of September 30, which is well before BTC’s subsequent decline. By November 16, total Bitcoin held by the funds had fallen to 1.25 million from 1.29 million at quarter-end, leaving the market’s response to the downturn unclear until the next round of institutional filings.

title: Bitcoin Poised For 'Great' 2027 as Fed Eyes Aggressive Rate Cuts, Expert Says
description:
Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) could stage a strong recovery in 2027 as the Federal Reserve shifts from near-term tightening to aggressive monetary easing.
Speaking in an interview with Bitcoin Magazine, “42 Macro” founder and CEO Darius Dale said the Fed’s expected December rate hike does not constitute a policy mistake because the U.S. economy remains exceptionally strong.
He expects a potential Fed-Treasury coordination framework to support long-term Treasury markets and improve liquidity conditions.
“We think that surprising and dramatic easing in 2027 and beyond is still on the table,” Dale said.
Worsening liquidity conditions, persistent inflation and risks surrounding AI infrastructure spending could trigger another market selloff before Bitcoin establishes a bottom.
Dale predicts 2027 should be a great year for Bitcoin, with easier monetary policy potentially supporting cryptocurrencies, gold, silver and equities.
Why Is Bitcoin Falling Ahead of Other Assets?
Dale said Bitcoin signals weakening liquidity before gold and equities because its volatility makes it more sensitive to tightening financial conditions.
He expects Bitcoin to bottom ahead of other assets within months, with inflation easing by the second quarter of 2027.
However, year-end de-risking, AI infrastructure uncertainty and institutional selling could extend the downturn, echoing late 2018.
Bitcoin’s Bullish 2027 Outlook
Dale expects AI-driven productivity gains to boost economic growth, corporate profits and asset valuations in 2027.
Growing institutional adoption could reduce Bitcoin’s volatility, limiting both sharp crashes and explosive rallies.
He emphasized managing risk over predicting market bottoms, noting his firm’s risk management models had previously signaled Bitcoin exits.

title: SEC Charges Eight Firms in $37M Crypto Scam Using Fake Trading Platforms
description: The US Securities and Exchange Commission SEC charges eight Colorado-based entities accused of defrauding American investors of more than $37 million through fake investment advisory services and cryptocurrency trading platforms. According to the regulator, the alleged scheme relied on social media advertisements, private messaging groups and fabricated regulatory documents to convince victims they were dealing […]
fullContent:
The US Securities and Exchange Commission SEC charges eight Colorado-based entities accused of defrauding American investors of more than $37 million through fake investment advisory services and cryptocurrency trading platforms.

According to the regulator, the alleged scheme relied on social media advertisements, private messaging groups and fabricated regulatory documents to convince victims they were dealing with legitimate financial professionals. Investors were initially offered stock market advice before being directed to platforms that appeared to facilitate cryptocurrency purchases but were allegedly created to steal their money.

The SEC believes individuals operating from overseas were likely behind the operation, which ran from August 2024 through May 2026. Rather than relying on a single company identity, the alleged perpetrators moved through four successive combinations of investment advisers and crypto platforms, abandoning each setup after several months.

The case highlights how scammers continue to exploit the growing interest in digital assets by using the appearance of regulatory approval and professional investment services to gain victims’ trust.

Fake Investment Advisers Used Social Media to Target Investors

The SEC’s complaint describes a process that began with advertisements on social media platforms. These promotions directed potential investors into group chats and private conversations controlled by individuals allegedly involved in the fraud.

People participating in the chats presented themselves as representatives of investment advisory businesses and initially provided guidance on trading US stocks. Once investors developed confidence in the supposed advisers, they were encouraged to transfer larger amounts of money to cryptocurrency trading platforms.

Victims were led to believe that they were purchasing genuine digital assets through these services. However, the SEC alleges that the platforms were fraudulent fronts intended to collect investor funds rather than facilitate legitimate cryptocurrency transactions.

The operators also allegedly used fabricated SEC certificates and misleading regulatory records to make their businesses appear authentic. Some investors who questioned the legitimacy of the services were directed to filings submitted to the SEC, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) and the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN).

Eight Entities Named in the SEC Complaint

The SEC identified eight Colorado-based entities involved in the alleged operation:

  • Advisor WeChat Capital

  • Tech Brokerage Asset Alliance Ltd.

  • HB Wealth Advisors

  • IdeaCrypto Exchange LLC

  • Convergent Wealth Advisors Inc.

  • RealSimple Crypto Exchange Inc.

  • Associated Wealth Advisors Ltd.

  • Essential Crypto Exchange

According to the complaint, the entities operated through four successive adviser-and-platform pairings between August 2024 and May 2026. The alleged perpetrators switched to new business identities every few months, allowing the scheme to continue under different names.

SEC Warns Investors About Crypto Scams and Fake Regulatory Credentials

The latest case follows previous SEC warnings about investment fraud schemes promoted through messaging applications and online group chats.

In December 2025, the regulator issued an investor alert highlighting how scammers impersonate financial professionals and use group conversations to promote fraudulent investment opportunities. The agency has also warned that claims of SEC registration should not be treated as proof that an investment or platform is legitimate.

The SEC encourages investors to check the background of individuals and businesses offering financial products through its Investor.gov resources. It also recommends reporting suspected investment fraud through the agency’s online reporting portal.

While those figures cover different reporting periods, they provide context for the regulator’s recent enforcement activity involving digital assets.

The SEC’s latest action underscores how fraudulent operators can exploit the reputation of established financial institutions and regulatory agencies to make fake crypto services appear credible. For investors, verifying the identity and registration status of an adviser or platform remains an important step before transferring funds.

title: SEC Charges Eight Firms in $37M Crypto Scam Using Fake Trading Platforms
description: The US Securities and Exchange Commission SEC charges eight Colorado-based entities accused of defrauding American investors of more than $37 million through fake investment advisory services and cryptocurrency trading platforms. According to the regulator, the alleged scheme relied on social media advertisements, private messaging groups and fabricated regulatory documents to convince victims they were dealing […]
fullContent:
The US Securities and Exchange Commission SEC charges eight Colorado-based entities accused of defrauding American investors of more than $37 million through fake investment advisory services and cryptocurrency trading platforms.

According to the regulator, the alleged scheme relied on social media advertisements, private messaging groups and fabricated regulatory documents to convince victims they were dealing with legitimate financial professionals. Investors were initially offered stock market advice before being directed to platforms that appeared to facilitate cryptocurrency purchases but were allegedly created to steal their money.

The SEC believes individuals operating from overseas were likely behind the operation, which ran from August 2024 through May 2026. Rather than relying on a single company identity, the alleged perpetrators moved through four successive combinations of investment advisers and crypto platforms, abandoning each setup after several months.

The case highlights how scammers continue to exploit the growing interest in digital assets by using the appearance of regulatory approval and professional investment services to gain victims’ trust.

Fake Investment Advisers Used Social Media to Target Investors

The SEC’s complaint describes a process that began with advertisements on social media platforms. These promotions directed potential investors into group chats and private conversations controlled by individuals allegedly involved in the fraud.

People participating in the chats presented themselves as representatives of investment advisory businesses and initially provided guidance on trading US stocks. Once investors developed confidence in the supposed advisers, they were encouraged to transfer larger amounts of money to cryptocurrency trading platforms.

Victims were led to believe that they were purchasing genuine digital assets through these services. However, the SEC alleges that the platforms were fraudulent fronts intended to collect investor funds rather than facilitate legitimate cryptocurrency transactions.

The operators also allegedly used fabricated SEC certificates and misleading regulatory records to make their businesses appear authentic. Some investors who questioned the legitimacy of the services were directed to filings submitted to the SEC, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) and the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN).

Eight Entities Named in the SEC Complaint

The SEC identified eight Colorado-based entities involved in the alleged operation:

  • Advisor WeChat Capital

  • Tech Brokerage Asset Alliance Ltd.

  • HB Wealth Advisors

title: S&P 500 Drops Below 7,000 as Nvidia Faces Accounting Investigation
description:
The S&P 500 broke below 7,000 as Nvidia's SEC probe reportedly turned to accounting. See the next market triggers.
The post S&P 500 Drops Below 7,000 as Nvidia Faces Accounting Investigation appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
S&P 500 has dropped 3% on Friday, dropping below 7,000 to its lowest price in 6 months. This comes as reports suggest the SEC is investigating Nvidia’s accounting. 

Meanwhile, Nvidia shares fell 12% to $128 – its lowest price in over a year. NVDA reportedly accounts for 6.1% of the  S&P 500

SEC Probe Into Nvidia’s Accounting

The Wall Street Journal first reported the civil probe on Nov. 17. Its focus then was whether Nvidia’s disclosures misled investors.

Friday’s reports said the inquiry now explores potential accounting issues. The SEC has not confirmed the probe or named the items under review.

The executive running Nvidia has overseen its finances since 2013.

Colette Kress became interim CEO on Nov. 11 after Jensen Huang resigned. Nvidia’s filing said she would keep the CFO role.

One reporting change has drawn scrutiny. Nvidia stopped listing Singapore as a separate revenue region in late 2025, after it billed $10.2 billion there in one quarter.

Nvidia said it switched to grouping sales by customer headquarters.

The Next Market Triggers for Nvidia and the S&P 500

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent gave Nvidia’s board and outside counsel 10 days to answer questions. He asked whether Nvidia knowingly sold chips to China to lift earnings.

On Dec. 1, Huang faces closed-door interviews with three House committees. General counsel Tim Teter follows on Dec. 2.

Nvidia also held back its quarterly report, the 10-Q, after Tuesday’s earnings. The 40-day filing window from the Oct. 25 quarter end closes in early December.

Nvidia has settled with the SEC before. In 2022, it paid $5.5 million over undisclosed crypto mining sales.

Nvidia now trades about 46% below its 52-week high of $243.37. Its slide sits inside a wider AI and tech selloff that also hit AMD this week.

title: Zcash Price Crashes Through $800 With Little Support Below
description:
Key Takeaways Mid-November support near $800 gave way. Bounce stalled at the 0.5 level near $975. 50-day average falling fast […]
The post Zcash Price Crashes Through $800 With Little Support Below appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

  • Mid-November support near $800 gave way.
  • Bounce stalled at the 0.5 level near $975.
  • 50-day average falling fast toward the 100-day.
  • RSI just under 30, no capitulation volume.

Friday’s drop came as part of a broader selloff across the crypto market.

A 15% Candle Through the $800-$810 Zone

ZEC opened Friday near $894, reached $899 and then fell as low as $746. As of 19:36 UTC, with more than four hours left in the session, it traded near $763, down 14.67%. That puts price under two levels that sit almost on top of each other: the 200-day simple moving average at $810 and the 0.618 retracement near $800.

The zone had already been tested once. ZEC’s first leg down in mid-November stopped just above it, and buyers pushed price back up from there. When ZEC traded near $921 earlier this week, Coindoo’s weekly chart analysis named the 200-day as the nearest daily support if the weekly channel floor gave way. On Friday the candle went straight through it, taking ZEC to prices it last traded at in late August.

How the Decline Built

From the peak to Friday, one step down at a time
Late September
Peak near $1,700
Early October
Rising trendline from the June low gives way
Oct – early Nov
Range capped around the 0.236 level near $1,355, with wicks above it but closes below
Mid-November
Range floor breaks; first slide stops just above $800-$810
Earlier this week
Bounce stalls at the 0.5 level near $975
November 20
Candle cuts through $800–$810

Each support has also held for less time than the one before. The October range kept ZEC up for about five weeks. The mid-November low lasted about one.

Little Trading History Below $746

Friday’s low near $746 marks the bottom of the area where ZEC paused after its August breakout. Below it, the climb from about $550 to $800 happened so fast that the chart has almost no closes in between. That’s why the next labeled support sits as far down as the 0.786 retracement near $560.

Trading history between $450 and $900
▼ -$763
$450
$900
■ $450–$500: core of the summer base, about two months of trading
■ $500–$580: upper summer range, with its ceiling near $560 tested in July
■ $580–$746: crossed in a few late-August candles
■ $746–$900: about two weeks of trading in late August and early September

Averages Overhead, Momentum Just Turning Oversold

ZEC has now lost all three daily averages, one at a time: the 50-day in October, the 100-day in the mid-November break and the 200-day, at $810, on Friday. Higher up, the 50-day at $1,169 is falling fast toward the 100-day at $1,116, which is still rising but flattening. The 0.382 retracement near $1,145 sits between the two, which makes $1,116-$1,169 the densest resistance band on the chart. The 50-day is still above the 100-day, but the gap between them has narrowed sharply since early November.

The 14-day RSI reads 29.52, just under the 30 line that marks oversold territory and well below its own average at 37.01. It has only just crossed that threshold: a fresh oversold reading, not a deep one.

Volume reads 238.25K ZEC with more than four hours left in the session, small next to the spikes that marked the June low and the late-August breakout. Nothing on the chart yet resembles the volume of a washout.

What the Daily Close Sets Up

BREAKDOWN HOLDS
Below $800
If: ZEC closes below $800 and retests into the $800-$825 zone fail
Then: the broken 200-day becomes resistance, and the $560–$580 area, just above the 0.786 level, is the next reference
WASHOUT AND BASE
Near $560
If: price reaches the area near $560 or sweeps into $500-$540, with a volume spike and RSI steadying in the low 20s
Then: the chart would show the exhaustion this week’s selling has lacked, at the strongest support below $746. If $560 gives way, the $450–$500 base is the next reference
FAILED BREAKDOWN
Above $860
If: ZEC closes back above $825-$850, reclaiming both the 200-day and the 0.618 level, and then clears $860
Then: Friday’s drop becomes a failed breakdown, and the 0.5 level near $975 comes back into range

That leaves ZEC with resistance about 6% above, at the 200-day average, and the next labeled support about 27% below, near $560.

title: NVDA Tanks 10% as SEC Reportedly Launches Nvidia Investigation
description: The stock price just dumped to $130.
fullContent:
Reports emerged minutes ago that the United States Securities and Exchange Commission has opened an investigation into Nvidia’s accounting practices.

Citing people familiar with the matter, the Wall Street Journal and Reuters reported that the agency will probe the company, but the actual focus of the investigation remains unclear at the moment.

Although details are scarce, the timing of the lawsuit is quite intriguing as it comes following the major scandal involving Nvidia’s co-founder and now former CEO, Jensen Huang.

The controversy began a few weeks ago after reports claimed that he had an extramarital relationship with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy. Although there’s no confirmation to this day whether she was indeed spying for Beijing, further reports indicated that he had a few more affairs with women working at Nvidia.

He broke his silence earlier this week, apologizing for his behavior and suggesting that he could return to the helm of the company he co-founded decades ago. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump urged Nvidia to reinstate him.

The lack of details from today’s SEC investigation reports couldn’t stop Nvidia’s stock price from dumping. NVDA has slumped by almost 11% during today’s trading session alone, dropping to $130 for the first time in a year and a half. The stock is down by almost 50% in less than two months.

Long liquidations: $542.6 million (55%) versus $448.2 million in shorts (45%).

Open interest: $786 million, down 19% over the past week.
Long/short ratio: 2.90, indicating crowded bullish positioning.
Top traders’ ratio: 1.40, suggesting more balanced positioning among larger traders.
On-chain metrics also point to significant investor losses.
Critical Liquidity Zone
Wedson identified $0.053 as a critical downside liquidity zone, with major long liquidation clusters concentrated around, $0.0534 ($26.8 million), $0.0531 ($27.4 million) and $0.0528 ($23.4 million).
A decline toward these levels could trigger additional forced selling as leveraged long positions unwind.
Meanwhile, the nearest short liquidation clusters sit at $0.0649 and $0.0652, representing $7.5 million and $7 million, respectively.
Wedson warned that leverage continues to exit the market even as retail traders maintain bullish bets, leaving Dogecoin vulnerable to further liquidation-driven volatility.
