title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
The SEC obtained an asset freeze against Backward Hat Capital and its founders, alleging a $560 million Ponzi scheme sold as AI-driven FX trading funded through crypto. Prosecutors and the CFTC filed parallel cases.
This post SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme

The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading.

The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme.

Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets.

The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month

According to the SEC’s complaint, Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange.

Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted.

Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase.

Where the money went

The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million.

Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme.

Prosecutors in Manhattan charged Williams and Johnson with securities fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to commit securities fraud. The FBI arrested Williams in Kokomo, Indiana, and Johnson in Gilbert, Arizona, on Wednesday. Prosecutors put the total raised at more than $600 million.

“As alleged, Phillip Patrick Williams and Devin Allen Johnson promised to use investor funds for profitable foreign exchange currency trading,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “Williams and Johnson instead stole hundreds of millions of dollars from their investors for personal expenses and to pay off earlier investors in a Ponzi-like fashion.”

Regulators’ latest crypto fraud cases

The CFTC put the Ponzi at more than $550 million from at least 2,100 participants and said defendants kept soliciting money through at least October 2026. Its complaint seeks restitution, disgorgement, civil penalties, trading bans and a permanent injunction. The SEC is seeking injunctions, disgorgement and civil penalties.

The case follows other recent enforcement actions tied to crypto-branded fraud. The SEC charged two companies in a $130 million crypto trading scheme last month, and New York sought a $1.37 billion judgment against the operators of the NovaTech Ponzi scheme. In August, the CFTC charged Goliath Ventures with a $400 million bitcoin fraud.

Anne McKinley, acting associate director of the SEC’s Chicago Regional Office, said the promise of “a low-risk, high rate of return on a purportedly complex investment should make all potential investors stop and think before investing their money.”

This post SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Solana Price Loses Its Summer Floor, June Low Back in View
description:
Key Takeaways Reclaim of the 0.786 level lasted one day Friday’s high stalled just under $74 Rally from June low […]
The post Solana Price Loses Its Summer Floor, June Low Back in View appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways
Reclaim of the 0.786 level lasted one day
Friday’s high stalled just under $74
Rally from June low is 87% erased
RSI near 23.5, oversold but not turning

The Level SOL Couldn’t Keep

When SOL traded near $79 a week ago, Coindoo’s November 13 analysis flagged the 0.786 Fibonacci retracement near $74 as the last level above $60. This week’s trading has revolved around that line. SOL broke below it within days, then closed back above it on November 17, near $75, for a single session. It slipped under the level again over the next two days, and Friday’s candle opened just below it, near $73. The high stopped roughly 35 cents short of the level before sellers pushed price to an intraday low near $68. As of 18:49 UTC, with about five hours left in the session, SOL traded near $69, down 6.14%.

The November 17 close also raises the bar for any recovery. One close above $75 has already happened and reversed within a day, so a reclaim that counts would need to hold for more than one session.

From Floor to Ceiling

The same level played the opposite role a few months ago.

July-August
The floor
The $73-$75 area was the base of a summer range SOL traded in for weeks. The 50-day average turned up from that zone in August, and the range became the launch point for September’s run to $125.
November
The ceiling
Since the mid-November break, the level has capped the bounce. It is now the first level any recovery has to retake.

87% of the Summer Rally Is Gone

June low to September high: what’s left
$60 · June low
87% given back
$125 · September high
Teal: the share of the rally SOL still holds at about $69.

Measured from the June low near $60 to the late-September peak at $125, SOL has given back about 87% of the rally and sits 45% below the high. Above price, the 0.618 retracement near $85 and the 200-day average at $89 sit close together, forming the next resistance band after the 0.786 level. Below, the full retracement near $60 is the only labeled level left. It marks the June low that the whole Fibonacci grid is drawn from.

What June Actually Looked Like

The space between Friday’s price and the June low has trading history on it. After the early-June plunge to near $60, SOL spent weeks moving between that low and the level it is now testing from below, with long wicks in both directions and a late-June pullback into the lower part of the range. None of that range carries a labeled level on this chart, but buyers and sellers have traded there before. Friday’s low near $68 is the first line to watch. Under it, the June range is the reference all the way down to the full retracement near $60.

Averages Above, Momentum Stretched

All three daily averages sit above price: the 100-day at $100, the 50-day at $97 and the 200-day at $89. The 50-day has just slipped under the 100-day as it turns sharply lower. It is still above the 200-day, so this isn’t the 50/200 “death cross,” but SOL trades about 22% below even the lowest of the three.

Momentum points the other way. The 14-day RSI reads 23.5, well inside oversold territory, and it is still under its own average near 24.1, so it hasn’t turned up. On this chart, the only comparable reading came in early June, at the low the Fibonacci grid starts from. Readings this low can persist through a strong selloff, and they can also produce sudden short-covering spikes, so the oversold reading cuts both ways.

Volume favors the sellers, with a caveat. It spiked on the mid-November breakdown, faded during the bounce, and picked up again on Friday: 2.91 million SOL with hours still left in the session, already above the bounce days. The candle isn’t finished, though, and it is still lighter than the breakdown days.

Outside the Chart

SOL’s slide ran through a busy stretch for the network. Solana completed its move to 200-millisecond slots on October 9, halving its original 400-millisecond target, according to the Solana Foundation’s upgrade page. SOL was trading above $100 at the time. Last weekend the network dropped its “mainnet beta” label and adopted Solana 1.0 as a shared version number, a change that CoinDesk noted doesn’t make transactions faster or affect holders. The Solana Foundation’s Breakpoint conference ran in London from November 15 to 17. None of it slowed the decline, and neither did long-range valuation work such as Bitwise’s $1,100 scenario, whose assumptions run out to 2031.

Fund flows line up more closely with the chart. US spot Solana ETFs took in $271.6 million in September, as SOL rallied to its high, then saw $143.7 million in net outflows in October as the breakdown began, according to CoinDesk. On November 18, Roundhill asked the SEC to withdraw its proposed Solana covered-call ETF, which had never sold a share. Friday’s drop also came alongside the wider market: Bitcoin briefly fell tog around $59,000.

Three Ways Out

Continuation
● Bounces stall in the $72-$74 zone, under the 0.786 level
● Friday’s low near $68 gives way
● The $61-$60 area comes into play, just above and then at the June low
Reversal setup
● Price sweeps below the June low near $60
● A fast daily close back above it, a swing failure
● RSI prints a higher low, a bullish divergence
● Only then does the path toward $74, then $85, reopen
Invalidation
● A daily close back above $75-$76
● It holds for more than one session, unlike November 17
● Friday’s breakdown becomes a bear trap, with the $85-$89 band as the next resistance

These are conditions, not a forecast. Until one of them triggers, SOL sits between a level it has failed to hold twice in a week and a low it hasn’t tested since June.

The levels and scenarios above describe conditions on the chart, not predictions of future prices. Cryptocurrencies are highly volatile, and you should do your own research and consider your own risk tolerance before making any investment decision.

title: Why Is Arista Networks Stock Plunging Friday?
description:
Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE:ANET) stock plunged about 10% on Friday as a broad technology sell-off weighed on AI infrastructure stocks amid mounting concerns over elevated valuations and heavy capital spending.
The decline came alongside sharp losses in semiconductor and technology shares, reflecting a broader retreat from AI-linked stocks.
The Nasdaq dropped 3.12%, the S&P 500 fell 1.56% and the Technology sector declined 4.65%.
       • Arista Networks stock is feeling bearish pressure. Why is ANET stock dropping?
Arista Networks, which provides networking solutions for AI data centers, cloud computing and enterprise environments, has benefited from accelerating infrastructure demand. However, concerns over the sustainability of AI spending and stretched valuations continue to pressure the sector.
At the end of the third quarter, Arista Networks reported purchase commitments of $11.4 billion, mostly representing purchases for chips related to new products and AI deployments.
During the earnings call, management anticipated strong demand in AI fabrics and campus networking, and provided a positive outlook on its AI-driven products, particularly the EtherLink portfolio and the autonomous virtual assistant, AVA.
Recent Results Highlights
On Nov. 3, Arista Networks reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, beating the $3.33 billion analyst estimate.
The company reported quarterly adjusted earnings of $1.20 per share, which beat the analyst estimate of $1.08.
The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $3.9 billion to $4 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.26 to $1.30, both exceeding Wall Street estimates.
Technical Analysis: Trading Below Short-Term Averages
From a longer-term trend view, ANET is still holding just above its 200-day SMA ($168.59), but it’s trading 6.5% below the 20-day SMA ($182.27) and 11.3% below the 50-day SMA ($192.06), which keeps the intermediate trend pointed lower.
The 20-day SMA is also below the 50-day SMA (a bearish crossover). That signals lingering short-term weakness.
Momentum has improved. The MACD is above its signal line, while the histogram is positive. Both indicators suggest buying momentum is strengthening.

Key Resistance: $191.00 — Round-number area that also lines up closely with the 50-day SMA/EMA zone.
Key Support: $158.50 — Nearby prior demand zone that sits below the 200-day trend area.
Analyst Outlook
The stock carries a Buy rating with an average price target of $233.38. Recent analyst moves include:

UBS: Maintained a Buy rating and raised its price target to $291 on Nov. 4.
JPMorgan: Maintained an Overweight rating and raised its price target to $270 on Nov. 4.
Piper Sandler: Maintained an Overweight rating and raised its price target to $261 on Nov. 4.
Benzinga Edge Rankings
Arista Networks scores highly for momentum, growth and quality on the Benzinga Edge Rankings.
Its Momentum score stands at 94.11, while Growth is 84.88 and Quality is 91.4. However, its Value score is just 7.61.
The combination reflects Arista’s strong price momentum and growth profile, alongside a valuation that leaves less room for disappointment.
ANET Price Action: Arista Networks shares were down 10.76% at $169.19 at the time of publication on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

title: Walmart Gets Bullish Rating Despite Pharmacy Deflation Headwinds
description:
Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) shares are recovering on Friday after declining on Thursday following its third-quarter results.
It reported an adjusted EPS of 65 cents, exceeding analyst expectations of 64 cents. The figure excludes an after-tax loss of 3 cents per share related to equity and other investments.
Revenue rose 5.2% year over year to $188.835 billion, topping the consensus estimate of $187.271 billion.
However, Walmart’s weight-loss drug windfall is losing momentum despite rising prescription volumes.
Analyst Price Forecast Revisions
Several analysts raised their price forecasts following Walmart’s third-quarter results and increased guidance, while maintaining their existing ratings.
Morgan Stanley analyst Simeon Gutman maintained an Overweight rating and raised his price forecast to $135 from $125.
Piper Sandler analyst Peter Keith maintained an Overweight rating and increased his price forecast to $138 from $128.
TD Cowen analyst Max Rakhlenko maintained a Buy rating and raised his price forecast to $147 from $125.
Truist Securities analyst Scot Ciccarelli maintained a Buy rating and increased his price forecast to $134 from $114.
BTIG analyst Robert Drbul reiterated a Buy rating and maintained his $140 price forecast.
BTIG Analyst View
Drbul believes Walmart’s underlying U.S. business remains healthy, although Health & Wellness (H&W) is expected to weigh on reported comparable sales.
Walmart’s 2.9% U.S. comparable sales growth included an approximately 125-basis-point drag from Maximum Fair Price-related pharmacy deflation and brand-to-generic transfers, partly offset by a roughly 60-basis-point contribution from GLP-1 drugs.
Excluding H&W, comparable sales increased 3.6%, slightly accelerating from the second quarter of fiscal 2027 and improving on a two-year basis.
Looking ahead, the analyst expects healthy underlying demand but anticipates continued pressure on reported comparable sales from H&W.
MFP-related headwinds are expected to remain near current levels or increase slightly, while the contribution from GLP-1 drugs is likely to moderate.
However, improving H&W gross profit margins should help cushion the impact of weaker reported sales, according to the analyst.
Earnings Estimates And Outlook
Drbul maintained his fiscal 2027 EPS estimate at $2.90 but lowered his fourth-quarter Walmart U.S. comparable sales growth forecast to 2.9% from 3.1%. He expects comparable sales to increase 3.6% excluding H&W.
The analyst expects fiscal 2027 net sales of $748 billion, representing approximately 6% year-over-year growth, with operating income projected to grow faster than sales.
For fiscal 2028, Drbul raised his EPS estimate to $3.25 from $3.15.
WMT Price Action: Walmart shares were up 2.82% at $129.60 at the time of publication on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) shares are recovering on Friday after declining on Thursday following its third-quarter results.

It reported an adjusted EPS of 65 cents, exceeding analyst expectations of 64 cents. The figure excludes an after-tax loss of 3 cents per share related to equity and other investments.

Revenue rose 5.2% year over year to $188.835 billion, topping the consensus estimate of $187.271 billion.

However, Walmart’s weight-loss drug windfall is losing momentum despite rising prescription volumes.

Analyst Price Forecast Revisions

Several analysts raised their price forecasts following Walmart’s third-quarter results and increased guidance, while maintaining their existing ratings.

  • Morgan Stanley analyst Simeon Gutman maintained an Overweight rating and raised his price forecast to $135 from $125.
  • Piper Sandler analyst Peter Keith maintained an Overweight rating and increased his price forecast to $138 from $128.
  • TD Cowen analyst Max Rakhlenko maintained a Buy rating and raised his price forecast to $147 from $125.
  • Truist Securities analyst Scot Ciccarelli maintained a Buy rating and increased his price forecast to $134 from $114.
  • BTIG analyst Robert Drbul reiterated a Buy rating and maintained his $140 price forecast.

BTIG Analyst View

Drbul believes Walmart’s underlying U.S. business remains healthy, although Health & Wellness (H&W) is expected to weigh on reported comparable sales.

Walmart’s 2.9% U.S. comparable sales growth included an approximately 125-basis-point drag from Maximum Fair Price-related pharmacy deflation and brand-to-generic transfers, partly offset by a roughly 60-basis-point contribution from GLP-1 drugs.

Excluding H&W, comparable sales increased 3.6%, slightly accelerating from the second quarter of fiscal 2027 and improving on a two-year basis.

Looking ahead, the analyst expects healthy underlying demand but anticipates continued pressure on reported comparable sales from H&W.

MFP-related headwinds are expected to remain near current levels or increase slightly, while the contribution from GLP-1 drugs is likely to moderate.

However, improving H&W gross profit margins should help cushion the impact of weaker reported sales, according to the analyst.

Earnings Estimates And Outlook

Drbul maintained his fiscal 2027 EPS estimate at $2.90 but lowered his fourth-quarter Walmart U.S. comparable sales growth forecast to 2.9% from 3.1%. He expects comparable sales to increase 3.6% excluding H&W.

The analyst expects fiscal 2027 net sales of $748 billion, representing approximately 6% year-over-year growth, with operating income projected to grow faster than sales.

For fiscal 2028, Drbul raised his EPS estimate to $3.25 from $3.15.

WMT Price Action: Walmart shares were up 2.82% at $129.60 at the time of publication on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

The post Coinbase Eyes In-House US Prediction Markets by Mid-2027 After CFTC Clearinghouse Approval appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
Coinbase is preparing to launch its own prediction markets directly in the United States by the first half of 2027.

The company currently offers these event contracts through a partnership with Kalshi but says it plans to bring the offering in-house to gain greater control over product listings and capture more trading revenue.

The company noted it will continue using partners for certain products such as margined derivatives and upcoming single stock perps.

The target timeline for the in-house launch is the first half of 2027.

title: Why Is Bitmine Immersion Stock Falling on Friday?
description:
Bitmine Immersion Technologies Inc. (NYSE:BMNR) stock is trading lower on Friday as cryptocurrency-linked equities decline alongside falling digital asset prices and a broader technology sector selloff.
Crypto Market Pullback
Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) fell 3.55% over the past 24 hours to $59,712 on Friday, marking its lowest level since July. 
Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH), the primary digital asset held in Bitmine Immersion’s treasury, dropped 6.49% over the same period to $1,639.
On Friday, the Nasdaq is down 3.47%, while the S&P 500 has declined 1.80%, with Technology leading sector losses, falling 5.08% to rank as the worst-performing sector.
Rate Expectations
The broader market is also retreating as investors move out of higher-risk assets amid rising expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate increases. 
According to the CME FedWatch tool on Friday, markets price a 95.5% probability that the Federal Reserve will raise its target rate to the 400 to 425 basis points range, up from 88.5% one week earlier. 
Wall Street’s Exposure to Crypto
Speaking on a recent CNBC Events panel, Bitmine Immersion Technologies Chairman Tom Lee said institutional investors still hold zero median exposure to Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana (CRYPTO: SOL). 
Lee noted that Ethereum serves as a security layer for tokenized assets trading continuously, benefiting from what he called its “100% uptime.”
Technical Analysis
From a trend perspective, BMNR is still in a clear downtrend relative to its major moving averages, trading 25.8% below its 20-day SMA ($18.73) and 38.1% below its 50-day SMA ($22.46). 
It’s also 31.5% below the 200-day SMA ($20.29), which tells you rallies have been getting sold well before the stock can reclaim longer-term trend support.
Momentum is the bigger story right now: RSI is 25.73, which is firmly oversold and signals the selling has become stretched versus recent history.
The moving-average structure is mixed on the longer lens: the 20-day SMA is below the 50-day SMA (bearish), even though a golden cross occurred in September (50-day SMA above the 200-day SMA). 
The later death cross in January adds to the message that the intermediate trend deteriorated after that earlier bullish phase, lining up with the recent swing low in November and the 52-week low set in June.
Key Resistance: $16 — a nearby round-number area where rebounds can stall before the stock gets anywhere close to the 20-day/50-day averages
Key Support: $13 — a nearby floor near the lower end of the 52-week range ($12.80 low), where buyers may try to defend again
BMNR Price Action: BitMine Immersion shares were down 8.83% at $13.74 at the time of publication on Friday. The stock is near its 52-week low of $12.80, according to Benzinga Pro data.

title: Bitcoin Falls to $59,000: Was the 30% Rally a 'Bull Trap?'
description:
Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) could face another sharp selloff if it decisively breaks below $60,000, as macro analysts warn that deteriorating growth expectations and rising deflation risks threaten the recovery.
Speaking on the Milk Road Crypto podcast, Market Radar analysts Arty and Gamma described Bitcoin’s recent 30% rally as a “nasty bull trap” that caught investors betting on a sustained recovery.
The firm’s systematic macro model has remained risk-off since July 14, despite Bitcoin briefly returning to a bullish technical trend.
The analysts highlighted two conditions required before turning bullish on Bitcoin:
Risk-on macro environment: Improving growth and inflation expectations that support risk assets.
Bullish price trend: Bitcoin must confirm a sustained technical recovery.
As neither condition is currently satisfied, Market Radar believes Bitcoin needs stronger consumer spending and excess liquidity to sustain another bull market.
Unlike the AI-driven equity rally, which benefited from massive corporate capital expenditure, BTC depends more heavily on broader consumer liquidity.
Could Bitcoin Crash Below $59,000?
Market Radar identified $58,000-$59,000 as critical support, warning that a breakdown could trigger aggressive selling and invalidate expectations of a market bottom.
Its model signals:
91% probability that stagflation ends soon.
Over 50% probability of deflation emerging next.
Continued Bitcoin downside risk as growth weakens.
These conditional forecasts are not guarantees. Analysts warned that deflation could make Bitcoin’s support levels harder to defend.

title: Senate Approves Bill Banning Prediction Market Bets on War, Terrorism and Death
description:
The U.S. Senate passed the DEATH BETS Act to prohibit prediction markets from listing contracts on terrorism, assassination, war, military operations, or individual deaths.
The post Senate Approves Bill Banning Prediction Market Bets on War, Terrorism and Death appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
The U.S. Senate has approved legislation barring prediction markets from offering contracts tied to some of the most sensitive events.

The measure known as the Discouraging Exploitative Assassination, Tragedy, and Harm Betting in Event Trading Systems Act or DEATH BETS Act amends the Commodity Exchange Act to stop registered entities from listing or clearing such contracts.

It specifically prohibits agreements referencing terrorism, assassination, war, U.S. Armed Forces military operations, or similar activities.

The bill also bans contracts expected to resolve principally based on an individual’s death.

Senator Adam Schiff is highlighting the passage alongside Senator John Curtis.

“BREAKING: The Senate just passed my bill with @SenJohnCurtis to prohibit prediction markets from listing contracts involving terrorism, assassination, war, military operations, or an individual’s death. With this bill, Congress is making it clear that these bets should be illegal.”

The legislation includes a rule of construction preserving other permitted activities under existing law.

It was introduced on March 10, 2026, and passed the Senate with an amendment by voice vote on November 19, 2026.

The action targets event contracts on prediction platforms while leaving other trading unaffected.

A Technical Guide to Mitigate Java4Shell with TruRisk Eliminate
description: Executive Summary Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a heap out-of-bounds write in HotSpot’s AVX-512 Base64 decoder on x86-64. Calif reported it and showed pre-auth RCE in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins, and PingFederate. Nobody has reported exploitation in the wild as of November 17, 2026. CISA issued an alert that same day, urging everyone to patch now. […]
fullContent:
Executive Summary

Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a heap out-of-bounds write in HotSpot’s AVX-512 Base64 decoder on x86-64. Calif reported it and showed pre-auth RCE in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins, and PingFederate. Nobody has reported exploitation in the wild as of November 17, 2026. CISA issued an alert that same day, urging everyone to patch now.

Your Java4Shell Response Plan 

  • Patch to Oracle 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, or 27.0.1.1, or to your vendor’s build with JDK-8393212. 
  • If you can’t patch today, start the JVM with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics and restart it. 
  • You’re only exposed on an x86-64 CPU with AVX-512 VBMI. ARM64 isn’t affected. 

Tip for Qualys customers: you can apply the step 2 flag with TruRisk Eliminate, targeting only the hosts that need it and rolling it back in one click. 

Affected Java Builds and Their Fixed Releases

Oracle shipped the fixed builds on November 17, 2026. October’s builds are still vulnerable. 

Distro packages built before the fix are vulnerable even when the version looks current. Ubuntu’s 17.0.21.0.3 and Oracle Linux’s 17.0.21 are two examples. 

How the Java4Shell Attack Chain Works

This is a typical Java4Shell attack chain:

  1. The attacker needs a Base64 decode value they can control. Vulnerability discoverers were able to reach this pre-authentication condition via authentication in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, and after login in Kafka, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit and Spinnaker. A Java client that opens a TLS connection to a malicious server is exposed too. 
  2. The attacker then sends valid decodes until the server compiler compiles the fast path, then the bad input: 64 valid characters and one =, or 128 and one = on older 17 builds. 
  3. The target must pass the gates in the source. The JVM must see avx512_vbmi and avx512bw with UseAVX=3, the intrinsic must be on, and on 17u the input must be longer than 128 characters. 
  4. The stub’s tail handling goes wrong. The next section walks through it. 
  5. On a fixed build, or with the intrinsic off, nothing happens. Otherwise, 62 or 63 bytes land past the destination array on the Java heap. 
  6. Vulnerability researchers mentioned that they groomed the heap (G1 regions, thread-local allocation buffers) to turn that write into code execution. Unsuccessful exploitation will lead to a denial-of-service condition on the endpoint. 

This remote code execution chain has only been mentioned as achieved by the vulnerability researchers. Nobody has reported it in the wild yet. 

Tracing Java4Shell to Its Root Cause

Based on the jdk17u source at the fix commit, HotSpot generates the stub in generate_base64_decodeBlock (it shows up as implDecode at runtime), and C2 calls it from java.util.Base64$Decoder.decode0 once that method is hot. JDK-8268276 added the AVX-512 decoder in JDK 18 and JDK-8296735 backported it to 17.0.6, so 17.0.5 and older are clean. 

The whole vector decoder sits inside if (VM_Version::supports_avx512_vbmi() && VM_Version::supports_avx512bw()). Without both features HotSpot only builds the scalar 4-character loop, which is fine. 17u has no AVX2 decoder; the AVX2 tables in that file are for encoding. MIME input goes straight to the scalar loop. Basic and URL input take the vector path once it’s longer than 128 characters. 

The vector code decodes 64 characters a pass, and L_finalBit handles the last 1 to 63. Before the fix, a tail of 1 to 3 characters ending in = gave an output size of 0, and the padding step subtracted 1 from it. The output mask then came from bzhiq with an index of -1. bzhiq only reads the low 8 bits of the index, so -1 became 255, nothing got cleared and the mask stayed all ones. The final masked store wrote a full 64 bytes where it should have written none.  

The exact trigger condition on 17u follows from the control flow. The input must be longer than 128 characters and go through the basic or URL decoder, since MIME goes to the scalar loop. Inputs of 256 characters or more run through 256-character passes, then everything runs through 64-character passes, so the tail left at L_finalBit is the length modulo 64. Every character in those passes must be valid Base64; a = or any other bad character inside a pass makes the stub exit early and hand the rest to Java. The tail must be 1 to 3 characters ending in =, and any non-padding character in it must also be valid. Put together, the bad lengths are 64k + 1 to 64k + 3 for k of 2 or more: 129 to 131, 193 to 195, 257 to 259 and so on. Legitimate padded Base64 always has a length that’s a multiple of 4, so none of these inputs is valid anyway. Unpadded values such as JWT segments can have other lengths, but they never end in =. That makes length modulo 64 plus a trailing = a tighter hunting signal than “not a multiple of 4”. 

The fix, JDK-8393212, adds four lines at L_finalBit: if fewer than 4 characters remain, jump to L_bruteForce, the scalar path. The commit title is “Base64 optimization improvements”, which tells you nothing. 

The fix closes the underflow and causes no other change. The new check runs before the stub computes either the input mask or the output size. With 4 or more characters left, the output size starts at (length / 4) × 3, which is at least 3. Padding takes off at most 2, so the size stays at 1 or more and bzhiq always gets a valid index. A tail made only of = fails the validity check and drops to the scalar loop. Tails of 1 to 3 characters never reach the vector code at all. I checked memory safety only. I didn’t check whether the stub decodes every odd-length tail of 4 to 63 characters correctly, and the fix doesn’t touch that logic. 

No CWE is assigned yet. I’d file it as an integer underflow (CWE-191) that causes an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). Windows x64 gets the same vector code; the function only differs in how it reads its arguments there. I’ve only read the 17u source. Calif’s shorter trigger on newer lines suggests a lower threshold than 128 characters there, but I haven’t confirmed it. 

Confirm Exposure From Inside the Java Runtime 

A JVM is exposed only when all four of these conditions are true: 

  1. It runs on an x86-64 CPU with avx512f, avx512bw, avx512vbmi and bmi2. That covers Intel Ice Lake, Sapphire, Emerald and Granite Rapids, and AMD Zen 4 and newer. Skylake-SP and Cascade Lake have AVX-512 but no VBMI. 
  2. It’s OpenJDK 17.0.6 or later, or 18 to 27, below the fixed builds. Oracle’s 8u511 Enterprise Performance Pack counts too, because it ships a 17-based VM. 
  3. UseAVX=3 and UseBASE64Intrinsics=true, which are the defaults on those CPUs. 
  4. Attacker input reaches the basic or URL decoder in java.util.Base64. Basic auth and JWT parsing do this before login. 

A quiet service isn’t safe. The attacker warms up C2 with valid decodes first. 

The OS doesn’t change the bug. Windows x64 gets the same generated code as Linux, though only Linux has public testing. 

I wouldn’t rely on /proc/cpuinfo. It doesn’t exist outside Linux, and an empty result looks like “not affected”. Ask the JVM what it sees instead, on any OS: 
java -Xlog:os+cpu -version 2>&1 | grep -oE ‘avx512f|avx512bw|avx512_vbmi|bmi2’ | sort -u 
java -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal -version 2>/dev/null | grep -E ‘ (UseAVX|UseBASE64Intrinsics) ‘ 

All four flags, UseAVX = 3 and UseBASE64Intrinsics = true mean that runtime is exposed. Run the check with each java binary on the host, since each runtime reports its own settings. 

Turn the intrinsic off with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics and restart the JVM. With that flag HotSpot never generates the stub, which I confirmed in the source and on a live JVM. Oracle hasn’t published it as a workaround. 

Skip -XX:DisableIntrinsic=_base64_decodeBlock. Upwind reports it fails unless you also pass -XX:+UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions. 

CISA’s alert also suggests validating Base64 at the application boundary, enforcing input-size limits and limiting unauthenticated access. Boundary validation helps if it rejects padded input whose length isn’t a multiple of 4 before the decoder runs. Size limits won’t: the trigger is 65 characters on newer lines, shorter than most Basic-auth and JWT values. Limiting unauthenticated access works, but it means network ACLs or a VPN in front, because the vulnerable decode happens before login.  

Mitigate Java4Shell with TruRisk Eliminate 

For Qualys customers, the Java4Shell mitigation is available now with TruRisk Eliminate on Linux and Windows hosts, linked to QIDs such as 389494. As additional QIDs are released for different operating systems, we will test them and add support. The Cloud Agent runs it on the hosts you pick. Before it changes anything, it checks that the host has an AVX-512 VBMI CPU and an affected Java runtime, so hosts that can’t hit the bug are left alone. On the hosts that can, it adds -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics to JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS and keeps whatever value was already there. 

The setting takes effect when each JVM restarts, so plan restarts with the application owners. Windows services pick it up after a host reboot. After the change, the agent reports every running Java process with its effective setting, worked out in the order HotSpot applies options. A JVM it can’t read shows up as unknown, so you know where to look instead of assuming it’s covered. 

Rollback is one click in the console and restores the previous value. The mitigation doesn’t reach containers; set the flag in the image or pod spec for those. Treat it as a bridge to the patched builds, since Oracle hasn’t published the flag as a workaround. 

Code execution is not the only outcome. A successful exploit chain can read Java heap memory before it runs any attacker code. That memory can hold private keys, tokens, and personal data. CISA also warns that crafted input can crash the JVM, so availability is at risk too. Java clients are exposed as well. The researchers report a client-side exploit in which a Java program is compromised simply by connecting over TLS to a malicious server.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

What is Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938)?
Java4Shell is a heap out-of-bounds write in the AVX-512 Base64 decoder of the HotSpot JVM on x86-64. A malformed Base64 value can make the decoder write 62 or 63 bytes past the end of an array on the Java heap. Researchers turned that into pre-authentication remote code execution in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate.

Which Java versions are affected by Java4Shell?
OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later, and versions 18 to 27, are affected below the fixed builds. Oracle’s 8u511 Enterprise Performance Pack is also affected because it uses a 17-based VM. Oracle released the fixed builds on November 17, 2026: 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, 27.0.1.1 and 8u513-perf. Vendor builds that include fix JDK-8393212 are also safe. Java 8 standard and Java 11 are not affected.

Is Java4Shell being exploited in the wild?
No exploitation in the wild had been reported as of November 17, 2026. Remote code execution has only been demonstrated by researchers. CISA issued an alert the same day urging organizations to patch now.

How do I know if my Java runtime is exposed to Java4Shell?
A Java runtime is exposed only when all four conditions are true. It runs on an x86-64 CPU with AVX-512 VBMI. It’s an affected version. UseAVX=3 and UseBASE64Intrinsics are on, which are the defaults on those CPUs. And attacker input reaches the Basic or URL Base64 decoder. Check by asking each Java binary what it sees, not by reading /proc/cpuinfo. ARM64 is not affected.

How can I close the Java4Shell vulnerability if I can’t patch yet?
You can mitigate it by starting the JVM with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics and restarting it. With this flag, HotSpot never generates the vulnerable code. Oracle hasn’t published it as an official workaround, so treat it as a bridge until you can patch.

How do I mitigate Java4Shell with TruRisk Eliminate?
Apply -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics with TruRisk Eliminate through the Qualys Cloud Agent. It automatically targets only Linux and Windows hosts that have an AVX-512 VBMI CPU and an affected Java runtime. It keeps existing JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS values, reports the effective setting for every running Java process and offers one-click rollback.

We’re thrilled to announce that BFI is available for trading on Kraken!

Funding and trading

BFI trading is live as of Nov. 20, 2026.

To add an asset to your Kraken account, navigate to Funding, select the asset you’re after, and hit ‘Deposit’. 

Make sure to deposit your tokens into networks supported by Kraken. Deposits made using other networks will be lost.

BFI is available on Kraken

Here’s some more information about this asset:

BitFi (BFI)

BitFi is An on-chain asset management platform bridging CeFi yields and DeFi returns for institutions & individuals. BFI is the native token of the BitFi ecosystem, designed to support governance, staking-based utility, incentives, liquidity pairing, and long-term protocol growth.

Please note:  

  • Trading via Kraken App and Instant Buy will be available once the liquidity conditions are met (when a sufficient number of buyers and sellers have entered the market for their orders to be efficiently matched).

Get started with Kraken

Will Kraken make more assets available?

Yes! But our policy is to never reveal any details until shortly before launch – including which assets we are considering. All of Kraken’s available tokens can be found here, and all future tokens will be announced on our Listings Roadmap and social media profiles. Our client engagement specialists cannot answer any questions about which assets we may be making available in the future.

title: Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal
Blockstream researchers published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a hash-based post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the community to review it for flaws.
This post Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal

Several researchers have published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a proposed post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the wider community to look for flaws in it. Researcher Mikhail Kudinov announced the first version Thursday in a thread on X, saying the paper reduces SHRINCS’ security to the properties of its underlying hash function.

The analysis, dated Nov. 18, estimates classical security of 121.4 to 122.7 bits for SHRINCS, though those figures rest on assumptions that include three unproven conjectures. Kudinov said the work is not finished. The team is still working on a new analysis of a property called SM-DSPR, whose bound has so far been conjectured, and on tightening a reprogramming step and improving a bound against quantum attackers.

How SHRINCS works

SHRINCS is a hash-based scheme, meaning its security rests on hash functions rather than the elliptic curve math behind today’s Bitcoin signatures. It places two designs under one key: a stateful part built on FXMSS with WOTS+C, and a stateless fallback built on SLH-DSA. Because both use the same hash function, Kudinov said, the proof has to cover both.

Signature size is the main cost. Under the draft proposal, stateful SHRINCS signatures run from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while the stateless fallback is 5,777 bytes. Schnorr signatures on Bitcoin today are 64 bytes, and ECDSA signatures typically come in around 71. Signatures take up scarce block space, so larger ones mean fewer transactions per block.

The risk of a stateful signature

The compact stateful path carries a danger. It relies on one-time keys, and if a wallet accidentally reuses one, an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal the funds. Wallet software therefore has to track the state of every key. The stateless path avoids the problem, but at a much larger size.

Jonas Nick, Blockstream’s director of research, told Isabel Foxen Duke, head of the MARA Foundation, on MARA Foundation TV that wallets must automatically fall back to the stateless path whenever a state counter could be compromised. “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” he said. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.”

Nick also warned that heavy use of the larger signatures would weigh on the network. “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin.”

Researchers ask for review

The authors are clear that the analysis needs scrutiny. Kudinov said it has not been sufficiently peer reviewed, and the project’s GitHub repository warns that the documents may contain errors and should not be the sole basis for deploying SHRINCS. “We tried to be careful, but a proof of this size can have mistakes,” he wrote, asking readers to open an issue if they find one.

The team also produced two results that are not specific to SHRINCS: a classical bound for a property called ITSR without reprogramming, and a quadratic quantum bound for undetectability. Kudinov said they also apply to SPHINCS+ and SLH-DSA, the hash-based schemes SHRINCS borrows from, and that they were published as separate papers.

The SHRINCS work lands as quantum risk climbs the agenda. A global securities regulators’ group this week warned that moving blockchains to quantum-resistant cryptography may be especially hard, and researchers recently built a post-quantum defense for the Lightning Network after Bitcoin’s first quantum-safe transaction was shown without a fork.

The draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal for SHRINCS is also open for comment. “We need all the possible feedback — engineers, cryptographers, protocol developers,” Kudinov, a post-quantum cryptography researcher at Blockstream, said of it. “There are a lot of things to check, test, complain about, or praise.”

This post Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: HTX Research Publishes Six-Month Outlook for Bitcoin and Crypto Markets
description: Apia, Samoa, November 20, 2026 – HTX Research, the dedicated research arm of HTX, has published a new report titled From a Price Rebound to a Recovery in Capital Flows: A Six-Month Outlook for Bitcoin and Crypto Markets. The report addresses a central question for the months ahead: after a significant amount of leverage has been liquidated, who has the capital to absorb the remaining selling pressure? Its base case is that selling pressure will ease and BTC will attempt to stabilize first, with the durability of any recovery depending on whether sustained inflows return. The report covers the current cycle position, macroeconomic and dollar liquidity constraints, ETF and digital asset treasury company flows, stablecoin market dynamics, on-chain cost ranges, derivatives and spot liquidity, and the divergence across crypto assets. It also sets out the key observation windows from late November 2026 through May 2027, along with conditional scenarios for the six-month period. title: Banks Are Adopting Stablecoins: Here Is Why Crypto-Native Dollars Still Win on User Freedom
description: As traditional giants rush into digital dollars, USDD’s Yvonne Chia explains why 24/7 access, self-custody, and transparent yield give decentralized stablecoins an edge banks can’t replicate. 20 November – Road Town, Totorla, British Virgin Islands – Decentralized stablecoin protocol USDD is accelerating its multichain utility across TRON, Ethereum, and BNB Chain—combining automated sUSDD yield via its Smart Allocator with GasFree zero-TRX transfers—as traditional financial giants race to build competing stablecoin rails.  In a recent industry interview with instant exchange partner ChangeNOW, USDD Head of Communications Yvonne Chia outlined why self-custody, 24/7 settlement, and transparent onchain reserves give decentralized digital dollars a structural advantage over bank-issued alternatives. 1. Permissionless Access vs. Gatekept Accounts For billions of people globally, opening and maintaining a traditional bank account still involves paperwork, minimum balance requirements, geographic restrictions, and approval delays. Even when banks integrate stablecoin rails behind the scenes, those services remain gated behind legacy compliance walls and intermediary control. Crypto-native stablecoins flip that model on its head. As Yvonne Chia highlighted during the interview: “Compare this to a stablecoin like USDD, where all you need is a phone, a working internet connection, you can immediately start a wallet and you have access to your funds right away.” With USDD, users can access and manage their digital dollars directly through their own wallets, without depending on traditional financial intermediaries.  This represents a fundamental shift in financial access: users are no longer limited to the services, operating hours, or account structures of a single institution. Instead, they have the freedom to hold, manage, and transfer their assets on their own terms. Self-custody also gives users greater autonomy over their financial decisions. They can choose which wallets to use, where to transfer their assets, and which supported decentralized applications to interact with, without needing to route every transaction through a centralized financial institution.  With USDD, users’ digital dollars can move with them across an open blockchain ecosystem, rather than remaining tied to a particular bank or service provider. 2. 24/7 Global Settlement vs. “Banking Hours” Legacy payment networks still operate on decades-old schedules: weekend cutoffs, bank holidays, and multi-day cross-border settlement delays accompanied by hefty wire fees. Blockchain networks never close. Whether it is a Sunday night or a public holiday, USDD moves globally without depending on traditional banking operating hours or settlement windows. “We are able to have transfers 24/7 and we’re not limited to any traditional banking hours. So I think that in some ways, stablecoins are not just becoming banks, but exceeding what traditional banks can offer to users.” To make everyday transfers even smoother than fintech apps, USDD introduced GasFree integration on TRON, allowing users on supported wallets to pay network fees directly in USDD without needing to hold TRX. This removes another practical barrier to stablecoin adoption: having to acquire and maintain a separate gas token just to transfer digital dollars. With GasFree, eligible users can pay approximately 0.5 USDD per transaction, compared with around 1.5 USDT for a standard USDT transfer under the referenced fee conditions. These improvements matter because the usefulness of a stablecoin is not determined by its peg alone. Low-cost transfers, straightforward wallet experiences, and around-the-clock availability are what make digital dollars practical for everyday payments and global value transfers. 3. Passing Yield Back to Users vs. Bank Spreads Perhaps the sharpest contrast between banks and decentralized stablecoins lies in how yield is distributed.  In traditional banking, institutions take customer deposits, deploy them into yield-generating markets, and retain a significant portion of the returns. Everyday depositors may receive relatively low interest rates, while higher-yielding products often come with eligibility requirements, minimum deposits, or fixed maturity periods. Stablecoins introduce another way to participate in digital-dollar opportunities. Rather than keeping capital entirely within a traditional deposit account, users can access onchain yield opportunities through decentralized protocols and transparent investment mechanisms. USDD was built to return that value directly to holders. Through USDD Earn, users can deposit USDD to receive sUSDD, earning automated, competitive yield powered by our Smart Allocator system, with no fixed lock-up periods restricting access to their capital. For users, the distinction is important: USDD Earn provides access to a productive stablecoin while maintaining flexibility, rather than requiring users to commit their capital to a conventional fixed-term product. 4. Onchain Verification vs. Institutional Trust Traditional banks ask customers to trust closed-door balance sheets and periodic regulatory filings—until a crisis proves otherwise.  USDD takes a different approach through its “Don’t trust, verify” ethos, emphasizing publicly accessible onchain information and independent verification. Onchain Transparency: Smart contract addresses, collateral reserves, and Smart Allocator deployments are publicly viewable, allowing users to examine relevant information directly on the blockchain. Structured Disclosures: Quarterly Treasury Reports provide additional information about reserve positions, financial performance, and operational developments. Independent Security Reviews: USDD undergoes third-party security audits to assess its smart contracts and identify potential vulnerabilities. Transparency does not eliminate financial or technical risks, but it changes how users can evaluate them. Instead of relying exclusively on an institution’s assurances, users have access to information that can be independently examined and verified. 5. Beyond a Single Network: An Open, Multichain Financial Ecosystem Financial freedom is not just about holding digital dollars. It is also about being able to use them wherever opportunities and applications exist. A stablecoin confined to a single network or limited use case cannot fully realize the potential of open blockchain finance. Following its January 2025 protocol upgrade, USDD expanded natively from TRON onto Ethereum and BNB Chain, extending its reach across multiple blockchain ecosystems. This multichain presence allows USDD to connect with different communities, liquidity environments, and decentralized applications. Its sUSDD product has also expanded into DeFi integrations, including Pendle and Morpho, giving users additional ways to access yield strategies across supported ecosystems. The bigger picture is an interconnected financial ecosystem in which users can move between holding, transferring, exchanging, and deploying their stablecoins according to their own needs. These are not isolated functions. Together, they make stablecoins more useful as everyday financial infrastructure. The Future: Interconnected, Open, and Multichain Banks will undoubtedly continue using stablecoin rails to modernize their back-end settlement. As traditional giants rush into digital dollars, USDD’s Yvonne Chia explains why 24/7 access, self-custody, and transparent yield give decentralized stablecoins an edge banks can’t replicate.

20 November – Road Town, Totorla, British Virgin Islands – Decentralized stablecoin protocol USDD is accelerating its multichain utility across TRON, Ethereum, and BNB Chain—combining automated sUSDD yield via its Smart Allocator with GasFree zero-TRX transfers—as traditional financial giants race to build competing stablecoin rails. 

In a recent industry interview with instant exchange partner ChangeNOW, USDD Head of Communications Yvonne Chia outlined why self-custody, 24/7 settlement, and transparent onchain reserves give decentralized digital dollars a structural advantage over bank-issued alternatives.

1. Permissionless Access vs. Gatekept Accounts

For billions of people globally, opening and maintaining a traditional bank account still involves paperwork, minimum balance requirements, geographic restrictions, and approval delays. Even when banks integrate stablecoin rails behind the scenes, those services remain gated behind legacy compliance walls and intermediary control.

Crypto-native stablecoins flip that model on its head. As Yvonne Chia highlighted during the interview:

“Compare this to a stablecoin like USDD, where all you need is a phone, a working internet connection, you can immediately start a wallet and you have access to your funds right away.”

With USDD, users can access and manage their digital dollars directly through their own wallets, without depending on traditional financial intermediaries. 

This represents a fundamental shift in financial access: users are no longer limited to the services, operating hours, or account structures of a single institution. Instead, they have the freedom to hold, manage, and transfer their assets on their own terms.

Self-custody also gives users greater autonomy over their financial decisions. They can choose which wallets to use, where to transfer their assets, and which supported decentralized applications to interact with, without needing to route every transaction through a centralized financial institution. 

With USDD, users’ digital dollars can move with them across an open blockchain ecosystem, rather than remaining tied to a particular bank or service provider.

2. 24/7 Global Settlement vs. “Banking Hours”

Legacy payment networks still operate on decades-old schedules: weekend cutoffs, bank holidays, and multi-day cross-border settlement delays accompanied by hefty wire fees.

Blockchain networks never close. Whether it is a Sunday night or a public holiday, USDD moves globally without depending on traditional banking operating hours or settlement windows.

“We are able to have transfers 24/7 and we’re not limited to any traditional banking hours. So I think that in some ways, stablecoins are not just becoming banks, but exceeding what traditional banks can offer to users.”

To make everyday transfers even smoother than fintech apps, USDD introduced GasFree integration on TRON, allowing users on supported wallets to pay network fees directly in USDD without needing to hold TRX.

This removes another practical barrier to stablecoin adoption: having to acquire and maintain a separate gas token just to transfer digital dollars. With GasFree, eligible users can pay approximately 0.5 USDD per transaction, compared with around 1.5 USDT for a standard USDT transfer under the referenced fee conditions.

These improvements matter because the usefulness of a stablecoin is not determined by its peg alone. Low-cost transfers, straightforward wallet experiences, and around-the-clock availability are what make digital dollars practical for everyday payments and global value transfers.

3. Passing Yield Back to Users vs. Bank Spreads

Perhaps the sharpest contrast between banks and decentralized stablecoins lies in how yield is distributed. 

In traditional banking, institutions take customer deposits, deploy them into yield-generating markets, and retain a significant portion of the returns. Everyday depositors may receive relatively low interest rates, while higher-yielding products often come with eligibility requirements, minimum deposits, or fixed maturity periods.

Stablecoins introduce another way to participate in digital-dollar opportunities. Rather than keeping capital entirely within a traditional deposit account, users can access onchain yield opportunities through decentralized protocols and transparent investment mechanisms.

USDD was built to return that value directly to holders. Through USDD Earn, users can deposit USDD to receive sUSDD, earning automated, competitive yield powered by our Smart Allocator system, with no fixed lock-up periods restricting access to their capital.

For users, the distinction is important: USDD Earn provides access to a productive stablecoin while maintaining flexibility, rather than requiring users to commit their capital to a conventional fixed-term product.

4. Onchain Verification vs. Institutional Trust

Traditional banks ask customers to trust closed-door balance sheets and periodic regulatory filings—until a crisis proves otherwise. 

USDD takes a different approach through its “Don’t trust, verify” ethos, emphasizing publicly accessible onchain information and independent verification.

  • Onchain Transparency: Smart contract addresses, collateral reserves, and Smart Allocator deployments are publicly viewable, allowing users to examine relevant information directly on the blockchain.
  • Structured Disclosures: Quarterly Treasury Reports provide additional information about reserve positions, financial performance, and operational developments.
  • Independent Security Reviews: USDD undergoes third-party security audits to assess its smart contracts and identify potential vulnerabilities.

Transparency does not eliminate financial or technical risks, but it changes how users can evaluate them. Instead of relying exclusively on an institution’s assurances, users have access to information that can be independently examined and verified.

5. Beyond a Single Network: An Open, Multichain Financial Ecosystem Financial freedom is not just about holding digital dollars. It is also about being able to use them wherever opportunities and applications exist. A stablecoin confined to a single network or limited use case cannot fully realize the potential of open blockchain finance. Following its January 2025 protocol upgrade, USDD expanded natively from TRON onto Ethereum and BNB Chain, extending its reach across multiple blockchain ecosystems. This multichain presence allows USDD to connect with different communities, liquidity environments, and decentralized applications. Its sUSDD product has also expanded into DeFi integrations, including Pendle and Morpho, giving users additional ways to access yield strategies across supported ecosystems.

The bigger picture is an interconnected financial ecosystem in which users can move between holding, transferring, exchanging, and deploying their stablecoins according to their own needs. These are not isolated functions. Together, they make stablecoins more useful as everyday financial infrastructure.

The Future: Interconnected, Open, and Multichain

Banks will undoubtedly continue using stablecoin rails to modernize their back-end settlement. However, true financial freedom comes from open networks where assets flow freely across protocols without intermediaries.

For USDD, the opportunity goes beyond offering a dollar-pegged asset. It is about making digital dollars accessible, transferable, and productive across an interconnected financial ecosystem. From self-custody and 24/7 transfers to flexible yield opportunities and multichain DeFi access, these capabilities give users more ways to put their money to work.

Banks may be bringing stablecoins into traditional finance. Crypto-native protocols are showing what stablecoins can make possible beyond it.

title: U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged the Fed not to embrace a bigger rate hike as Citi and traders still see a quarter-point move in December and bitcoin fell below $60,000.
This post U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Friday on calls for a bigger Federal Reserve rate hike, even as bitcoin broke below $60,000 for the first time since July and stocks sank on bets that the Fed will keep tightening into a selloff.

Bessent told CNBC he would encourage the Fed not to embrace a half-point increase at its Dec. 8-9 meeting. He cited the energy supply shock and a drop in crude prices as reasons for the central bank to hold back.

Bessent says the Fed should look forward

He argued that one governor now backing a 50 basis point hike had wanted a similar cut within the last year. Bessent said it “seems somewhat peripatetic” to want the bigger increase only 11 or 12 months later. He did not name the governor.

“I would encourage the Fed to look forward, not backwards,” Bessent said.

The comments came two days after Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC a half-point hike is probably necessary in December and that the central bank may need to “shock people.” Waller said inflation is “headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out.”

Fed officials split on how far to go

Waller is not alone. Minutes of the October meeting showed nearly all officials expect a quarter-point hike in December, and two floated a larger one. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee also declined to rule out a bigger move on Thursday.

“We’ve now had multiple months in a row of borderline disturbingly high inflation rates with little progress in the sectors where we would expect to be seeing some progress,” Goolsbee told reporters. “So everything’s always on the table.”

Not everyone wants to go bigger. New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that “I don’t think the situation calls for dramatic action.” St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem has suggested as many as four hikes by the spring of 2027.

The Fed raised rates in September for the first time in more than three years and held them steady in October. Inflation has stayed hot since the Iran strikes pushed up energy prices earlier this year.

Citi and traders still see a quarter-point hike

Citi still expects a quarter-point increase in December. Global chief economist Nathan Sheets said Thursday he does not see a need for 50 basis points despite persistent inflation. In a note Friday, the bank wrote that “Fed officials will consequently have little appetite to hike into an equity sell-off.”

Citi expects the Fed to hold after December and begin cutting later in 2027. Traders agree on the next step: the CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed a more than 98% chance of a quarter-point hike, and the 10-year Treasury yield fell more than 10 basis points to 4.95% as investors bought bonds.

Stocks fell for another day. The Nasdaq Composite dropped more than 2% in morning trading, and the VIX volatility index topped 30, its highest level since March.

What it means for bitcoin

Bitcoin traded near $59,700 shortly before 11 a.m. ET, down more than 5% on the day, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro. It broke below $60,000 for the first time since early July and is on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, the longest streak since 2022.

Higher rates are a headwind for assets that pay no yield, and the selloff has reached companies that hold bitcoin. Strategy’s stock fell for a sixth straight session on Thursday, and the bitcoin price has dropped roughly 25% in a month, a slide Bitcoin Magazine tracked earlier this week.

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill tied the outlook to inflation in a note dated Nov. 18. “Our base case remains range trading around USD 60k to 90k through much of 2027, until falling inflation gives monetary policy room to ease,” he said.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $59,300.

This post U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 for the first time since early July on Friday as a tech stock rout, rate hike bets and record ETF outflows hit risk assets.
This post Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens

The bitcoin price crashed below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since early July, falling about $1,800 in roughly an hour as a deepening U.S. tech stock selloff dragged risk assets lower.

Bitcoin traded near $61,400 at 9:40 a.m. ET and slid to about $59,600 by 10:45 a.m., a drop of nearly 3%, according to Look Into Bitcoin data. The bitcoin price is down about $3,400, or more than 5%, from the same time Thursday, when it traded near $63,000.

The break of $60,000 is a key psychological level, and it came with little warning. Bitcoin price had held above $61,000 for most of the morning, even after a third straight daily loss.

Stocks and rate hike bets drive the selloff

Wall Street opened sharply lower. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% in morning trading as shares of Anthropic extended losses in its second day since a record Nasdaq debut. Nvidia and AMD also traded lower.

Bitcoin has been moving with tech stocks. The market has questioned whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will pay off, and Friday’s open did nothing to ease that worry.

Rate expectations are adding pressure. Traders see a roughly 94% chance the Federal Reserve raises rates in December, CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed. Higher rates tend to hurt bitcoin and other assets that pay no yield.

Earlier Friday, South Korea’s Kospi index fell more than 5% and chipmakers sank across Asia. That selling carried into U.S. trading and then into bitcoin.

Some analysts had flagged $60,000 as a floor. Katie Stockton of Fairlead Strategies told CNBC the bottom of bitcoin’s trading range sits “just below 60,000,” and that it “appears to be trying to find a footing.” Friday’s drop tests that view.

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said this week the drop is a “continuation of the existing bear market.” His base case is range trading around $60,000 to $90,000 through much of 2027.

ETF outflows and liquidations

Funds have been sellers. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost $541.1 million on Thursday, its biggest one-day outflow on record. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total, extending a streak of heavy withdrawals this week.

Leveraged traders were hit as well. More than $700 million in crypto positions were liquidated in the 24 hours before the latest drop, and about 86% were bets on higher prices. The slide below $60,000 likely forced out more of them.

The move extends a month-long slump. Bitcoin has dropped roughly $20,000 in the past month, a slide tracked as the price fell under $62,000 on Thursday.

Crypto stocks fall harder than bitcoin price

Crypto stocks fell even faster. Strategy (MSTR) was down about 7% near $79.85, a day after it tumbled for a sixth straight session. Coinbase (COIN) fell about 3% to $105.36. Shares of Strive (ASST) fell to $15.31 Friday morning, down 21.47%, or $4.19, over the past five days. The stock has slid steadily from near $19.50 as bitcoin price’s sell-off deepened, with its sharpest drop in Friday’s trading.

Bitcoin miners took the worst of it. MARA Holdings (MARA) dropped about 11% to $5.55. Riot Platforms (RIOT) lost about 11% to $15.85, and CleanSpark (CLSK) fell about 12% to $5.13.

Data center operators that also mine bitcoin were hit hard. IREN fell about 12% to $12.62, and Cipher Digital (CIFR) dropped 14% to $5.58. Both have traded with AI stocks, which are also under pressure.

The bitcoin price is now at its lowest since the first days of July. Bitcoin set its record above $126,000 in October 2025, so it has lost more than half its value from that peak.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $59,600.

This post Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Why the Agent Era Needs a New Operating System | DHH
description:
David Heinemeier Hansson thinks the agent era is reopening a window in computing that has been closed for decades: the chance to build a new operating system people actually want to use.
DHH joins a16z General Partners Martin Casado and Anish Acharya to explain why he’s building Omarchy, an agent-first Linux distribution designed around a computer that users can modify simply by asking. They discuss why the command lines, config files, and detailed error messages that once made Linux intimidating now make it unusually well suited to agents, and why DHH believes software development has become cheap enough to challenge decades-old platform lock-in.
But if code is becoming abundant, what still matters? DHH argues that taste, craft, and the willingness to obsess over the final 2% become more important, not less. The conversation moves from tiny teams wielding the productive capacity of thousands of people to open models, competition at the frontier, and the return of hacker, demo, and pseudonymous internet culture.

title: Bitcoin Dips Under $60,000 as Crypto Market Sinks at US Open
description:
Update, 16:08 UTC: Bitcoin extended its slide below $60,000 and dipped to about $59,000, according to CoinMarketCap data. SUMMARY ▸Bitcoin […]
The post Bitcoin Dips Under $60,000 as Crypto Market Sinks at US Open appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Update, 16:08 UTC: Bitcoin extended its slide below $60,000 and dipped to about $59,000, according to CoinMarketCap data.

SUMMARY
▸Bitcoin lost 3% in a single hour
▸Ether fell harder, sliding under $1,700
▸BlackRock’s IBIT logged a record daily outflow
▸Overnight losses hit HYPE and Zcash first

The drop came as chip stocks extended their slide after the US open, adding to a selloff that had already taken bitcoin to nearly $61,200 overnight, CoinDesk reported.

The Hour That Did Most of the Damage

As of 15:24 UTC, CoinMarketCap data showed Bitcoin at $60,079 and Ethereum at $1,672. Less than an hour earlier, CoinDesk’s live coverage still had bitcoin near $61,700, down under 1% on the day. The gap between those two readings accounts for most of Friday’s decline in the two largest cryptocurrencies.

How much of the 24-hour loss came in the last hour

Last hour

Earlier in the day

ETH
70% of −6.53%
BTC
59% of −5.14%
XRP

27% of −16.11%
HYPE
25% of −10.10%
CoinMarketCap data, 15:24 UTC, November 20. Shares are approximate: the last-hour change divided by the 24-hour change.

No crypto-specific headline came with the final leg down. It matched the timing of the stock market. Nvidia fell another 5% after the open to $139, leaving it about 42% below its October peak, according to CoinDesk. Anthropic, which priced its IPO at $83 and closed its first trading day at $97, had already slid about 13% to $88 in premarket trading. With the tech trade unwinding, bitcoin traded alongside chip stocks, not as a hedge against them.

Two Selloffs, Not One

The split bars show that Friday’s decline came in two separate waves. The overnight wave hit trading tokens hardest. By 10:25 a.m. ET, the CoinDesk 20 index was down 1.9% with none of its 20 members higher. Zcash had fallen 11%, NEAR 9.3%, Hyperliquid’s HYPE 7%, and Lighter and Derive 11% and 10%, according to the same CoinDesk coverage, which identified tokens tied to decentralized exchanges and derivatives platforms as among the hardest hit. Most of HYPE’s and Zcash’s daily losses were already in place before the US open.

The same morning, CoinDesk reported that the CFTC had said Hyperliquid and other onchain venues would get no special exemptions. Nothing in the reporting links that statement to the drop in derivatives tokens, but it landed on a day when that sector was already under the most pressure.

The second wave, after the open, hit the large caps. Ether lost the biggest share of its day in that hour, which is what took it below $1,700.

The Buyer That Stepped Back

Earlier dips this year met steady buying from spot ETFs. That support is now going the other way. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust recorded $541.1 million in net outflows on Thursday, its largest single-day withdrawal since launch, according to Farside Investors data cited by CoinDesk. Across all US spot bitcoin ETFs, Thursday’s net outflows topped $580 million, taking November’s total to about $3.47 billion, according to SoSoValue figures in CoinDesk’s Friday market briefing.

That briefing also noted that an argument popular earlier in the week has not played out: that money would rotate back into bitcoin once Anthropic’s record IPO was done. Instead, bitcoin is down about 28% for the quarter.

A Broad Retreat From Risk

Crypto wasn’t the only market falling. Nasdaq futures dropped more than 1% before Friday’s open as Anthropic shares retreated and hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials weighed on sentiment, Reuters reported. On Wednesday, Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC that a half-point rate hike is probably necessary at the December 8–9 meeting, saying “you might need to, like, shock people.” Waller and Governor Lisa Cook were both scheduled to speak on Friday.

Gold, often compared with bitcoin as a store of value, fell nearly 3% to about $3,514, its lowest since early September. Treasury yields fell as money moved into government bonds instead. Implied volatility rose across asset classes: the VIX reached 29.5, its highest since March, and Volmex’s bitcoin volatility index climbed to 52.2, according to CoinDesk. Reuters, cited in the same briefing, reported that Asian shares were heading for their worst week since 2020.

Who Held Up Over the Week

On a weekly view, the order looks different from Friday’s. TRON lost a small fraction of what the rest of the top ten did. XRP, despite a steeper Friday than bitcoin, is still down less than bitcoin over seven days. Speculative assets took the heaviest weekly losses: Dogecoin, Zcash, Monero and HYPE.

What Traders Are Watching Into the Weekend

The near-term schedule is short. Friday’s remarks from Waller and Cook are the last Fed comments before the weekend, and the December 8-9 meeting is now the main reference point for rate expectations. CoinDesk’s briefing noted that weekend trading may leave crypto to absorb market stress on its own, with stock markets closed and spot ETFs not trading until Monday. Sunday’s weekly close will be the first full candle to include this week’s ETF exits and Friday’s post-open drop.
